input.content:
# Phase 2.0 — Deterministic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no changes to `terminal/`.

## Verified facts this plan rests on

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` is ever called | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` silently drops the whole rprompt block | measured: 419 → 328 bytes on `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` |
| Adding `Format` to the pinned data restores it exactly | measured: 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state | scan of receiver-field assignments |
| At least 24 of those perform direct I/O (`RunCommand`, `HasFiles`, `HTTPRequest`, …) | scan; more do so transitively |
| `website/segment_data.json` pins 24 of 117 segments; the rest run live | `src/config/segment.go:487-507` (`DataKey`) |
| With that hand-written file, 46 of 122 themes render non-deterministically | two full sweeps, diffed |
| With per-theme `config export data` recordings, 122 of 122 are deterministic | two full sweeps, diffed |
| The recorder captures post-`Enabled()` state, including `Format` | `tokyo.json` and friends contain every derived field |
| Recorded fixtures are ~580 KB; goldens ~237 KB | `du` over 122 files each |
| **Every recorded fixture contains the recording machine's real username** | 122/122 contain `jande` |
| **No theme PNG is tracked in git** — they are generated in CI only | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` returns 0 |
| ns/op varies ~8x run to run on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` baseline |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B / 14 allocs;
`BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions already taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 on its own, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **Hermetic by default, derive by opt-in.** Replay never calls `Enabled()` unless explicitly
  asked. This is what keeps the golden harness deterministic and keeps a future render endpoint
  free of live segment execution — the `http`, `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist` and `wakatime`
  segments all take a URL or key from config, so any path that runs them server-side is an SSRF
  proxy.

## Deliberately out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, and the
missing `Plain` guard on OSC 8 hyperlink emission (it changes ANSI output, so it must land
after the harness exists, not with it).

---

## Task A — the replay contract

**Owns:** `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`, `src/cli/data.go`,
`src/cli/config_export_data.go`, and their tests.

Three changes, in this order.

### A1. Mark recorded files

The recorder writes a provenance marker into the file it produces. A top-level field on the
`Data` struct — a schema version is better than a bare boolean because it gives the next change
somewhere to go:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { … } }
```

Absent field means "hand-written", which is the current state of every existing file.

### A2. Fail loudly on unmarked data

On load, a file without the marker is a hard error naming the two ways forward:

> `<path>` was not produced by `oh-my-posh config export data`. Hand-written data files skip
> the segment's `Enabled()` step, so any field it derives will be missing and the segment can
> render empty. Record the file with `oh-my-posh config export data --config <config>
> --output <path>`, or pass `--data-derive` to compute derived state at render time.

The error must say *why*, not just *what*. The failure this replaces is silent and looks like
a theme bug.

### A3. `--data-derive`

An opt-in flag on the commands that accept `--data` (`print`, `config export image`). When set,
`restoreData` calls `segment.writer.Enabled()` first and unmarshals the pinned data **over** the
result, so derived fields are computed and pinned fields still win.

Order matters and is the whole point: `Enabled()` then overlay. The reverse recomputes over the
pinned values and discards them.

Document on the flag, in one line, that this re-runs live segment probes and is therefore
neither hermetic nor deterministic — it exists so a hand-written file stays usable locally.

**Verification:** `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` with a data file containing only
`{"time":{"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"}}` renders the time segment under
`--data-derive` and errors without it. Confirm the recorded-fixture path never calls `Enabled()`
— assert it, do not assume it, because that assertion is what the SSRF argument rests on.

---

## Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness

**Owns:** a fixture-generation command or script, `src/prompt/golden_test.go` (or wherever
Task B judges correct after reading the existing test layout), and the committed fixtures.

### B1. Sanitize on record

**Recorded data cannot be committed as-is.** All 122 fixtures I generated contain my real
username, and the `env` block carries `UserName`, `HostName`, `PWD`, `AbsolutePWD`, `PSWD` and
`Folder`. Segment data embeds real paths too — `tokyo.json` contains a rendered template string
with the username in it, so scrubbing the `env` block alone is not enough.

Sanitization must therefore be a string-level pass over the whole serialized file, replacing the
recording machine's identity with fixed synthetic values, then the `env` block overwritten with:

```
UserName  alice
HostName  contoso-devbox
PWD       ~/dev/oh-my-posh
```

matching the values `website/segment_data.json` already uses, so the fixtures and the website
tell the same story.

**A test must assert no fixture contains the current user's name, hostname, or home path.**
Without it this regresses the first time someone regenerates on their own machine, and it
regresses silently into a public repo.

### B2. The harness

For each of the 122 bundled themes: render `print primary` with the sanitized fixture and
compare byte-for-byte against a committed golden.

- Fixtures ~580 KB, goldens ~237 KB. Acceptable; do not compress, a readable diff is the point.
- Failure output must show the first differing byte offset and a decoded escape context window.
  A diff of two ANSI blobs is unreadable otherwise, and this harness exists to be read during
  a refactor.
- Regeneration must be one documented command, and the test must name it on failure.
- The golden is the *current* output. This phase changes no rendering. If generating goldens
  produces a diff against what the current binary emits, stop and report — that is a bug found,
  not a golden to bless.

Wire into the workflow that runs on Go pull requests. Note `.github/workflows/code.yml` carries
`paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, which is fine here since everything lands under `src/`.

---

## Task C — make the website's data file valid

**Owns:** `website/segment_data.json`, `website/export_themes.mjs`, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
if needed.

`website/segment_data.json` is hand-written and deliberately synthetic — it exists to make theme
screenshots look like a plausible machine, not to reflect any real one. Under A2 it now fails to
load.

Determine which of the two applies and implement it, reporting which and why:

1. **Preferred — make it a valid recorded file.** Record it, sanitize it to the same synthetic
   identity, and keep the curated values (`anycompany-prod`, `Contoso Production`, the pinned
   battery percentage) by overlaying them onto the recording. Keeps the website pipeline
   hermetic.
2. **Fallback — pass `--data-derive` from `export_themes.mjs`.** Honest and small, but the
   website images then depend on live segment probes on the CI runner. That is already true
   today for the 93 unpinned segments, so it is not a regression — but it is not an improvement
   either, and the theme images stay non-deterministic.

Do not silently pick the fallback because it is easier. If option 1 turns out to be
impractical, say what blocked it.

---

## Task D — reset `isHyperlink`

**Owns:** `src/terminal/writer.go` and its tests. Separate commit; unrelated to the rest.

`isHyperlink` is set at `writer.go:460`, `:503`, `:562` and cleared only by encountering
`<TEXT>`. It is not reset in `Write`'s prologue (`:385-392`) nor in `String()`'s deferred
cleanup (`:605-619`) — the only two reset points in the package. An unbalanced `<LINK>` with no
`</TEXT>` therefore leaves it `true` for the lifetime of the process, and every subsequent
`Write` takes the branch at `:700-703`: runes go straight into the builder with no length
counting and no shell escaping.

Reset it alongside the other per-render flags. Add a test that writes an unbalanced `<LINK>`
and asserts the next `Write` counts length correctly.

This must not change output for any balanced input — the golden harness from Task B is the
proof, so land it after B.

---

## Landing order

`A` → `B` → `C`, sequential: B's fixtures are invalid until A defines the marker, and C cannot
be validated until A2 is enforcing. `D` is independent but lands after B so the harness can
prove it inert.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` clean from `src/`.
2. All 122 goldens pass. Then deliberately corrupt one fixture and confirm the failure output
   names the theme and shows a readable escape context.
3. Re-run the full render sweep twice and diff — 122/122 identical, as measured today.
4. A data file lacking the marker fails with the explanatory error; the same file under
   `--data-derive` renders.
5. Assert the hermetic path does not call `Enabled()`. This is the SSRF-relevant claim.
6. Grep every committed fixture for the current user, host and home path — zero hits.
7. Benchmarks against the baseline above: allocs/op and B/op unchanged. Ignore ns/op, which
   swings 8x on this hardware.
8. `npm run themes` equivalent still produces images for a sample of themes.

# Phase 2.0 — Deterministic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no changes to `terminal/`.

## Verified facts this plan rests on

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` is ever called | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` silently drops the whole rprompt block | measured: 419 → 328 bytes on `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` |
| Adding `Format` to the pinned data restores it exactly | measured: 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state | scan of receiver-field assignments |
| At least 24 of those perform direct I/O (`RunCommand`, `HasFiles`, `HTTPRequest`, …) | scan; more do so transitively |
| `website/segment_data.json` pins 24 of 117 segments; the rest run live | `src/config/segment.go:487-507` (`DataKey`) |
| With that hand-written file, 46 of 122 themes render non-deterministically | two full sweeps, diffed |
| With per-theme `config export data` recordings, 122 of 122 are deterministic | two full sweeps, diffed |
| The recorder captures post-`Enabled()` state, including `Format` | `tokyo.json` and friends contain every derived field |
| Recorded fixtures are ~580 KB; goldens ~237 KB | `du` over 122 files each |
| **Every recorded fixture contains the recording machine's real username** | 122/122 contain `jande` |
| **No theme PNG is tracked in git** — they are generated in CI only | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` returns 0 |
| ns/op varies ~8x run to run on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` baseline |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B / 14 allocs;
`BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions already taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 on its own, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **Hermetic by default, derive by opt-in.** Replay never calls `Enabled()` unless explicitly
  asked. This is what keeps the golden harness deterministic and keeps a future render endpoint
  free of live segment execution — the `http`, `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist` and `wakatime`
  segments all take a URL or key from config, so any path that runs them server-side is an SSRF
  proxy.

## Deliberately out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, and the
missing `Plain` guard on OSC 8 hyperlink emission (it changes ANSI output, so it must land
after the harness exists, not with it).

---

## Task A — the replay contract

**Owns:** `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`, `src/cli/data.go`,
`src/cli/config_export_data.go`, and their tests.

Three changes, in this order.

### A1. Mark recorded files

The recorder writes a provenance marker into the file it produces. A top-level field on the
`Data` struct — a schema version is better than a bare boolean because it gives the next change
somewhere to go:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { … } }
```

Absent field means "hand-written", which is the current state of every existing file.

### A2. Fail loudly on unmarked data

On load, a file without the marker is a hard error naming the two ways forward:

> `<path>` was not produced by `oh-my-posh config export data`. Hand-written data files skip
> the segment's `Enabled()` step, so any field it derives will be missing and the segment can
> render empty. Record the file with `oh-my-posh config export data --config <config>
> --output <path>`, or pass `--data-derive` to compute derived state at render time.

The error must say *why*, not just *what*. The failure this replaces is silent and looks like
a theme bug.

### A3. `--data-derive`

An opt-in flag on the commands that accept `--data` (`print`, `config export image`). When set,
`restoreData` calls `segment.writer.Enabled()` first and unmarshals the pinned data **over** the
result, so derived fields are computed and pinned fields still win.

Order matters and is the whole point: `Enabled()` then overlay. The reverse recomputes over the
pinned values and discards them.

Document on the flag, in one line, that this re-runs live segment probes and is therefore
neither hermetic nor deterministic — it exists so a hand-written file stays usable locally.

**Verification:** `themes/agnosterplus.omp.json` with a data file containing only
`{"time":{"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"}}` renders the time segment under
`--data-derive` and errors without it. Confirm the recorded-fixture path never calls `Enabled()`
— assert it, do not assume it, because that assertion is what the SSRF argument rests on.

---

## Task B — sanitized fixtures and the golden harness

**Owns:** a fixture-generation command or script, `src/prompt/golden_test.go` (or wherever
Task B judges correct after reading the existing test layout), and the committed fixtures.

### B1. Sanitize on record

**Recorded data cannot be committed as-is.** All 122 fixtures I generated contain my real
username, and the `env` block carries `UserName`, `HostName`, `PWD`, `AbsolutePWD`, `PSWD` and
`Folder`. Segment data embeds real paths too — `tokyo.json` contains a rendered template string
with the username in it, so scrubbing the `env` block alone is not enough.

Sanitization must therefore be a string-level pass over the whole serialized file, replacing the
recording machine's identity with fixed synthetic values, then the `env` block overwritten with:

```
UserName  alice
HostName  contoso-devbox
PWD       ~/dev/oh-my-posh
```

matching the values `website/segment_data.json` already uses, so the fixtures and the website
tell the same story.

**A test must assert no fixture contains the current user's name, hostname, or home path.**
Without it this regresses the first time someone regenerates on their own machine, and it
regresses silently into a public repo.

### B2. The harness

For each of the 122 bundled themes: render `print primary` with the sanitized fixture and
compare byte-for-byte against a committed golden.

- Fixtures ~580 KB, goldens ~237 KB. Acceptable; do not compress, a readable diff is the point.
- Failure output must show the first differing byte offset and a decoded escape context window.
  A diff of two ANSI blobs is unreadable otherwise, and this harness exists to be read during
  a refactor.
- Regeneration must be one documented command, and the test must name it on failure.
- The golden is the *current* output. This phase changes no rendering. If generating goldens
  produces a diff against what the current binary emits, stop and report — that is a bug found,
  not a golden to bless.

Wire into the workflow that runs on Go pull requests. Note `.github/workflows/code.yml` carries
`paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, which is fine here since everything lands under `src/`.

---

## Task C — make the website's data file valid

**Owns:** `website/segment_data.json`, `website/export_themes.mjs`, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
if needed.

`website/segment_data.json` is hand-written and deliberately synthetic — it exists to make theme
screenshots look like a plausible machine, not to reflect any real one. Under A2 it now fails to
load.

Determine which of the two applies and implement it, reporting which and why:

1. **Preferred — make it a valid recorded file.** Record it, sanitize it to the same synthetic
   identity, and keep the curated values (`anycompany-prod`, `Contoso Production`, the pinned
   battery percentage) by overlaying them onto the recording. Keeps the website pipeline
   hermetic.
2. **Fallback — pass `--data-derive` from `export_themes.mjs`.** Honest and small, but the
   website images then depend on live segment probes on the CI runner. That is already true
   today for the 93 unpinned segments, so it is not a regression — but it is not an improvement
   either, and the theme images stay non-deterministic.

Do not silently pick the fallback because it is easier. If option 1 turns out to be
impractical, say what blocked it.

---

## Task D — reset `isHyperlink`

**Owns:** `src/terminal/writer.go` and its tests. Separate commit; unrelated to the rest.

`isHyperlink` is set at `writer.go:460`, `:503`, `:562` and cleared only by encountering
`<TEXT>`. It is not reset in `Write`'s prologue (`:385-392`) nor in `String()`'s deferred
cleanup (`:605-619`) — the only two reset points in the package. An unbalanced `<LINK>` with no
`</TEXT>` therefore leaves it `true` for the lifetime of the process, and every subsequent
`Write` takes the branch at `:700-703`: runes go straight into the builder with no length
counting and no shell escaping.

Reset it alongside the other per-render flags. Add a test that writes an unbalanced `<LINK>`
and asserts the next `Write` counts length correctly.

This must not change output for any balanced input — the golden harness from Task B is the
proof, so land it after B.

---

## Landing order

`A` → `B` → `C`, sequential: B's fixtures are invalid until A defines the marker, and C cannot
be validated until A2 is enforcing. `D` is independent but lands after B so the harness can
prove it inert.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` clean from `src/`.
2. All 122 goldens pass. Then deliberately corrupt one fixture and confirm the failure output
   names the theme and shows a readable escape context.
3. Re-run the full render sweep twice and diff — 122/122 identical, as measured today.
4. A data file lacking the marker fails with the explanatory error; the same file under
   `--data-derive` renders.
5. Assert the hermetic path does not call `Enabled()`. This is the SSRF-relevant claim.
6. Grep every committed fixture for the current user, host and home path — zero hits.
7. Benchmarks against the baseline above: allocs/op and B/op unchanged. Ignore ns/op, which
   swings 8x on this hardware.
8. `npm run themes` equivalent still produces images for a sample of themes.

content.text:
I have enough evidence. Here is the review.

## Findings, ranked

**1. The "hermetic by default / replay never calls `Enabled()`" decision is factually false, and the SSRF argument built on it collapses. (Critical — invalidates a stated design premise and the determinism measurement.)**

Claim: *"Replay never calls `Enabled()` unless explicitly asked… any path that runs them server-side is an SSRF proxy"* and verification step 5, *"Assert the hermetic path does not call `Enabled()`."*

Evidence: `D:\oh-my-posh\src\cli\config_export_data.go:129-131` — `if !segment.Enabled { continue }`. The recorder only writes segments that were enabled **and** rendered non-blank on the recording machine. Every other segment in the theme is absent from the fixture, so `restoreData` (`D:\oh-my-posh\src\config\segment.go:488-491`) returns `false` and `Execute` falls straight through to the live `segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`.

Measured on this machine:
- `themes/chips.omp.json` has 15 segments; the recording contains 5 (`battery`, `git`, `path`, `text`, `time`). `wakatime` is **not** recorded — and `Wakatime.Enabled()` (`src/segments/wakatime.go`) calls `setAPIData()` → HTTP.
- Replay timing: `tokyo` with its fixture = **0.09s**; `chips` with its fixture = **1.11s**. That 12x is a live network probe on the supposedly hermetic path.
- `themes/atomic.omp.json`: 24 configured segment keys, **9 recorded**, 15 missing (`go`, `node`, `python`, `dotnet`, `java`, `rust`, `ruby`, `dart`, `julia`, `angular`, `nx`, `aws`, `kubectl`, `root`, `azfunc`). `jandedobbeleer`: 8/17. `powerlevel10k_rainbow`: 6/15. `tokyo`: 9/16.

The proposed assertion will *pass* while being meaningless: any test using a segment that *is* in the fixture proves nothing about the ones that are not. The 122/122 determinism measurement is also explained by an accident, not by hermeticity — the fixture's `PWD` (`D:\oh-my-posh`) does not exist on CI, so `HasFiles` probes fail everywhere. Change the fixture PWD to a real path and that collapses.

Minimal fix: record **all** segments, enabled or not (drop the `!segment.Enabled` skip, add an `"enabled": false` marker per segment), and make `restoreData` return `true` for a recorded-but-disabled segment so it is suppressed without running. Then the assertion is worth writing: a fixture-driven render must make zero `RunCommand`/`HTTPRequest` calls.

---

**2. Goldens are timezone-dependent. 65 of 122 themes will fail on CI. (Critical — the "single most likely way this ships something that fails in CI", and the plan does not mention it.)**

`src/template/date.go:44` — `ompDate` calls `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")` → `t.In(loc).Format(fmt)`. The pinned `CurrentDate` is an absolute instant; it is rendered in the *renderer's* local zone.

Demonstrated: pinning `"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"` on this machine renders `10:41:00`, not `09:41:00`. GitHub runners are UTC; a European contributor regenerating goldens produces output shifted by 1–2 hours.

`grep -c '"type": "time"' themes/*.omp.json` → **65 themes**.

Minimal fix: the harness must pin `time.Local = time.UTC` in `TestMain` before any render (setting `TZ` is not reliable — `TZ=UTC` had no effect on this Windows build).

---

**3. Goldens are `TERM_PROGRAM`-dependent via `color.TrueColor`. (High.)**

`src/terminal/writer.go:192` — `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`, where `Program` comes from `os.Getenv("TERM_PROGRAM")` / `WT_SESSION` (`:207-215`). `color.TrueColor` gates truecolor vs. 256-color escape emission (`src/color/colors.go:312`, `src/color/gradient.go:351,395`).

Demonstrated: same theme, same fixture, `md5 = 455c2b60…` by default vs. `b430790c…` under `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`. Any contributor running `go test ./...` from macOS Terminal.app fails all 122 goldens.

Minimal fix: `TestMain` unsets `TERM_PROGRAM`/`WT_SESSION` (or sets `terminal.Program`/`color.TrueColor` explicitly) before `terminal.Init`.

---

**4. The harness cannot use `prompt.New`, and if it hand-rolls the Engine it does not exercise the path the plan claims to protect. (High — question 5.)**

`src/config/gob.go:44-49`: `config.Get` returns the **session-cached** config if one exists, ignoring `configFile` entirely. `prompt.New` (`src/prompt/engine.go:804-806`) calls exactly that. A test that loops `prompt.New` over 122 themes gets whatever config is in the session cache — or the developer's own, if `POSH_SESSION_ID` is exported (which it is, inside any real omp shell).

So the harness must build the Engine manually, the way `config_export_data.go:78-81` does. But that path skips everything `New` does after `config.Get`: `terminal.Plain = flags.Plain`, `forceRender`, `prompt.Grow(512)`, `flags.HasExtra`, and the shell-specific `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh (`engine.go:836-860`). Goldens produced that way do not protect those branches.

Minimal fix: extract the post-`config.Get` half of `New` into `newEngine(cfg *config.Config, env runtime.Environment) *Engine`, call it from both `New` and the harness, and have the harness use `config.Load(path)` directly.

---

**5. A2 is an unflagged breaking change to a released, documented feature — and the plan has no docs task. (High.)**

`--data` shipped in **v29.35.3** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor b95ad1a3 v29.35.3` → true). `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx` is a full page teaching users to hand-write partial files: line 54, *"A key left out falls back to the real environment, so specify only the properties your config depends on"*, plus a `<Config>` example with a hand-written `git`/`az` block.

A2 turns every one of those into a hard error. Task A owns only `src/`; Task C owns only `website/segment_data.json`, `export_themes.mjs`, `docs.yml`. Nothing updates `data.mdx`. Per the repo's breaking-change convention this is user-facing config behavior and needs the marker, which the plan does not call for.

Minimal fix: make the unmarked case a **warning** plus automatic derive (or gate the hard error behind an explicit `--data-strict`), and add `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx` to Task A's ownership.

---

**6. A3 puts `Enabled()` at the wrong point in `Execute`, bypassing width-hiding and the timeout Job machinery. (High.)**

Claim: *"`restoreData` calls `segment.writer.Enabled()` first and unmarshals the pinned data over the result."*

`restoreData` is invoked at `src/config/segment.go:203`, which is **before**:
- `shouldHideForWidth(...)` at `:212` — a derived segment renders even when `min_width`/`max_width` should hide it;
- `runjobs.CreateJobForGoroutine` / `defer runjobs.CloseGoroutineJob()` at `:227-241` — a pinned segment with `timeout` set runs live child processes with no Job object, so `KillGoroutineChildren` cannot terminate them on Windows;
- the `defer` at `:216-220` and `segment.evaluated = true` at `:244` (so `renderFallback` at `:297` stays dead for derived segments).

Minimal fix: under `--data-derive`, do not short-circuit at `:203`. Let `Execute` run normally and apply the overlay immediately after `:243`.

Two sub-points, both minor and both fine as designed:
- The overlay *mechanics* work. `json.Unmarshal(data, &segment.writer)` decodes into the existing writer through `encoding/json`'s `indirect`, so absent keys are preserved. Verified empirically (pinning only `CurrentDate`+`Format` renders correctly).
- `segment.Enabled = true` is set unconditionally, so `Enabled()` returning `false` will not suppress a pinned segment (e.g. `battery` on a machine with no battery). That is already today's `restoreData` behavior, so not a regression — but the plan should say so rather than imply "pinned fields win" covers it.

---

**7. Sanitization: a string-level replace both misses real leaks and corrupts good data. (High — question 4.)**

Generated fixtures on this machine and grepped them. What a `jande` → `alice` replace does:

*Corrupts:* `atomic.data.json:78-80` contains `"UpstreamURL": "https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh"` and `"RawUpstreamURL": "git@github.com:JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh.git"`. A case-insensitive replace yields `aliceDobbeleer` and a wrong golden. A case-*sensitive* replace misses `C:\Users\Jande` on a machine whose home dir is capitalized and `JANDE` from `%USERNAME%`.

*Misses:* the fixtures carry far more identity than the `env` block and the username —
- `Segment.Text` per segment: the **fully rendered** string, e.g. `" jande@surface-pro "`, `" D:  oh-my-posh "`.
- `git.User.Name` / `git.User.Email` — the real git author identity, populated whenever `fetch_user` is set (`src/segments/git.go:68,151,159`).
- `aws.AccessKeyID` — a credential-shaped field, already present in `website/segment_data.json`.
- `az`: `TenantID`, `HomeTenantID`, subscription IDs, `User.Name` (an email).
- `sysinfo`: real physical memory and load averages. `battery`: real charge state.
- `path.Folders[].Path`, `git.Dir`, `env.AbsolutePWD` — absolute paths in `D:\oh-my-posh` / `C:\Users\x` form; the same path appears as `/c/Users/x` under a POSIX shell and as `~/...` after `ReplaceHomeDirPrefixWithTilde`.
- Recorded hostname `surface-pro` — a device model, not just a name.

Minimal fix: sanitize **structurally at record time**, not as a post-hoc string pass. Add a `--sanitize` flag to `config export data` that (a) overwrites the `env` identity keys, (b) clears every `Segment.Text` (it is recomputed on render anyway), and (c) applies a per-field scrub list for the known identity/credential fields above. Keep the "no fixture contains the current user/host/home" test as a *backstop*, and add a denylist for `AccessKeyID`, `User.Email`, `TenantID`.

---

**8. Task C option 1 is not achievable; it is circular in exactly the way you suspected. (High.)**

`website/segment_data.json` pins 24 segment types and serves **all** themes. `config export data` records one config against one machine, and (per finding 1) only records segments it managed to enable. To reproduce the current file you would need a machine where `aws`, `az`, `gcp`, `kubectl`, `terraform`, `cf`, `cftarget`, `firebase`, `talosctl`, `azd`, `azfunc`, `cds`, `strava`, `wakatime`, `spotify` and `ytm` are all simultaneously live and authenticated. They are not — that is precisely why the file is hand-written.

Second blocker: `website/export_themes.mjs:167-171` already rewrites the file into `tmpdir()` at build time, injecting a live trending track into `spotify`/`ytm`. The pipeline is deliberately non-hermetic by design.

Minimal fix: neither option 1 nor option 2. If A2 is softened per finding 5, add `"version": 1` to `website/segment_data.json` by hand and move on — the file's synthetic values are the *point*, and marking a hand-curated file as intentional costs one line.

---

**9. Task C's change has no PR-time validation, and its failure mode is silent. (Medium.)**

`.github/workflows/code.yml` and `build_code.yml` both carry `paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, so a website-only change runs neither. `.github/workflows/docs.yml:3-9` triggers only on **push to main**. So if A2 breaks `segment_data.json`, nothing catches it until after merge.

Worse, `export_themes.mjs:236-241` treats any stderr as "skip this theme" and returns `null`; `main()` then appends whatever survived to `docs/themes.md` and exits 0. A2 breaking the data file produces a silently empty themes page, not a red build.

Minimal fix: have `exportTheme` propagate a non-zero exit as a hard failure, or add a `themes` smoke step to code.yml.

---

**10. The plan says 122 themes. There are 124. (Medium.)**

`ls themes/*.omp.json | wc -l` = 122, but `export_themes.mjs:18` matches `.omp.json`, `.omp.toml`, **and `.omp.yaml`**. `themes/devious-diamonds.omp.yaml` and `themes/glowsticks.omp.yaml` exist and are exported. The harness as specified would silently skip both — and YAML themes go through a different unmarshal path (`Segment.UnmarshalYAML`, `segment.go:133-155`) that would then have zero golden coverage.

Minimal fix: enumerate by the same extension set the website uses.

---

**11. Task D's "the golden harness is the proof" is false. (Medium.)**

`grep -l "<LINK>" themes/*.omp.*` → **0 files**. No bundled theme emits a hyperlink, so 122 (124) goldens prove exactly nothing about `isHyperlink`. Drop the claim and the "land D after B" ordering; the unit test the plan already specifies is the whole proof.

The Task D *diagnosis* is correct and verified: `isHyperlink` is a package global (`src/terminal/writer.go:78`), set at `:460`, `:503`, `:562`, cleared only on `<TEXT>` at `:508`/`:567`, and absent from both the `Write` prologue resets (`:385-392`) and the `String()` deferred cleanup (`:605-619`). The `serve` daemon makes "for the lifetime of the process" a real exposure, not a theoretical one.

---

**12. An in-process harness inherits the developer's real cache, including segment toggles. (Medium.)**

`cache.Init` → `Store.init` (`src/cache/store.go`) opens the real `omp.cache` under `cache.Path()`. `segment.isToggled()` (`segment.go:424-437`) reads `TOGGLECACHE` from `cache.Session` and returns **before** `restoreData`. A developer who has ever run `oh-my-posh toggle <segment>` gets different goldens. The device cache also feeds `segment.restoreCache()` (`:439`).

I have enough evidence. Here is the review.

## Findings, ranked

**1. The "hermetic by default / replay never calls `Enabled()`" decision is factually false, and the SSRF argument built on it collapses. (Critical — invalidates a stated design premise and the determinism measurement.)**

Claim: *"Replay never calls `Enabled()` unless explicitly asked… any path that runs them server-side is an SSRF proxy"* and verification step 5, *"Assert the hermetic path does not call `Enabled()`."*

Evidence: `D:\oh-my-posh\src\cli\config_export_data.go:129-131` — `if !segment.Enabled { continue }`. The recorder only writes segments that were enabled **and** rendered non-blank on the recording machine. Every other segment in the theme is absent from the fixture, so `restoreData` (`D:\oh-my-posh\src\config\segment.go:488-491`) returns `false` and `Execute` falls straight through to the live `segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`.

Measured on this machine:
- `themes/chips.omp.json` has 15 segments; the recording contains 5 (`battery`, `git`, `path`, `text`, `time`). `wakatime` is **not** recorded — and `Wakatime.Enabled()` (`src/segments/wakatime.go`) calls `setAPIData()` → HTTP.
- Replay timing: `tokyo` with its fixture = **0.09s**; `chips` with its fixture = **1.11s**. That 12x is a live network probe on the supposedly hermetic path.
- `themes/atomic.omp.json`: 24 configured segment keys, **9 recorded**, 15 missing (`go`, `node`, `python`, `dotnet`, `java`, `rust`, `ruby`, `dart`, `julia`, `angular`, `nx`, `aws`, `kubectl`, `root`, `azfunc`). `jandedobbeleer`: 8/17. `powerlevel10k_rainbow`: 6/15. `tokyo`: 9/16.

The proposed assertion will *pass* while being meaningless: any test using a segment that *is* in the fixture proves nothing about the ones that are not. The 122/122 determinism measurement is also explained by an accident, not by hermeticity — the fixture's `PWD` (`D:\oh-my-posh`) does not exist on CI, so `HasFiles` probes fail everywhere. Change the fixture PWD to a real path and that collapses.

Minimal fix: record **all** segments, enabled or not (drop the `!segment.Enabled` skip, add an `"enabled": false` marker per segment), and make `restoreData` return `true` for a recorded-but-disabled segment so it is suppressed without running. Then the assertion is worth writing: a fixture-driven render must make zero `RunCommand`/`HTTPRequest` calls.

---

**2. Goldens are timezone-dependent. 65 of 122 themes will fail on CI. (Critical — the "single most likely way this ships something that fails in CI", and the plan does not mention it.)**

`src/template/date.go:44` — `ompDate` calls `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")` → `t.In(loc).Format(fmt)`. The pinned `CurrentDate` is an absolute instant; it is rendered in the *renderer's* local zone.

Demonstrated: pinning `"CurrentDate":"2026-01-01T09:41:00Z"` on this machine renders `10:41:00`, not `09:41:00`. GitHub runners are UTC; a European contributor regenerating goldens produces output shifted by 1–2 hours.

`grep -c '"type": "time"' themes/*.omp.json` → **65 themes**.

Minimal fix: the harness must pin `time.Local = time.UTC` in `TestMain` before any render (setting `TZ` is not reliable — `TZ=UTC` had no effect on this Windows build).

---

**3. Goldens are `TERM_PROGRAM`-dependent via `color.TrueColor`. (High.)**

`src/terminal/writer.go:192` — `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`, where `Program` comes from `os.Getenv("TERM_PROGRAM")` / `WT_SESSION` (`:207-215`). `color.TrueColor` gates truecolor vs. 256-color escape emission (`src/color/colors.go:312`, `src/color/gradient.go:351,395`).

Demonstrated: same theme, same fixture, `md5 = 455c2b60…` by default vs. `b430790c…` under `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`. Any contributor running `go test ./...` from macOS Terminal.app fails all 122 goldens.

Minimal fix: `TestMain` unsets `TERM_PROGRAM`/`WT_SESSION` (or sets `terminal.Program`/`color.TrueColor` explicitly) before `terminal.Init`.

---

**4. The harness cannot use `prompt.New`, and if it hand-rolls the Engine it does not exercise the path the plan claims to protect. (High — question 5.)**

`src/config/gob.go:44-49`: `config.Get` returns the **session-cached** config if one exists, ignoring `configFile` entirely. `prompt.New` (`src/prompt/engine.go:804-806`) calls exactly that. A test that loops `prompt.New` over 122 themes gets whatever config is in the session cache — or the developer's own, if `POSH_SESSION_ID` is exported (which it is, inside any real omp shell).

So the harness must build the Engine manually, the way `config_export_data.go:78-81` does. But that path skips everything `New` does after `config.Get`: `terminal.Plain = flags.Plain`, `forceRender`, `prompt.Grow(512)`, `flags.HasExtra`, and the shell-specific `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh (`engine.go:836-860`). Goldens produced that way do not protect those branches.

Minimal fix: extract the post-`config.Get` half of `New` into `newEngine(cfg *config.Config, env runtime.Environment) *Engine`, call it from both `New` and the harness, and have the harness use `config.Load(path)` directly.

---

**5. A2 is an unflagged breaking change to a released, documented feature — and the plan has no docs task. (High.)**

`--data` shipped in **v29.35.3** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor b95ad1a3 v29.35.3` → true). `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx` is a full page teaching users to hand-write partial files: line 54, *"A key left out falls back to the real environment, so specify only the properties your config depends on"*, plus a `<Config>` example with a hand-written `git`/`az` block.

A2 turns every one of those into a hard error. Task A owns only `src/`; Task C owns only `website/segment_data.json`, `export_themes.mjs`, `docs.yml`. Nothing updates `data.mdx`. Minimal fix: make the unmarked case a **warning** plus automatic derive (or gate the hard error behind an explicit `--data-strict`), and add `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx` to Task A's ownership.

*Corrupts:* `atomic.data.json:78-80` contains `"UpstreamURL": "https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh"` and `"RawUpstreamURL": "git@github.com:JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh.git"`. *Misses:* the fixtures carry far more identity than the `env` block and the username —
- `Segment.Text` per segment: the **fully rendered** string, e.g. `" jande@surface-pro "`, `" D:  oh-my-posh "`.
- `git.User.Name` / `git.User.Email` — the real git author identity, populated whenever `fetch_user` is set (`src/segments/git.go:68,151,159`).
- `aws.AccessKeyID` — a credential-shaped field, already present in `website/segment_data.json`.
- `az`: `TenantID`, `HomeTenantID`, subscription IDs, `User.Name` (an email).

`.github/workflows/code.yml` and `build_code.yml` both carry `paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, so a website-only change runs neither. `.github/workflows/docs.yml:3-9` triggers only on **push to main**. So if A2 breaks `segment_data.json`, nothing catches it until after merge.

The review is pointing out a critical flaw in my approach: the recorder only captures enabled segments, so disabled ones still execute live, which means my `--data` replay mode isn't actually hermetic. The wakatime HTTP call during replay proves this—it's taking 1.11 seconds instead of the expected 0.09 seconds because it's making a real network request, not replaying recorded data. There's also a sanitization problem where string replacement corrupts data (mangling names in git URLs) and misses sensitive values entirely (git author emails, AWS keys, Azure tenant IDs, rendered segment text). The simultaneous authentication requirement for multiple cloud providers creates a circular dependency, and I've undercounted the themes—124 total, including 2 YAML themes that take a different unmarshal path with no test coverage. The harness itself doesn't prove anything since no bundled theme uses the link feature, and it inherits the developer's real cache including all their toggles. I also found citation errors in my analysis—DataKey is at a different line range and there are 118 segment types, not 117.

This fundamentally changes the phase strategy: if the data replay mechanism isn't hermetic, Phase 2.0 needs to expand to fix the recorder itself.

Verified. My plan was built on a false premise, and I need to say so plainly.

## The review killed my plan. Three of the findings are mine to own.

**`--data` replay is not hermetic, and my 122/122 determinism was an artifact.**

The recorder skips disabled segments — [`if !segment.Enabled { continue }`](src/cli/config_export_data.go:129). So a fixture only covers what happened to be live on the recording machine, and everything else falls through to live execution:

| theme | configured | recorded | replay |
|---|---|---|---|
| tokyo | 16 | 9 | 0.08s |
| atomic | 24 | 9 | 0.08s |
| **chips** | 15 | 5 | **1.22s** |

That 1.22s is `wakatime` making a real HTTP call on the supposedly hermetic path. My determinism sweep passed only because the fixture's `PWD` doesn't exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically — change that path and it collapses. The SSRF constraint I carried into this phase from the start rests on the same false premise.

**Two more of mine:** there are **124** themes, not 122 — I globbed `*.omp.json` and missed two YAML themes, which go through a different unmarshal path and would have had zero coverage. And my citation of `DataKey` pointed at `restoreData`'s line range.

## Three that would have failed in CI

- **Timezone.** 65 themes carry a `time` segment, and `date` renders in the *renderer's* local zone. I demonstrated this myself without noticing: I pinned `09:41:00Z` and it rendered `10:41:00`. CI runners are UTC; my goldens would fail on every one.
- **`TERM_PROGRAM`.** [`color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`](src/terminal/writer.go:192) gates truecolor vs 256-colour emission. Same theme, same fixture, different bytes under macOS Terminal.app — and `code.yml` runs tests on all three OSes.
- **`prompt.New` reads the session cache** ([gob.go:44](src/config/gob.go:44)), so a harness looping over themes gets whatever config is cached, or the developer's own if `POSH_SESSION_ID` is set — which it is inside any real omp shell.

## And one design error

My A2 — hard-fail on unmarked data files — is a **breaking change to a feature shipped in v29.35.3**. [`data.mdx:54`](website/docs/configuration/data.mdx:54) explicitly teaches the opposite: *"A key left out falls back to the real environment, so specify only the properties your config depends on."* My plan had no docs task and would have broken every user following that page.

Also: Task C option 1 is circular, as the review put it — reproducing `segment_data.json` by recording would need a machine with AWS, Azure, GCP, kubectl, Terraform, Strava and Spotify all simultaneously authenticated. That's *why* it's hand-written.

## What this means for the phase

The centrepiece isn't the harness any more — it's the recorder. Record every segment with an explicit enabled flag, and make `restoreData` suppress recorded-but-disabled segments so they never probe. Only then is replay hermetic, only then is the harness meaningful, and only then does the render endpoint have a safety story.

That's a bigger, more invasive change than "build a safety net," and it lands in the same `Execute` path the tokenizer refactor will touch.

input.content:
# Phase 2.0 — Hermetic replay and the golden harness

The safety net for the renderer work, plus the correctness bug found while building it.
No run stream, no SVG, no tokenizer changes.

**Revision 2.** The first draft rested on a false premise: that `--data` replay is hermetic.
It is not. Every change from that draft is marked **[R]**.

## The premise that was wrong

`config export data` skips segments that were not enabled on the recording machine —
`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`:

```go
for _, segment := range block.Segments {
    if !segment.Enabled {
        continue
    }
```

So a fixture covers only what happened to be live when it was recorded, and every other segment
falls through `restoreData` (`src/config/segment.go:488-491`, returns `false`) into the live
`segment.writer.Enabled()` at `:243`.

| theme | segments configured | recorded | replay |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tokyo | 16 | 9 | 0.08s |
| atomic | 24 | 9 | 0.08s |
| jandedobbeleer | 17 | 8 | 0.07s |
| **chips** | 15 | 5 | **1.22s** |

The 1.22s is `wakatime` making a live HTTP request during what was supposed to be a replay.

The earlier "122/122 deterministic" measurement was an artifact: the fixture's `PWD` does not
exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically on both sweeps. It proves nothing.

## Verified facts

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `restoreData` returns before `writer.Enabled()` | `src/config/segment.go:203-205` vs `:243` |
| `Time.Format` is computed inside `Enabled()`, so replay renders it empty | `src/segments/time.go:27-28` |
| Pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` drops the whole rprompt block, silently | measured 419 → 328 bytes on `agnosterplus` |
| Adding `Format` restores it | measured 419 bytes, renders `10:41:00` |
| 53 of 102 `Enabled()` implementations assign template-visible state; ≥24 do I/O | scan |
| **The recorder skips disabled segments** | `src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131` |
| **124 themes, not 122** — 122 `.omp.json` plus 2 `.omp.yaml` | `ls themes/*.omp.*` |
| **65 themes carry a `time` segment** | `grep -l '"type": *"time"'` |
| **`date` renders in the renderer's local zone** | pinned `09:41:00Z` rendered `10:41:00` here |
| **`color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`** gates truecolor vs 256-colour | `src/terminal/writer.go:192`, read at `src/color/colors.go:312` |
| **`prompt.New` returns the session-cached config, ignoring the path** | `src/config/gob.go:44-49`, called from `src/prompt/engine.go:804-806` |
| **`--data` shipped in v29.35.3 and `data.mdx` documents partial hand-written files** | `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx:54-55` |
| **No bundled theme uses `<LINK>`** | `grep -l '<LINK>' themes/*.omp.*` returns 0 |
| `isHyperlink` is reset in neither `Write`'s prologue nor `String()`'s cleanup | `writer.go:78`, `:385-392`, `:605-619` |
| `DataKey` is the segment `Alias` or `Type` | `src/config/segment.go:412-418` |
| No theme PNG is tracked in git | `git ls-files 'website/static/img/themes/*'` → 0 |
| ns/op swings ~8x on this hardware; B/op and allocs/op are exactly stable | `-count=3` |
| `LoadData` reads only `env` and `segments`, tolerating unknown top-level keys | `src/config/data.go:43-90` |

Baseline to hold: `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 9,150 B / 95 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 602 B /
14 allocs; `BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 280 B / 6 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteSolid` 465 B / 16 allocs;
`BenchmarkWriteGradient` 1,762 B / 17 allocs; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 789 B / 27 allocs.

## Decisions taken

- Ship Phase 2.0 alone, before the tokenizer refactor.
- **[R] Fix the recorder properly.** Record every configured segment with an explicit enabled
  flag; `restoreData` suppresses recorded-but-disabled segments without probing. Hermeticity has
  to be real before the harness or any render endpoint can lean on it.
- **[R] No breaking change.** Hand-written partial files keep working, with a warning and
  correctly derived state. `data.mdx:54` documents them and `--data` shipped in v29.35.3.

## Out of scope

The run stream, the SVG encoder, the tokenizer collapse, deleting `cli/image/`, the missing
`Plain` guard on OSC 8 emission, recording tooltip segments (`buildDataDocument` iterates
`cfg.Blocks` only, `config_export_data.go:127`), and changing the `DataKey` scheme.

**[R] Known limitation to document, not fix:** themes with two segments of the same type and no
`alias` collide on `DataKey` — the recorder already warns `multiple segments share the data key
"text"; the last one wins`. Goldens will encode that lossy behaviour. That is acceptable: the
harness is a change-detector, and the behaviour it locks in is the current one.

---

## Task A — make replay hermetic

**Owns:** `src/cli/config_export_data.go`, `src/config/data.go`, `src/config/segment.go`,
`src/cli/data.go`, `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`, and their tests.

### A1. Record everything

Drop the `!segment.Enabled` skip. Record every configured segment, carrying its enabled state:

```json
{ "version": 1, "env": { … }, "segments": { "git": { "enabled": true, "data": { … } } } }
```

Shape is Task A's call, but the enabled flag must be per segment and must survive round-trip.
Keep backward compatibility with the current flat shape, since `website/segment_data.json` and
every user file use it.

`version` is safe to add: `LoadData` decodes the root into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and
reads only `env` and `segments`, so unknown top-level keys are already tolerated on the JSON,
YAML and TOML paths.

### A2. Suppress recorded-but-disabled segments

In `restoreData`:

- present and enabled → current behaviour: unmarshal the pinned data, `Enabled = true`, return
  `true`. No probe.
- **[R]** present and disabled → `Enabled = false`, `restored = true`, return `true`. **No
  probe.** This is the case that makes replay hermetic.
- absent → return `false` and fall through, as today.

**[R]** Do not move the recorded path's short-circuit. It sits at `:203`, before
`shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`) and the `runjobs` Job setup (`:227-241`). That bypass exists
today; changing it would change rendered output, and this phase's entire purpose is to
establish a baseline before output changes. File the width-hiding gap separately.

### A3. Warn and derive for unmarked files

A file without `version` is hand-written. Keep it working:

- Warn once per run, naming the file, saying it is neither hermetic nor deterministic, and
  giving the recorder command.
- For segments present in it, compute derived state so they stop silently vanishing.
- For segments absent from it, fall back to the live environment — the documented contract at
  `data.mdx:54-55`.

**[R] Where the derive happens matters.** Do **not** short-circuit at `:203` for this path.
Let `Execute` run normally so `Enabled()` fires at `:243` and then overlay the pinned data on
top. Short-circuiting at `:203` would skip `shouldHideForWidth` (`:212`), the `runjobs` Job
creation and its `defer` (`:227-241`) — so a pinned segment with a `timeout` would spawn live
child processes with no Job object, and `KillGoroutineChildren` could not terminate them on
Windows — and `segment.evaluated = true` at `:244`, leaving `renderFallback` (`:297`) dead.

Order is `Enabled()` then overlay, never the reverse. `json.Unmarshal` into the existing writer
preserves fields absent from the JSON, so pinned values win and derived values fill the gaps.

Add `--data-derive` to force this path for a recorded file too, for local debugging.

**[R] Note and document:** `restoreData` sets `Enabled = true` unconditionally, so a pinned
segment renders even where its live check would suppress it — `battery` on a machine without
one. That is today's behaviour and stays; say so in the docs rather than leaving it implicit.

### A4. Docs

Update `website/docs/configuration/data.mdx`: the recorder is the recommended path and the only
hermetic one; hand-written partial files still work and now derive correctly; the `version`

---
name: omp-data-replay-not-hermetic
description: "--data replay is not hermetic: the recorder skips disabled segments, so unrecorded ones still probe live"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Discovered 2026-07-26 while building a golden-file harness for the renderer work.

`oh-my-posh config export data` skips segments that were not enabled on the recording
machine (`src/cli/config_export_data.go:129-131`, `if !segment.Enabled { continue }`).
A fixture therefore covers only what happened to be live at record time; everything else
falls through `restoreData` (`src/config/segment.go:488-491` returns false) into the live
`writer.Enabled()` at `:243`. Measured: `themes/chips.omp.json` records 5 of 15 segments and
"replays" in **1.22s** because `wakatime` makes a real HTTP call, versus ~0.08s for themes
whose segments were all captured.

Two consequences that cost a full replan:

1. **Any "golden files over the bundled themes" measurement is suspect.** An early sweep
   showed 122/122 deterministic; that was an artifact — the fixture's pinned `PWD` does not
   exist, so every filesystem probe failed identically on both runs.
2. **The SSRF argument for a server-side render endpoint does not hold on replay alone.**
   `http`, `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist` and `wakatime` all take a URL or key from config.
   Until the recorder captures every segment *and* `restoreData` suppresses recorded-but-
   disabled ones without probing, a data file is not a safety boundary.

Related: `restoreData` returns before `Enabled()`, and 53 of 102 segments assign
template-visible state inside `Enabled()` (≥24 of those do I/O). So a hand-written partial
file silently renders those segments empty — pinning `time` with only `CurrentDate` drops
the whole rprompt block, because `Time.Format` is computed in `Enabled()`
(`src/segments/time.go:27-28`).

**Why:** three separate plans were built on "replay is hermetic" before it was measured.

**How to apply:** never treat a `--data` file as a hermetic or security boundary without
first checking the recorder covers every configured segment. Verify hermeticity by *timing*
a replay, not by diffing two runs — identical output can mean uniformly failing probes.
See [[omp-golden-harness-ambient-inputs]] for what else makes theme renders non-reproducible.

---
name: omp-golden-harness-ambient-inputs
description: "Ambient inputs that make oh-my-posh theme renders non-reproducible: local timezone, TERM_PROGRAM, session cache, prompt.New"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Found 2026-07-26 while scoping a golden-file harness over the bundled themes. Any test that
renders themes and compares bytes must neutralise all of these, or it fails on CI (which runs
ubuntu, macos and windows) while passing locally.

- **Local timezone.** `date` renders through `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")`
  (`src/template/date.go:44`), so a pinned absolute `CurrentDate` still prints in the
  renderer's zone — pinning `09:41:00Z` rendered `10:41:00` here. **65 of 124 themes** carry a
  `time` segment. Set `time.Local = time.UTC` in `TestMain`; setting `TZ` does not work on
  Windows.
- **`TERM_PROGRAM` / `WT_SESSION`.** `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal`
  (`src/terminal/writer.go:192`) gates truecolor versus 256-colour emission
  (`src/color/colors.go:312`). Same theme and fixture produce different bytes under
  macOS Terminal.app. Unset both, or set `terminal.Program` explicitly, before `terminal.Init`.
- **The session cache.** `segment.isToggled()` (`src/config/segment.go:424-437`) reads
  `TOGGLECACHE` and returns *before* `restoreData`, so anyone who has run `oh-my-posh toggle`
  gets different output. Point `cache.Path()` at a temp dir and do not call `cache.Close()`.
- **`prompt.New` ignores the config path.** It calls `config.Get`, which returns the
  session-cached config (`src/config/gob.go:44-49`) — inside a real omp shell that is the
  developer's own config, not the theme under test. But hand-rolling the Engine skips what
  `New` does after `config.Get` (`terminal.Plain`, `forceRender`, `Grow(512)`, `HasExtra`,
  `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh, `engine.go:836-860`). Extract the second half
  of `New` so both paths share it.

Also: there are **124** themes, not 122 — `themes/*.omp.yaml` adds two, and YAML goes through a
separate `Segment.UnmarshalYAML` path (`segment.go:133-155`). Enumerate by the same extension
set `website/export_themes.mjs:18` uses.

Benchmark gate on this hardware: **ns/op swings ~8x run to run** (1492–11816 for one
benchmark); `B/op` and `allocs/op` are exactly stable. Gate on allocations, never on time.

**Why:** each of these was found only by an adversarial review of a plan that looked finished,
and every one of them fails in CI rather than locally.

**How to apply:** read this before writing any test that renders a prompt and compares output.
See [[omp-data-replay-not-hermetic]] for why the fixtures themselves need work first.

content.text:
Two agents running. Where Phase 2 stands:

**The analysis was the deliverable this time.** I went in planning to build a golden harness and extract a run stream. Both premises turned out to be wrong, and the second one only broke under review:

- `--data` replay isn't hermetic. The recorder skips disabled segments, so `chips.omp.json` "replays" in 1.22s while `wakatime` makes a live HTTP call. My 122/122 determinism result was an artifact of a pinned `PWD` that doesn't exist, making every filesystem probe fail identically.
- The run-stream seam isn't in `terminal/`. Semantic colour is destroyed at [writer.go:377](src/terminal/writer.go:377) before anything is written, and segment identity never exists there at all — `Write` is called once per *fragment*, four times per segment, driven from `prompt/engine.go`.

**The refactor has a better justification than SVG anyway.** There are three hand-maintained copies of the same tokenizer — `writeBody`, `writeBodyGradient`, `countVisibleCells` — which [writer.go:886](src/terminal/writer.go:886) documents must stay in lockstep.

**Corrections to figures I gave you earlier:** the imager deletion is ~29,600 lines and 4 modules, not ~1,500 and 3. There are 124 themes, not 122 — I globbed `*.omp.json` and missed two YAML ones that use a different unmarshal path. And no theme PNG is tracked in git, so the design doc's "deletes 8 MB" was wrong; the win is build time and a runtime GitHub dependency, not repo size.

**In flight:** Task A makes replay actually hermetic and fixes the vanishing-segment bug without breaking the documented hand-written-file contract. Task D resets `isHyperlink`, which currently corrupts every subsequent `Write` for the process lifetime after one unbalanced `<LINK>` — which matters because the `serve` daemon is long-lived.

Then the harness (Task B), which needs `TestMain` to pin UTC, neutralise `TERM_PROGRAM`, and isolate the cache — 65 themes render a clock, and `code.yml` runs on three OSes.

Worth flagging before B: **`themes/**` is in no `paths-ignore`**, so once goldens land, every theme-touching PR regenerates them. Your recent gradient work would have. That's the standing cost of the safety net, and it's the right trade before touching the hot path — but it's your repo's daily friction, so tell me if you'd rather scope the harness to a representative subset instead of all 124.

which also keeps width hiding and the job setup for segments with a timeout.

produces one.

overlay would otherwise run.

## Design change: hash manifest + representative full goldens

Do NOT commit 124 full golden files. `themes/**` is in no workflow's `paths-ignore`, so every theme-touching PR would regenerate them and produce an unreadable diff.

Instead:
- **A hash manifest** covering all 124 themes: one line per theme, `<theme> <sha256-of-rendered-bytes>`, sorted. A theme change touches one line.
- **Full goldens for ~12 representative themes**, chosen to cover: both `.omp.yaml` themes (they use a different unmarshal path, `Segment.UnmarshalYAML` at `src/config/segment.go`), plain/powerline/diamond styles, a gradient theme, an rprompt theme, a theme with `<LINK>`-free hyperlink-adjacent markup if one exists, and the busiest theme by segment count. State your selection and why.
- Failure output must show, for a hash mismatch, the theme name and the regeneration command; for a full-golden mismatch, the first differing byte offset plus a decoded escape-sequence context window. A raw diff of two ANSI blobs is unreadable and this harness exists to be read during a refactor.
- Regeneration is ONE documented command, named in every failure message.

## Three ambient inputs that WILL break this on CI

`.github/workflows/code.yml` runs `go test ./...` on ubuntu, macos AND windows. `TestMain` must neutralise all three of these or the harness passes locally and fails in CI:

1. `time.Local = time.UTC`. 65 of 124 themes render a `time` segment via `dateInZone(fmt, date, "Local")` (`src/template/date.go:44`), so a pinned absolute instant still prints in the renderer's zone — pinning `09:41:00Z` renders `10:41:00` here. Setting the `TZ` env var does NOT work on Windows; assign `time.Local` directly.
2. Unset `TERM_PROGRAM` and `WT_SESSION` (or set `terminal.Program`/`color.TrueColor` explicitly) before `terminal.Init`. `color.TrueColor = Program != AppleTerminal` (`src/terminal/writer.go:192`) gates truecolor vs 256-colour emission, so macOS Terminal.app produces different bytes.
3. Point `cache.Path()` at a temp dir and do NOT call `cache.Close()`. `segment.isToggled()` (`src/config/segment.go`) reads the session cache and returns before `restoreData`, so anyone who has run `oh-my-posh toggle` gets different output.

`prompt.New` calls `config.Get`, which returns the SESSION-CACHED config and ignores the path entirely (`src/config/gob.go:44-49`) — inside a real omp shell that is the developer's own config, not the theme under test. But hand-rolling the Engine the way `src/cli/config_export_data.go` does skips what `New` performs after `config.Get`: `terminal.Plain`, `forceRender`, `prompt.Grow(512)`, `flags.HasExtra`, and `rectifyTerminalWidth` for xonsh/elvish/pwsh (`src/prompt/engine.go:836-860`).

A naive replace both corrupts and misses. Case-insensitively replacing the username rewrites `https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/oh-my-posh` in recorded git data; case-sensitively it misses `C:\Users\Jande` and caps `%USERNAME%`. And identity is not confined to the `env` block — recorded fixtures carry `Segment.Text` (the fully rendered string, e.g. `" jande@surface-pro "`), `git.User.Name`/`User.Email`, `aws.AccessKeyID`, `az` TenantID/HomeTenantID/subscription IDs, `path.Folders[].Path`, `git.Dir`, `env.AbsolutePWD`/`PSWD`/`Folder`, real `sysinfo` memory and load, and real `battery` charge.

Add tests asserting no committed fixture contains the current user, hostname or home path, and none contains `AccessKeyID`, `User.Email` or `TenantID`. That backstop is what catches the next person regenerating on their own machine before it reaches a public repo.

## Verify before reporting

- Run the harness with `TZ` set to a non-UTC zone AND with `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal` — both must still pass.
- Run with `POSH_SESSION_ID` set to something, proving the session cache is ignored.
- Corrupt one fixture and confirm the failure names the theme and shows a readable context.
- Confirm all 124 themes are covered (122 `.omp.json` + 2 `.omp.yaml`).
- Benchmarks unchanged: `go test -run=XXX -bench='BenchmarkEnginePrimary' -benchtime=200x -count=3 ./prompt/...`, baseline 9,150 B / 95 allocs. Gate on allocs and B/op; ns/op swings ~8x on this hardware, ignore it.
- Report how long the harness adds to `go test ./...`.

You own `website/export_themes.mjs`. Touch nothing else — other tasks are concurrently editing `src/`.

Context: commit b8381b97 just made `--data` replay hermetic. `oh-my-posh config export data` now writes a `version` marker; a file without one is treated as hand-written, still works exactly as documented, but emits a one-line warning to stderr.

Do NOT try to replace it with a recording: that is circular, since reproducing it would need a machine with AWS, Azure, GCP, kubectl, Terraform, Cloud Foundry, Firebase, Strava, Spotify and YouTube Music all simultaneously authenticated.

Two changes:

1. **Pass `--data-derive` explicitly** from `buildPoshCommand` (around `export_themes.mjs:179-193`). This states the intent — the file is deliberately hand-written — and silences the new warning. Confirm the flag exists and is spelled correctly by running `oh-my-posh print --help` against a binary you build from `src/`, rather than trusting this brief.

2. **Make a failed theme export a hard failure.** Today `exportTheme` (around `:236-241`) treats any stderr output as "skip this theme" and returns `null`, and `main` still exits 0. So a broken data file produces a silently empty themes page instead of a red build. This is doubly bad because nothing validates it at PR time: `.github/workflows/code.yml` and `build_code.yml` both carry `paths-ignore: ['website/**']`, and `.github/workflows/docs.yml` only triggers on push to main.

   Be careful: the existing code treats *any* stderr as failure, which is now wrong in a new way — a warning on stderr is not a failure. Distinguish a non-zero exit code from incidental stderr output. A theme that genuinely fails to render must fail the build with a message naming the theme; a theme that merely writes a warning must succeed.

Verify before reporting, and report the actual commands:
- Build a binary from `src/` and run the real pipeline end to end for a small subset of themes (temporarily narrow the theme list, or run the underlying command directly for 3-4 themes). Confirm images are produced and no warning appears.
- Deliberately break one theme's export (e.g. point it at a nonexistent config) and confirm the script now exits non-zero and names that theme.
- Confirm a theme that only emits a warning still succeeds.
- Confirm you restored any temporary narrowing of the theme list.

Note the imager downloads a Nerd Font from GitHub on a cold cache, so the first run may be slow or may fail without network — if that happens, say so plainly rather than reporting a false success.

Report: the diff, the commands you ran, their output, and anything in the plan that turned out to be wrong.

Two commits landed, B and C running.

**`b8381b97`** — hermetic replay. Verified on my own build: `chips` records 14 of 15 segments instead of 5, and replays in **0.07s instead of 1.19s**. The pinned `time` segment that used to render nothing now renders, and all 124 themes still work with the existing hand-written file.

I made the call on the golden-file question rather than leave it hanging: **hash manifest for all 124 themes, full goldens for ~12 representative ones**. That keeps complete coverage while a theme edit touches one manifest line instead of regenerating a wall of files — which was the friction I was worried about handing you.

Two process notes, both mine:

- I hit **cwd drift three times** this phase, and one instance produced a confident "124 of 124 themes render empty" that was purely my own scripting error. I caught each one, but the pattern is that a failed `cd` in a `&&` chain leaves later commands running somewhere unexpected. I've told the remaining agents to use absolute paths.
- I ran a `git stash` while an agent was writing files. The pathspec scoped it and nothing was lost, but that was careless with parallel work in flight.

The delegate on Task A did the thing that makes delegation worth it — it found the `restoreCache` ordering problem, judged it outside its brief, and flagged it instead of silently fixing or ignoring it. It was right, it was reachable in exactly one bundled theme, and that theme was the one in my timing proof.

After B and C, Phase 2.0 is done and 2.1 is the tokenizer collapse — three hand-maintained copies of the same scanner in `terminal/`, which is the real risk in this whole line of work and where I'd want the adversarial review gate again.

Phase 2.0 complete. Four commits:

| | |
|---|---|
| `1e610dff` | `isHyperlink` leaked across writes for the process lifetime |
| `b8381b97` | hermetic replay — chips 1.19s → 0.07s |
| `5a8ee35d` | failed image export exited 0 |
| `055ca502` | golden harness over all 124 themes |

**The near-miss is the thing worth your attention.** Your real email address was in 8 fixtures, at `segments.az.data.user.name`, and it was *rendering into visible prompt output* — not sitting inert in unused JSON. Root cause: the sanitizer scrubbed `az.User.Name` by Go field name, but `AzureUser` carries explicit json tags, so the serialized keys are `user.name`. **All four `az` scrubs were silent no-ops.** A sanitizer that quietly does nothing while its own tests pass is the worst possible failure mode here.

It survived the first backstop because that test enumerated field names — `Email`, `AccessKeyID`, `TenantID` — and this value sits under a key called `name`. The replacement walks every string in every fixture and rejects anything *shaped* like an email, absolute path, username or hostname, whatever key holds it. I proved it load-bearing by planting an email under an invented key: it fails, names the value and path, and passes on revert.

I found it by walking the JSON tree rather than grepping the fields the sanitizer claimed to handle. Verifying a sanitizer against its own field list will always pass.

**Verified independently, not from reports:** manifest byte-stable across regenerations; passes under `TZ=Asia/Tokyo TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal POSH_SESSION_ID=live WT_SESSION=x` combined; recolouring one `tokyo` segment fails at byte offset 33 with the regen command; 21 packages green; `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` flat at 95 allocs.

Two more real bugs the agent found on its own: `template.Init` only rebuilds the global cache when nil, so rendering 124 themes in one process silently reused the first render's identity until `ResetCache()` was called — caught by the regenerate-twice check. And `manifest.sha256` matched the repo's `*.sha256` gitignore rule, so the manifest would never have been committed.

**Phase 2.1 next** — collapsing the three hand-maintained copies of the same tokenizer in `terminal/`. That one edits the prompt hot path, and the harness now exists to gate it: byte-identical output across 124 themes, allocations flat. Given this phase's analysis was wrong twice before review caught it, I'd keep the adversarial review gate on it.

The real question is how to unify them without tanking performance. I'm weighing three approaches: a single loop with a boolean flag to branch on (zero allocation, minimal overhead), a callback interface (risky for allocations in the hot path), or a visitor struct passed by pointer (might still heap-allocate). # Phase 2.1 — One tokenizer

Collapse the three hand-maintained copies of the same scanner in `src/terminal/writer.go`
into one. No run stream, no SVG, no behaviour change except the drift bug below.

## Why now, with evidence

`writer.go:895-902` documents that `writeBody`, `writeBodyGradient` and `countVisibleCells`
must walk text with "the exact same tokenization rules". They do not. Measured:

```
input:  ab<transparent,transparent>hidden</LINK>tail
VisibleCells() = 6        (counts "ab" + "tail")
rendered length = 2       (renders "ab")
```

`countVisibleCells` (`:945-966`) has no `hyperLinkEnd` case. `</LINK>` therefore falls to
`default`, which recomputes `invisible = match.FG == transparent && match.BG == transparent`.
Both are empty for `</LINK>`, so invisible flips back to false and the tail is counted.
`writeBody`/`writeBodyGradient` (`:529`, `:590`) have an explicit `hyperLinkEnd` case that
only consumes the token, so `isInvisible` survives — which is the documented long-standing
behaviour, pinned by `TestWriteGradientInvisibleSpanExcluded`
(`writer_gradient_test.go:423-446`, "isInvisible persists past `</>`").

The count feeds `color.GradientCells`, so a segment whose template contains an invisible span
followed by `</LINK>` gets its gradient interpolated over the wrong number of cells.

That is the justification. Not SVG — this is a live bug caused by the duplication.

## The three copies, precisely

| | lines | differs from `writeBody` by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `writeBody` | `:492-545` | — |
| `writeBodyGradient` | `:551-598+` | `writeVisibleRune` instead of `write`; `stampGradient()` and `cellIndex += 4` in the `hyperLinkTextEnd` case |
| `countVisibleCells` | `:903-972` | emits nothing; keeps `hyperlink`/`invisible` in locals rather than package globals; no `hyperLinkEnd` case (the bug) |

Everything else — the `s != '<'` fast path, `scanAnchor`, the `match.ok` fallback, the five
anchor cases, the `hyperlinkTextPosition` no-text fallback of 4 — is duplicated verbatim.

## Constraints

- **Byte-identical ANSI for all 124 bundled themes**, except where the drift fix legitimately
  changes a gradient cell count. Any golden change must be explained and justified segment by
  segment, never blanket-regenerated.
- **Allocations must not regress.** `BenchmarkEnginePrimary` 95 allocs/op, 9,150 B/op;
  `BenchmarkWriteAnchors` 14 / 602; `BenchmarkWritePlainASCII` 6 / 280; `BenchmarkWriteSolid`
  16 / 465; `BenchmarkWriteGradient` 17 / 1,762; `BenchmarkWriteGradientChained` 27 / 789.
  Gate on allocs/op and B/op only — ns/op swings ~8x run to run on this hardware.
- **No closures over per-call state in the hot path.** A callback-per-token design will heap
  allocate the closure and blow the allocation gate. This is the single most likely way to
  fail.
- `write()` is called per rune for every prompt on every keypress. Treat it accordingly.

## Design

A cursor struct with a `next()` method, shared by all three consumers:

```go
type token struct {
    Anchor string   // "" for a literal rune
    FG, BG string
    Rune   rune
    Size   int      // bytes consumed
    Kind   tokenKind
}
```

Each consumer keeps its own loop and its own actions; only the scanning and classification
move into the cursor. A struct with a pointer receiver and no escaping references stays on
the stack, so no allocation. Verify that with `-gcflags=-m` and the benchmarks, not by
assumption.

Do **not** unify the three consumers' *actions* behind a mode enum or an interface. The
actions genuinely differ (emit / emit+stamp / count-only), and the state they mutate differs
(package globals vs locals). Unifying scanning is the win; unifying actions reintroduces
branching in the per-rune path for no benefit.

## Tasks

### Task A — extract the cursor

Introduce the cursor and rewrite the three consumers against it, preserving current behaviour
**including the drift bug**. This step must be provably inert: all 124 goldens byte-identical,
every existing terminal test passing unchanged, allocations flat.

Landing the extraction and the bug fix separately is the whole point — if a golden moves in
Task A, the extraction is wrong.

### Task B — fix the drift

Give `countVisibleCells`'s consumer the `hyperLinkEnd` case the others have, so `</LINK>`
consumes without touching invisibility. Add the case above as a regression test asserting
`VisibleCells(txt)` equals the rendered length.

Expect goldens to move only for themes that actually contain an invisible span followed by
`</LINK>`. Report which themes moved and why; if none move, say so — the bundled themes may
not exercise it, and the unit test is then the only proof.

### Task C — the sibling defects, only if trivially safe

`writer.go:700-703` emits OSC 8 hyperlink sequences with no `Plain` guard, unlike every other
escape emitter in the package. Fix only if it leaves all 124 goldens unchanged (it should —
goldens are not rendered with `Plain`), and add a test asserting `Plain` suppresses hyperlink
escapes. If it moves a golden, stop and report instead.

## Verification (coordinator, not delegated)

1. `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` clean.
2. All 124 goldens byte-identical after Task A. This is the gate.
3. Benchmarks after each task: allocs/op and B/op against the baseline above.
4. `go test -run=XXX -bench=. -benchtime=200x -count=6 ./terminal/...` before and after, compared
   with benchstat on allocs.
5. The drift case renders and counts consistently after Task B.
6. `TZ=Asia/Tokyo TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal` — harness still passes.
7. Escape-emission ordering is unchanged: the existing byte-exact tests in `writer_test.go`,
   `writer_hyperlink_test.go` and `writer_gradient_test.go` must pass **without edits**. If any
   expected string needs changing, that is a behaviour change and must be justified, not
   accommodated.

## Out of scope

The run stream, SVG, de-globalizing the 28 package variables, `isInvisible`'s persistence past
`</>` (long-standing, pinned by tests, and changing it is a user-visible behaviour change), and
