## Investigation summary

I read `src/svg/svg.go` in full, `src/cli/image/image.go` in full (920 lines), the goreleaser/workflow config, and checked license/maintenance/dependency facts for each rasterizer candidate via GitHub's API and web search. Findings below are evidence-backed; nothing was modified.

### 1. CGO today: none — and the release pipeline actively forbids it

- `grep -r 'import "C"' src/` — **zero matches**. No CGO anywhere in the module.
- `src/.goreleaser.yml:26`: `CGO_ENABLED=0`, plus build tags `netgo, osusergo, static_build, timetzdata` and `-extldflags "-static"`. One `goreleaser` job cross-compiles for `goos: [linux, windows, darwin, freebsd] × goarch: [amd64, arm64, arm]` (minus darwin/arm and windows/arm) from what is effectively a single build step — no per-platform native runners, no sysroots.
- `.github/workflows/code.yml` only runs `go test` natively on `[ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]` — that's test coverage, not the release build matrix.

**Conclusion: a CGO dependency is a non-starter.** It would break the single-job cross-compile model outright (CGO cross-compilation needs a C toolchain/sysroot per target) and contradicts the explicit `CGO_ENABLED=0` + static-link posture the project has already committed to. Anything considered must be pure Go.

### 2. Pure-Go SVG rasterizer options

| Option | CGO? | Renders `<text>`? | License | Maintained? | Dependency weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tdewolff/canvas` | No by default (optional `harfbuzz_cgo.go`/`fribidi_cgo.go` behind `//go:build harfbuzz`/`fribidi` tags, off unless opted in) | Yes — but its own SVG *file* parsing (`ParseSVG`) is the least mature part of the library per its issue tracker; its real strength is emitting from a Go drawing API, not reading SVG back in | MIT | Active (pushed within days) | **Very heavy.** `go.mod` pulls in `fyne.io/fyne` (a full GUI toolkit + systray + glfw-js + IndexedDB shims), `gioui.org` (+ shader/GPU), `go-gl/gl`+`glfw`, `gonum.org/v1/plot`, `go-sql-driver/mysql`, `go-webp`, `go-avif`, a LaTeX renderer, a PDF library, geo/projection packages (`paulmach/orb`, `paulmach/osm`, `wgs84`) — dozens of transitive deps with nothing to do with drawing monospace text on a grid. Adopting it to delete 27,700 lines of scoped third-party code would replace it with a far larger, far less scoped dependency graph. |
| `srwiley/oksvg` + `srwiley/rasterx` | No | **No — confirmed unsupported.** oksvg is a path-only icon rasterizer; `<text>` is a documented gap, not a bug. | BSD-3-Clause | **Stale.** oksvg last pushed 2023, rasterx last pushed 2022 — ~3 years untouched. | Light, but irrelevant — it can't render our SVG at all since our SVG is essentially all `<text>`. |
| resvg via WASM + `wazero` (`kanrichan/resvg-go`) | No — `wazero` is genuinely zero-dependency pure Go, no CGO | Yes, and specifically supports `textLength`/`lengthAdjust` (added upstream in resvg 0.27.0, 2022) — the exact mechanism our SVG relies on for monospace-grid alignment | **GPL-3.0** (confirmed via GitHub's license field on the repo) vs. oh-my-posh's **MIT** | Not abandoned (last commit Jan 2026) but thin: 50 stars, 27 commits, effectively one maintainer (commit messages in Chinese) | Bundles a ~783 KB gzipped (roughly 2–3 MB decompressed) precompiled `resvg.wasm` blob baked into the Go module via `go:embed`. |

**resvg is the one real licensing blocker here.** Upstream resvg itself is fine — it was re-licensed to Apache-2.0/MIT under Linebender stewardship after RazrFalcon stepped back — but the only ready-made Go wrapper (`kanrichan/resvg-go`) declares **GPL-3.0** for its own code. Statically embedding a GPL-3.0 package into an MIT binary that's distributed via Homebrew/winget/scoop/apt is a real compatibility problem: either the combined binary gets relicensed GPL-3.0 (a cost nobody's signed up for) or this specific wrapper can't be used. The workaround — compile resvg's own Apache/MIT Rust source to `wasm32-wasi` yourself and drive it through `wazero` directly, skipping the GPL wrapper — is not "add a library," it's "become the maintainer of a Rust→WASM SVG toolchain," a materially larger and open-ended commitment than the original framing implies.

**So: your instinct (resvg) is the right rasterizer technically, but the concrete path to it (the only existing Go binding) is GPL-3.0-encumbered, and the alternative is building your own binding.** Say this to the user plainly rather than quietly picking a different design.

### 3. What our SVG actually needs (read the full 333-line `src/svg/svg.go`)

Confirmed narrow feature set, nothing more:
- One `<svg>` root (width/height/viewBox), one `<style>` block setting `font-family`/`font-size`/`dominant-baseline: hanging`/`white-space: pre` on all `<text>`, plus `.omp-blink { animation: omp-blink 1s steps(1,end) infinite }` / `@keyframes` for blink (`svg.go:124-134`).
- `<rect>` elements: `x`/`y`/`width`/`height`/`fill` only — no stroke, no rx, no gradients (`writeRect`, `svg.go:174-186`).
- `<text>` elements: `x`/`y`, `textLength`+`lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"` (pins every run to an exact monospace cell width regardless of the renderer's own font metrics — `svg.go:188-228`), optional `fill`, `font-weight="bold"`, `font-style="italic"`, `text-decoration` (underline/overline/line-through, combinable), `opacity="0.6"` for dim, `class="omp-blink"`.
- No paths, gradients, patterns, transforms, groups, clipping, images, `<use>`/`<defs>`.

This is a genuinely narrow target. A general-purpose SVG/CSS engine is overkill in every direction: none of oksvg/rasterx's icon-path machinery applies, none of canvas's PDF/geo/plot/audio-codec baggage applies, and even resvg's animation support is moot for a PNG (a single static frame — the blink CSS simply never needs to progress).

### 4. Driving the existing `gg` pipeline from `[]terminal.Run` instead

Read `src/cli/image/image.go` end to end (920 lines) and `src/terminal/run.go`. Rough split:

**Pure ANSI-parsing, deleted outright if driven by the Run stream** (~455 lines):
- `NewRGBColor` (~11) — parses `"r;g;b"` capture groups
- `ansiSequenceRegexMap` literal, `image.go:185-208` (~24)
- `doubleWidthRunes` table + `runeAdditionalWidth`, `image.go:324-372` (~48) — the hand-maintained double-width table you asked about
- `cleanContent`, `image.go:374-401` (~28)
- `buildLayout`, `image.go:449-528` (~101) — the broken layout walk, drives `processAnsiSequence` in a loop
- `fitRow`/`longestPaddingRun`/`wrapRow`, `image.go:539-620` (~91) — **this whole block is redundant with the Run stream**: `svg.go`'s own doc comment confirms `prompt.Engine.CapturedRuns()` already returns rows pre-fit to terminal width (`svg.go:66-68`), so a Run-stream-driven PNG path never needs to re-wrap.
- `processAnsiSequence`, `image.go:767-820` (~54)
- `setBase16Color`/`colorNameFromCode`, `image.go:822-920` (~98)

**Kept and adapted (actual drawing)** (~230 lines): `loadFonts`/`loadDefaultFonts`/`fontHeight` (~95) and `SavePNG`'s `gg` canvas work — rounded rect, `stackblur` shadow, traffic-light circles, then the per-glyph `dc.SetFontFace`/`dc.DrawRectangle`/`dc.DrawString`/`dc.DrawLine` loop (`image.go:631-765`, ~135 lines). That inner loop would be reworked to iterate `[]terminal.Run` (one `DrawString` call per run instead of per rune — simpler and fewer draw calls, since runs already batch same-style spans) rather than a hand-rolled `glyphPlan`.

**This would delete the bugs you named, and the code confirms exactly why each one exists:**
- **256-colour blindness**: `ansiSequenceRegexMap` only has patterns for true-colour (`38;2;r;g;b`/`48;2;r;g;b`) and the 16 legacy SGR codes (30-37/40-47/90-97/100-107 via `color16`) — there is no `38;5;N`/`48;5;N` (8-bit 256-colour) pattern anywhere in the map, so any such sequence just isn't recognized. `terminal.Run.ForegroundRGB`/`BackgroundRGB` (`run.go:55-56`) already carry the fully-resolved RGB regardless of the source depth — this class of bug can't recur.
- **Single-attribute limit**: `ir.style` is one string field; `processAnsiSequence`'s `case bold, italic, underline, overline: ir.style = sequence` (`image.go:803-808`) means setting one always overwrites another — bold+underline simultaneously is structurally impossible today. `terminal.Run.Attributes` is `[8]uint8`, one independent slot per attribute (`run.go:64`, mirrored in `svg.go:234-243`) — already fixed in the SVG path, would be inherited here for free.
- **Dropped hyperlinks**: the `link` case in `processAnsiSequence` (`image.go:814-816`) reinjects only the visible text (`match[text]`) and discards the OSC-8 URL entirely. The Run model at least carries the concept (`run.go:51-53`'s doc on zero-`Cells` runs for hyperlink URL text) — though a raster PNG has nowhere to put a clickable link either way, this is moot for PNG specifically but stops the parser from mangling the visible text.
- **Hand-maintained double-width table**: `doubleWidthRunes` (39 lines) + `runeAdditionalWidth` (9 lines) exist only because the ANSI parser has to guess glyph width from Unicode ranges. `terminal.Run.Cells` is already the authoritative per-run width computed once, centrally, by the same logic the ANSI writer and SVG encoder both already trust (`svg.go:69-74` — this is literally called out as the problem the SVG's `textLength` mechanism was built to avoid).

### 5. Font handling per option

- **Today** (`image.go:236-246`): downloads Hack Nerd Font v3.2.1 from GitHub at runtime, caches it under `cache.Path()/Hack.zip`, fails with a `ConnectionError` if offline and uncached.
- **tdewolff/canvas**: still needs font bytes handed to it explicitly (it embeds/subsets whatever font you give it) — same runtime-fetch-or-bundle problem, no improvement.
- **oksvg/rasterx**: moot — it can't render `<text>` at all.
- **resvg-go**: needs fonts loaded through its own `FontDB` API (`LoadFontData`) — same "someone still has to feed it the Nerd Font bytes" problem as today, just a different API surface.
- **Option 4 (Run-stream + kept `gg`)**: unchanged from today — `loadFonts`/`loadDefaultFonts` (`image.go:147-308`) are kept verbatim; this path fixes zero font-provisioning problems but also introduces zero new ones.

None of the four options make the font-fetch problem better or worse in a meaningful way; it's an orthogonal concern to the rasterizer choice.

## Recommendation

**Go with option 4: keep `gg`, delete the ANSI re-parsing, drive drawing from `[]terminal.Run` directly.** Evidence:

1. Your own stated preference (resvg) is technically the best-fitting rasterizer — it supports exactly the `textLength`/`lengthAdjust` mechanism the SVG relies on — but the only real Go binding is GPL-3.0, incompatible with this MIT project, and rolling your own binding is a large, open-ended commitment (own a Rust build step, a wasm32 target, a font/glyph FFI boundary) far beyond "swap in a rasterizer."
2. `oksvg`/`rasterx` can't render `<text>` at all — disqualified outright, independent of its ~3-year-stale maintenance.
3. `tdewolff/canvas` is well-maintained and MIT, but adopting it would replace 27,700 lines of scoped third-party code with a dependency graph that drags in two GUI toolkits, OpenGL bindings, a plotting library, a MySQL driver, geo/projection libraries, and PDF/LaTeX renderers — directly opposed to the stated goal, and its SVG-reading path (as opposed to its Go-API drawing path) is the least mature part of the library.
4. Option 4 deletes essentially all four named bugs (evidenced above, tied to specific line ranges) by removing the ANSI regex parser (~455 of 920 lines) and keeping the ~230 lines of `gg` drawing that already work, fed from the same `[]terminal.Run` the SVG encoder already trusts — zero new dependencies, zero licensing questions, and the two output formats (`svg`/`png`) end up sharing one data source instead of one correct encoder and one broken parser.

Files read (no changes made): `D:\oh-my-posh\src\go.mod`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\.goreleaser.yml`, `D:\oh-my-posh\.github\workflows\code.yml`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\svg\svg.go`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\cli\image\image.go`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\cli\config_export_image.go`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\cli\config_export_svg.go`, `D:\oh-my-posh\src\terminal\run.go`.

- **256-colour blindness**: `ansiSequenceRegexMap` only has patterns for true-colour (`38;2;r;g;b`/`48;2;r;g;b`) and the 16 legacy SGR codes (30-37/40-47/90-97/100-107 via `color16`) — there is no `38;5;N`/`48;5;N` (8-bit 256-colour) pattern anywhere in the map, so any such sequence just isn't recognized. `terminal.Run.ForegroundRGB`/`BackgroundRGB` (`run.go:55-56`) already carry the fully-resolved RGB regardless of the source depth — this class of bug can't recur.
- **Single-attribute limit**: `ir.style` is one string field; `processAnsiSequence`'s `case bold, italic, underline, overline: ir.style = sequence` (`image.go:803-808`) means setting one always overwrites another — bold+underline simultaneously is structurally impossible today. `terminal.Run.Attributes` is `[8]uint8`, one independent slot per attribute (`run.go:64`, mirrored in `svg.go:234-243`) — already fixed in the SVG path, would be inherited here for free.
- **Dropped hyperlinks**: the `link` case in `processAnsiSequence` (`image.go:814-816`) reinjects only the visible text (`match[text]`) and discards the OSC-8 URL entirely. The Run model at least carries the concept (`run.go:51-53`'s doc on zero-`Cells` runs for hyperlink URL text) — though a raster PNG has nowhere to put a clickable link either way, this is moot for PNG specifically but stops the parser from mangling the visible text.
- **Hand-maintained double-width table**: `doubleWidthRunes` (39 lines) + `runeAdditionalWidth` (9 lines) exist only because the ANSI parser has to guess glyph width from Unicode ranges. `terminal.Run.Cells` is already the authoritative per-run width computed once, centrally, by the same logic the ANSI writer and SVG encoder both already trust (`svg.go:69-74` — this is literally called out as the problem the SVG's `textLength` mechanism was built to avoid).

### 5. Font handling per option

- **Today** (`image.go:236-246`): downloads Hack Nerd Font v3.2.1 from GitHub at runtime, caches it under `cache.Path()/Hack.zip`, fails with a `ConnectionError` if offline and uncached.
- **tdewolff/canvas**: still needs font bytes handed to it explicitly (it embeds/subsets whatever font you give it) — same runtime-fetch-or-bundle problem, no improvement.
- **oksvg/rasterx**: moot — it can't render `<text>` at all.
- **resvg-go**: needs fonts loaded through its own `FontDB` API (`LoadFontData`) — same "someone still has to feed it the Nerd Font bytes" problem as today, just a different API surface.
- **Option 4 (Run-stream + kept `gg`)**: unchanged from today — `loadFonts`/`loadDefaultFonts` (`image.go:147-308`) are kept verbatim; this path fixes zero font-provisioning problems but also introduces zero new ones.

None of the four options make the font-fetch problem better or worse in a meaningful way; it's an orthogonal concern to the rasterizer choice.

## Recommendation

**Go with option 4: keep `gg`, delete the ANSI re-parsing, drive drawing from `[]terminal.Run` directly.** Evidence:

1. Your own stated preference (resvg) is technically the best-fitting rasterizer — it supports exactly the `textLength`/`lengthAdjust` mechanism the SVG relies on — but the only real Go binding is GPL-3.0, incompatible with this MIT project, and rolling your own binding is a large, open-ended commitment (own a Rust build step, a wasm32 target, a font/glyph FFI boundary) far beyond "swap in a rasterizer."
2. `oksvg`/`rasterx` can't render `<text>` at all — disqualified outright, independent of its ~3-year-stale maintenance.
3. `tdewolff/canvas` is well-maintained and MIT, but adopting it would replace 27,700 lines of scoped third-party code with a dependency graph that drags in two GUI toolkits, OpenGL bindings, a plotting library, a MySQL driver, geo/projection libraries, and PDF/LaTeX renderers — directly opposed to the stated goal, and its SVG-reading path (as opposed to its Go-API drawing path) is the least mature part of the library.
4. Option 4 deletes essentially all four named bugs (evidenced above, tied to specific line ranges) by removing the ANSI regex parser (~455 of 920 lines) and keeping the ~230 lines of `gg` drawing that already work, fed from the same `[]terminal.Run` the SVG encoder already trusts — zero new dependencies, zero licensing questions, and the two output formats (`svg`/`png`) end up sharing one data source instead of one correct encoder and one broken parser.

content.text:
Confirmed: `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-extldflags "-static"`, cross-compiled for four OSes × three arches from a single job. **resvg can't work here the way you'd want.**

- **CGO binding** — breaks the cross-compile model outright; the project has explicitly committed to static pure-Go builds.
- **WASM via wazero** — technically fine, pure Go, and resvg supports the exact `textLength`/`lengthAdjust` mechanism our SVG depends on. But the only existing Go binding, `kanrichan/resvg-go`, is **GPL-3.0**, and oh-my-posh is MIT distributed through Homebrew, winget and scoop. Statically embedding it would either relicense the binary or isn't permissible. Compiling resvg's own Apache/MIT Rust source to `wasm32-wasi` yourself avoids that, but means owning a Rust→WASM toolchain.
- **oksvg/rasterx** — cannot render `<text>` at all. Our SVG is essentially all text.
- **tdewolff/canvas** — MIT and maintained, but its dependency graph pulls in two GUI toolkits, OpenGL bindings, gonum/plot, a MySQL driver and geo libraries. Deleting 27,700 scoped lines to add that is backwards.

**The realistic alternative** is to keep `gg` but feed it the run stream instead of parsed ANSI. That deletes ~455 of `image.go`'s 920 lines — the entire regex parser, the layout walk, the re-wrapping (redundant, since runs already arrive fit to width), and the hand-maintained double-width table — and kills all four bugs, because `Run` already carries resolved RGB, independent attribute slots, and authoritative cell widths.

But I want to be explicit about the cost, since it differs from what you chose: **it does not delete the 27,700 lines of `gg`/`freetype`/`x-image`.** Those stay.

content.thinking: Font subsetting means taking a massive font file like a Nerd Font that contains thousands of glyphs and extracting only the specific characters your design actually uses, then embedding that smaller file directly into the SVG as a data URI so it renders without needing an external font file.

content.text: A font file contains every glyph the font ships — a Nerd Font is on the order of ten thousand, because it merges several icon sets into a normal typeface. That's why the file is megabytes. Any one theme uses almost none of them. Measured earlier on this repo: | | glyphs | |---|---| | all 124 themes combined | 246 | | night-owl (the busiest) | 51 | | a typical theme | a handful | Subsetting means building a new, small font file containing only the glyphs actually used, and dropping the rest. A 51-glyph subset is a few kilobytes instead of a few megabytes. **Why it matters here.** The SVG currently says "draw this in CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font" and relies on the viewer having it installed. Someone browsing the themes gallery to decide whether to try oh-my-posh hasn't installed anything yet, so they'd see tofu boxes where the icons should be — on the exact page meant to sell them the tool. Embedding a subset directly inside the SVG file, as a data URI, removes that dependency. The image carries its own glyphs and renders identically everywhere. It works even in an `` tag because the font is *in* the file — no network fetch, which is the thing that isolation blocks. The cost is bytes. A theme SVG is ~2.6 KB today; a subset would add a few KB. Still an order of magnitude smaller than the 60 KB PNG it replaces, and sharp at any zoom. The catch — and the reason I was mid-investigation when you asked — is that Go has no obvious pure-Go font subsetter. `ConradIrwin/font` is already a dependency but appears to only parse and write whole fonts, not subset them. So the real question is whether this is a small job or a "write a TrueType table serialiser" job, and I'd rather find that out before promising it.

import glob
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from fontinfo import cmap_codepoints, read_font  # noqa: E402

repo = sys.argv[1]
font = sys.argv[2]

data, tables = read_font(font)
covered = cmap_codepoints(data, tables)

ESC = re.compile(r"\\u([eEfF][0-9a-fA-F]{3})|\\U000([fF][0-9a-fA-F]{4})")


def is_pua(cp):
    return 0xE000 <= cp <= 0xF8FF or 0xF0000 <= cp <= 0xFFFFD


used = set()
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(repo, "themes", "*.omp.*")):
    raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    for ch in raw:
        if is_pua(ord(ch)):
            used.add(ord(ch))
    for m in ESC.finditer(raw):
        cp = int((m.group(1) or m.group(2)), 16)
        if is_pua(cp):
            used.add(cp)

missing = sorted(used - covered)
print("glyphs used by bundled themes:", len(used))
print("covered by the hosted font:", len(used) - len(missing))
print("MISSING:", len(missing))
if missing:
    print("  " + " ".join(f"U+{c:04X}" for c in missing[:20]))

`oh-my-posh config export image` historically produced a PNG by re-parsing the ANSI escape codes the prompt had already printed. An SVG exporter now draws from the prompt's own structured run stream instead (`src/svg/`, `--format svg`, commit 368839ff), and the website's theme gallery has been migrated to it (commit eb421824). The PNG path has no remaining consumer.

## Scope

**Delete:**
- `src/cli/image/` entirely — `image.go`, `config.go`, `fonts.go`, and their tests (~1,877 lines).
- The four dependencies that exist only for it: `github.com/fogleman/gg`, `github.com/esimov/stackblur-go`, `golang.org/x/image`, `github.com/golang/freetype`. **Rework `src/cli/config_export_image.go`:**

If you look at the generated SVGs, we can see that the glyphs are taking up a bigger place in height compared to the colored background, which makes a power line segment. For example, if you take the M365Princess, it is not aligned with what we have or had previously.

Also, the SVG rendering does not have a terminal-like background, which the images did have, which makes it more clean because we have a fixed length, fixed height, or at least fixed length. A visualization of how a theme or configuration is rendered when we use the image exporter. All of this is gone, and I would like to have that reintroduced.

Secondly, the dual code point glyphs, for which we initially had a map in the code base, that issue is still visible here because the glyphs are too large, so they start to overlap. You can see this easily when comparing one to the other, or at least the previous PNG on the website compared to what we created in SVG. There's a lot of overlap there.

Secondly, if we do an inverted coloring of a powerline glyph, we color the powerline and not the background, which is incorrect because that actively ruins the rendering. This happens, for example, in clean detailed, but also in cloud native azure. You can see this cobalt 2 as well. Everything that uses this makes it incorrect.

What I want to do is create a good list of these, pass that to fable, and have fable do the analysis of what we need to do to fix this. Can we have a PNG that was correct and an SVG that's rendered afterwards, and visually these two should be identical.

content.text:
All evidence is in hand. Here is the plan.

---

# Plan: SVG exporter parity with the retired PNG renderer

## Preliminary: the four defects re-counted

The framing is mostly right, with two corrections:

1. **Defect 1 is two distinct problems.** (a) An encoder bug: both "transparent" run modes paint the glyph and fill inverted. (b) A defect-2 symptom: `RunNormal` runs with a genuinely transparent background (leading/trailing diamonds, final powerline caps) *correctly* have no rect — they only look broken because there is no canvas background behind them. Evidence: in `M365Princess.svg` every powerline→powerline separator **already emits a correct rect** (`<rect fill="#da627d"/>` + triangle `fill="#9a348e"` — previous color over next background). The "no rect" cases are exclusively the transparent-mode runs. The maintainer's three named themes (clean-detailed, cloud-native-azure, cobalt2) are exactly the three whose configs use the `<transparent,…>` idiom; M365Princess (named only for defect 4) has no such run.
2. **Defect 3 is compression, not overlap, in Chromium/Firefox** — but a real fix must not rely on `textLength` for icons at all, because WebKit historically applies `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"` incompletely, where it degrades to genuine overlap. Details under defect 3.

Bonus wart while in there: coordinates like `x="140.79999999999998"` and `width="627.1999999999999"` (`formatFloat`, `src/svg/svg.go:351-353`) — round to 2 decimals.

## Defect 1 — transparent-mode runs are painted inverted

**What the writer actually emits.** For a run whose foreground is `transparent` (the `<transparent,background>\ue0b0</>` / `<transparent,#FEF5ED>\ue0b2</>` transition idiom):

- `RunReverseVideo` branch (`src/terminal/writer.go:1250-1259`): `writeTransparentStart` emits `\x1b[0m\x1b[<fg-code-of-segment-bg>;49m\x1b[7m` (`writer.go:137-138`). SGR 7 swaps channels: the **cell is filled with the segment background, and the glyph is painted in the terminal's default background** — a cutout.
- `RunBackgroundPainted` branch (`writer.go:1241-1249`): emits the terminal background as the *foreground* code (`Colors.ToAnsi(terminalBackground, false)`) and the segment background as the *background* code via the misleadingly-named `ToForeground()`, which actually rewrites `38;` → `48;` (`src/color/colors.go:168-174`). Same visual: **rect = segment bg, glyph = terminal bg.**
- The old PNG renderer confirms this: its `invertedColor` handler (`/tmp/omp-png/src/cli/image/image.go:776-779`) sets `foregroundColor = defaultBackgroundColor` (the window fill) and `backgroundColor = segment bg` — dark cutout glyph on a colored rect, visible in every reference PNG.

**What the encoder does instead** (`src/svg/svg.go:319-332`, `paintRun`):

- `RunReverseVideo`: `textRGB = state.bg`, `rectRGB = nil` — glyph painted **in the segment background with no rect**. Exactly inverted. This is the measured cobalt2/clean-detailed output.
- `RunBackgroundPainted`: `textRGB = state.bg`, `rectRGB = opts.TerminalBackground` — also inverted (glyph and fill swapped).

The doc comments on both `RunMode` constants (`src/terminal/run.go:28-37`) and in `paintRun` restate the same wrong reading ("the segment's background prints as the glyph color on top") — the comment misled the encoder. Fix the comments too.

**Fix** (encoder-local, ~10 lines):

```
RunBackgroundPainted:  rectRGB = state.bg;  textRGB = opts.TerminalBackground
RunReverseVideo:       rectRGB = state.bg;  textRGB = <canvas background>
```

For the glyph color when no terminal background is configured (`terminal.BackgroundColor` is empty for almost every theme, so runs capture as `RunReverseVideo` — `run.go:170-181`), use the canvas/window background from defect 2. Until defect 2 lands, hardcode the old default `#151515` as `Options` fallback.

**Tradeoff:** none. This is a faithful-emulation bug fix.

## Defect 2 — no chrome, shrink-wrapped canvas

**Current:** `Encode` sizes the canvas to `maxCells` (`src/svg/svg.go:99-126`) and emits at most a flat full-canvas rect when `TerminalBackground` is set (`svg.go:149-153`). `--terminal-width 120` already exists and *is* passed to the engine (`src/cli/config_export_image.go:68,117`) so alignment gaps are computed for 120 columns — but the width never reaches `svg.Options`, so the canvas shrink-wraps anyway. `exportSVG`/`svgOptions` (`src/cli/config_export_svg.go:19-57`) never see it.

**What the old renderer built** (`image.go:631-765`, `initDefaults` 164-208, all at `factor = 2.0`):

- fixed content width `columns × spaceAdvance` (120 cols), `margin 96`, `padding 48`, `titleOffset 80`
- drop shadow: stackblur radius 32, offset (32, 32), color `#10101066`
- rounded window: corner radius 12, fill `#151515` default, stroke `#404040` width 2
- traffic lights: circles radius 18, spacing 50, colors `#ED655A`/`#E1C04C`/`#71BD47`
- content additions from `cleanContent` (`image.go:374-401`): cursor indicator appended to the prompt (the `_` in the PNGs), then `\n\n` + bold `ohmyposh.dev` watermark (+ ` by <author>`)
- row overflow policy (`fitRow`, `image.go:539-562`): collapse the longest ≥5-space padding run first, hard-wrap otherwise.

**Fix:**

1. Add `Columns int` to `svg.Options`; plumb `imageTerminalWidth` through `exportSVG`. Canvas content width = `Columns × CellWidth`, independent of content.
2. Emit the window as SVG primitives: `<rect rx>` fill + stroke, three `<circle>`s, and a shadow via `<filter><feDropShadow>` (native SVG equivalent of stackblur; supported by all evergreen browsers). Scale the old constants by `FontSize/48` (the PNG ran at a 48 px em: 3648 = 120×28-px advance + 2×96 + 2×48) so proportions match.
3. Cursor + watermark: append as extra captured rows in the encoder (or CLI) — a plain run row for the cursor, a bold `ohmyposh.dev` row. **Decision point for you:** pixel-parity with the reference PNGs requires both; the gallery may not want the watermark now that the page provides context. Default to parity.
4. Overflow: with the engine already rendering at `Columns`, rows should fit; port `fitRow`'s two-step policy anyway (gap runs are identifiable: colorless, all-space — `src/prompt/runs.go:117-123`) because defect 3's icon inflation will push exactly those rows over budget.

**Tradeoffs:** the gallery cards get window chrome inside whatever card styling `ThemeGallery` has — needs one visual pass on the website. The old per-theme `--background-color` override map was deleted from `export_themes.mjs` (line 42-47 comment) — themes that set `terminal_background` keep it via `svgOptions`; others get `#151515`, same as the old default.

## Defect 3 — double-width Nerd Font glyphs

**Root cause.** `Encode` pins every run to `Cells × CellWidth` with `textLength` + `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"` (`src/svg/svg.go:226-233`), and `Cells` comes from `go-runewidth`, which reports 1 for PUA icons. In the non-Mono Nerd Font stack the SVG declares (`svg.go:36`), those icons' natural advance is ~1.25 cells (measured 12 px vs 9.6). Per spec, `spacingAndGlyphs` scales glyph outlines, so Chromium/Firefox **compress the run to ~80%** — distortion, not overlap; the doc comment at `svg.go:70-75` explicitly (and wrongly) declares this the replacement for the old width table. WebKit's long-standing partial `textLength` support can instead leave the natural 12 px ink overhanging the slot — the overlap the maintainer perceives is real in that engine. Every mismatching glyph measured (`\uf408`, `\uf044`, `\ue62a`, `\ue266`, `\uf489`, `\u2665`, …) falls inside the old `doubleWidthRunes` table; the powerline separators (`\ue0b0-\ue0bf`, `\ue0b4`, `\ue0b6`) do not — matching the table's regression comment (`/tmp/omp-png/src/cli/image/image.go:347-351`): separator glyphs are designed to fill exactly one cell, and doubling them once pushed fitting lines across the wrap boundary. **Keep that exclusion.**

**Fix** (encoder-local):

1. Port `doubleWidthRunes` + `runeAdditionalWidth` (`image.go:330-372`) into `src/svg/`, comment included.
2. In `encodeRow`, split each run's text into spans: contiguous ordinary runes → one `<text>` with `textLength` pinned as today; each table rune → its own `<text>` allocated **2 cells, with no `textLength`/`lengthAdjust`**, left-aligned at its cell origin (exactly what `dc.DrawString` + doubled advance did, `image.go:497-509,744`). No `textLength` because pinning to 19.2 px would *stretch* a 12 px glyph 1.6× — the opposite distortion; letting it render naturally inside a 2-cell slot reproduces the PNG.
3. Row accounting: the extra cells shift everything rightward, so right-aligned rows now exceed `Columns` — reconcile via defect 2's ported `fitRow` (shrink the row's longest ≥5-cell gap run by the overflow, then hard-wrap).

**Rejected alternatives, stated:** asking the font for real advances is impossible — the SVG has no embedded font; advances belong to whatever font the *viewer* resolves. Switching the stack to `Nerd Font Mono` variants would make every icon exactly 1 cell and delete the problem — but icons render half-size and the output diverges from the accepted PNG look. Embedding the font as a data URI was already rejected for the inline gallery (124 SVGs per page).

**Real risk to flag:** the website renders these SVGs in **Victor Mono** (`website/export_themes.mjs:29`, `ThemeGallery/index.js:9-12`), not the default stack. If that patched font has single-width icons, 2-cell allocation leaves a visible right-gap per icon on the gallery. The fix must be eyeballed under Victor Mono before shipping; if it looks sparse there, the pragmatic compromise is making the extra-width table conditional on an `Options` knob the website exporter can disable.

## Defect 4 — glyphs fill the whole cell

**Root cause.** `LineHeight` defaults to `1.2 × FontSize` = 19.2 px (`svg.go:56-58`) and `writeText` anchors with `dominant-baseline="hanging"` at the rect's top edge (`svg.go:233`, y set in `encodeRow:187`). The maintainer's three named themes (clean-detailed, cloud-native-azure, cobalt2) are exactly the three whose configs use the `<transparent,…>` idiom; M365Princess (named only for defect 4) has no such run.
2. **Defect 3 is compression, not overlap, in Chromium/Firefox** — but a real fix must not rely on `textLength` for icons at all, because WebKit historically applies `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"` incompletely, where it degrades to genuine overlap. Details under defect 3.

content.text:
Verified — and the root cause is mine.

`writer.go` emits `\x1b[0m\x1b[<segment-bg>;49m\x1b[7m`. It sets the segment background *as a foreground code*, then **SGR 7 swaps them**. Final state: cell filled with the segment background, glyph painted in the terminal's default background — a cutout.

The doc comment in `run.go` describes the state *before* the swap. It's true of the bytes and wrong about the rendering. The SVG encoder faithfully implemented the comment, which is why the glyph gets the segment colour and the rect gets nothing.

That comment came from my Stage 3 brief. A wrong comment propagated into a wrong renderer one stage later.

## Fable's findings

**It corrected my framing twice.**

1. **Defect 1 is two problems, not one.** M365Princess's powerline→powerline separators *already emit correct rects* — previous colour over next background. The missing-rect cases are exclusively the transparent-mode runs, which is why the three broken themes you named are exactly the three using the `<transparent,…>` idiom. The rest looks broken only because there's no canvas behind it, which is defect 2.

2. **Defect 3 is compression, not overlap — in Chromium and Firefox.** `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"` squeezes those 12px glyphs into 10px. But WebKit implements `textLength` partially, where it degrades to *genuine* overlap. Both need fixing, and the fix must stop pinning `textLength` on icons at all.

**The most important answer: nothing upstream is missing.** All four are encoder- or CLI-local. `Run.Cells` is correct — a real terminal also treats those icons as one cell, which is why Mono font variants exist. Double-width is presentation, and belongs where the old renderer had it.

**Measured targets:** cell height should be ~1.375 em (backed out from the reference PNGs: 48px em, 66px rows), currently 1.2. Baseline at 0.75 × line height, which is what `image.go`'s `bgY` offset encoded.

**One risk it flagged that I'd have missed:** the website renders in Victor Mono, not the default stack. If that patched build has single-width icons, a 2-cell allocation leaves a gap per icon in the gallery. The fix has to be checked there, not just against the default.

One decision is yours before I start.

input.prompt:
Repo: D:\oh-my-posh. Go module root `src/`. Use absolute paths when changing directory.

Two related fixes to the SVG exporter (`src/svg/`). Both are encoder-local. A reference copy of the retired PNG renderer is readable at the git worktree `/tmp/omp-png` (`/tmp/omp-png/src/cli/image/image.go`) — consult it, it got these right.

Reference renders for comparison are in:
`C:\Users\jande\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--oh-my-posh\6c0a282a-886f-458d-a426-93d95104b4a6\scratchpad\compare\`
(`.png` from the old renderer, `.svg` from the current one, for `M365Princess`, `clean-detailed`, `cloud-native-azure`, `cobalt2`).

## Fix 1 — transparent runs are painted inverted

`src/terminal/writer.go:137-138` emits, for a transparent-foreground run:

```
transparentStartPrefix = "\x1b[0m\x1b["
transparentStartSuffix = ";49m\x1b[7m"
```

That sets the segment background **as a foreground code**, then SGR 7 **swaps** the channels. So the actual rendering is: **cell filled with the segment background, glyph painted in the terminal's default background** — a cutout. The old PNG renderer agrees: its `invertedColor` handler (`/tmp/omp-png/src/cli/image/image.go:776-779`) sets `foregroundColor = defaultBackgroundColor` and `backgroundColor = segment bg`.

`src/svg/svg.go` `paintRun` (around :319-332) does the inverse:
- `RunReverseVideo` → `textRGB = state.bg`, `rectRGB = nil`
- `RunBackgroundPainted` → `textRGB = state.bg`, `rectRGB = opts.TerminalBackground`

Both paint the glyph in the segment background and lose the fill. That is why powerline transitions look broken in `clean-detailed`, `cloud-native-azure` and `cobalt2` — those are the three themes whose configs use the `<transparent,…>` idiom.

Correct mapping:
- `RunBackgroundPainted` → `rectRGB = state.bg`, `textRGB = opts.TerminalBackground`
- `RunReverseVideo` → `rectRGB = state.bg`, `textRGB = <canvas background>`

`terminal.BackgroundColor` is empty for almost every theme, so most transparent runs capture as `RunReverseVideo`. Until the canvas/window background lands (a separate task), use the old renderer's default `#151515` as the fallback for the glyph colour, via an `Options` field so the next task can supply the real canvas colour.

**Also fix the comments that caused this.** `src/terminal/run.go:28-37` documents both modes as "the segment's background prints as a foreground code on top of it" — that describes the state BEFORE the SGR 7 swap, and the encoder implemented the comment rather than the rendering. Rewrite both comments to describe what is actually rendered. Leave the rest of `run.go` alone.

## Fix 2 — glyphs fill the entire cell height

`LineHeight` defaults to `1.2 × FontSize` = 19.2px (`src/svg/svg.go:56-58`) and text is anchored `dominant-baseline="hanging"` at the rect's top edge. A 16px line of CaskaydiaCove occupies ~19px of ink, so glyphs span the whole cell with zero leading and anything past the em box escapes its background rect. Measured: rect height 19.2, text bbox 19.0.

The old renderer used a cell of `fontHeight × 1.2` where `fontHeight` is the font's natural line height (ascent+descent, larger than the em), and placed the background rect at `baseline − 0.75 × lineHeight` (`/tmp/omp-png/src/cli/image/image.go:724-736`, with a comment about centring powerline glyphs). Backed out from the reference PNGs (48px em, 66px content rows) that is a cell of ≈1.375 em.

Change: default `LineHeight` to `1.4 × FontSize`, drop `dominant-baseline` entirely, and place the baseline at `y = rowTop + 0.75 × LineHeight` using the default alphabetic baseline. Rationale for dropping `hanging`: we have no font metrics server-side, and `hanging` baseline placement is inconsistently implemented across browsers; an alphabetic baseline at a computed offset is deterministic.

Note this changes every row's vertical geometry, so the canvas height changes too. Keep it consistent.

## While you are in there

`formatFloat` (`src/svg/svg.go:351-353`) emits coordinates like `x="140.79999999999998"` and `width="627.1999999999999"`. Round to 2 decimals.

## Constraints

- **124 theme goldens byte-identical**: `go test ./prompt/ -run TestGoldenThemes -count=1`. These are ANSI goldens; you are changing SVG only, so they must not move. If one does, you touched something you should not have.
- Existing `src/svg/` tests: update only where the output shape genuinely changed, and say which and why.
- Do not touch `src/terminal/writer.go` (only the comments in `run.go`).

## Verify before reporting

1. `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` clean.
2. 124 ANSI goldens byte-identical.
3. Regenerate the four comparison SVGs into the scratchpad `compare/` directory (build a binary; use `--data src/prompt/testdata/fixtures/prompt.data.json` for determinism) and **inspect the markup**: every transparent-mode run must now have a `<rect>` whose fill is the segment background, and a `<text>` whose fill is the canvas/terminal background.
4. Confirm no coordinate in the output has more than 2 decimal places.
5. `golangci-lint run ./...` clean.
6. Report the before/after markup for one transparent run in `cobalt2`, and the new canvas height for a single-row theme.

Report: the diff, the corrected comments, what changed in the four sample SVGs, and anything in this brief that turned out to be wrong.

First fix running. The plan, in Fable's ordering — riskiest last:

| | defect | why this position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | inverted transparency + wrong comments | smallest, unambiguous, unblocks the three broken themes |
| 2 | cell height & baseline | small; land before chrome so vertical maths is final and goldens churn once |
| 3 | terminal window, fixed 120-column canvas, cursor, watermark | medium; supplies the canvas colour defect 1 falls back to |
| 4 | double-width glyph table | **riskiest** — changes layout accounting, interacts with overflow collapse, depends on per-viewer font advances |

**On verification.** Fable was straight that pixel-identity isn't achievable in the strict sense — different rasterisers, `stackblur` versus `feDropShadow`, antialiasing — and isn't CI-able in pure Go for the reasons we already established. So it proposed two tiers, and I think that's the honest answer to your criterion:

- **Tier 1, in CI:** golden SVG files plus structural assertions parsed with `encoding/xml` — canvas dimensions constant across themes, every transparent run having a rect whose fill matches the segment background, per-row cell sums within the column budget, every baseline at the computed offset.
- **Tier 2, human-reviewed:** render the SVG headless in Chromium against the *exact same* `HackNerdFont-Regular.ttf` the PNG renderer used, screenshot at 3× to match the PNG's 48px em, then `pixelmatch` with diff heatmaps as artifacts.

That gives automated *comparison* with sign-off on the heatmaps, rather than automated *identity*.

The `/tmp/omp-png` worktree stays until this is done — it's how we generate reference PNGs, and it's the only remaining copy of the old renderer.

Repo: D:\oh-my-posh. Go module root `src/`. Use absolute paths when changing directory.

Final two fixes to the SVG exporter (`src/svg/`). A comparison harness now exists at `D:\oh-my-posh\tools\svg-png-compare\` — use it to judge your work. The retired PNG renderer is readable at the worktree `/tmp/omp-png` (`/tmp/omp-png/src/cli/image/image.go`).

cd D:\oh-my-posh\tools\svg-png-compare
npm install          # once

```
Current structural difference, which you are trying to reduce: M365Princess 10.36%, clean-detailed 7.84%, cloud-native-azure 14.20%, cobalt2 8.69%, jandedobbeleer 12.30%, atomic 9.79%.

## Fix A — the cell width ratio is wrong (do this first, it is exact)

`src/svg/svg.go:93` sets `CellWidth = FontSize * 0.6`. Hack Nerd Font's actual advance is **28/48 = 0.58333 em**, which is verifiable from the PNG renderer's own geometry: its canvas is 3648px = 120 columns × 28px advance + 2×96 margin + 2×48 padding, at a 48px em.

Consequence: every column is 2.9% too wide, so content drifts progressively rightward — 32px of accumulated error across 120 columns at a 16px em. The harness sees this as ghosting that widens toward the right of each row.

Change the default to `FontSize * 7.0 / 12.0`. This makes the canvas 1216 wide at 16px, and 3648/1216 = **exactly 3.0**, so the comparison rasterises at a clean 3× with no resampling slop.

**Important:** `CellWidth` is already an `Options` field. Keep it overridable, and document that the default matches Hack's advance ratio — because the website renders these in **Victor Mono**, whose ratio may differ. Do not hardcode the assumption anywhere else.

## Fix B — double-width Nerd Font glyphs

`Run.Cells` comes from `go-runewidth`, which reports 1 for Private Use Area icons. But in a non-Mono Nerd Font those glyphs are drawn ~1.25 cells wide. The encoder pins every run to `Cells × CellWidth` via `textLength` + `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"`, so those glyphs are **compressed to ~80%** — visibly narrower than the PNG, crowding the text after them. (In WebKit, which implements `textLength` partially, the same markup can instead overlap.)

The retired renderer solved this with a table: `doubleWidthRunes` plus `runeAdditionalWidth` (`/tmp/omp-png/src/cli/image/image.go:330-372`), allocating those codepoints two cells.

**Read that table's comment at :346-351 before you touch anything.** It records a regression: powerline separators (`\ue0b0`-`\ue0d4`) were once included and must not be — they are designed to fill exactly one cell, and doubling them pushed otherwise-fitting lines past the wrap boundary.

Implement:
1. Port the table and its comments into `src/svg/`.
2. In row encoding, split a run's text into spans: contiguous ordinary runes keep one `<text>` pinned with `textLength` as today; each table rune gets its own `<text>` allocated **2 cells with NO `textLength`/`lengthAdjust`**, left-aligned at its cell origin. No pinning, because forcing a 12px glyph into a 19.2px slot would stretch it 1.6× — the opposite distortion. Letting it draw naturally in a 2-cell slot is what the PNG did.
3. The extra cells shift rows rightward, so rows can now exceed the column budget. The overflow policy landed in commit `d0a42809` (`src/svg/fit.go`) — collapse the widest gap run first, then wrap. Make sure the two interact correctly.

- **124 ANSI goldens byte-identical**: `go test ./prompt/ -run TestGoldenThemes -count=1`.
- Existing `src/svg/` tests: update only where output genuinely changed, and say which and why.
- `golangci-lint run ./...` clean.

import struct
import sys


def tables(data):
    n = struct.unpack(">H", data[4:6])[0]
    t = {}
    for i in range(n):
        off = 12 + i * 16
        tag = data[off:off + 4].decode("latin-1")
        to, tl = struct.unpack(">II", data[off + 8:off + 16])
        t[tag] = (to, tl)
    return t


def cmap_lookup(data, t):
    off, _ = t["cmap"]
    n = struct.unpack(">H", data[off + 2:off + 4])[0]
    best = None
    for i in range(n):
        rec = off + 4 + i * 8
        pid, eid, sub = struct.unpack(">HHI", data[rec:rec + 8])
        if (pid, eid) in ((3, 10), (0, 4)):
            best = off + sub
            break
        if (pid, eid) in ((3, 1), (0, 3)) and best is None:
            best = off + sub
    m = {}
    fmt = struct.unpack(">H", data[best:best + 2])[0]
    if fmt == 4:
        segx2 = struct.unpack(">H", data[best + 6:best + 8])[0]
        seg = segx2 // 2
        def arr(o):
            return [struct.unpack(">H", data[o + i * 2:o + 2 + i * 2])[0] for i in range(seg)]
        ends = arr(best + 14)
        starts = arr(best + 16 + segx2)
        deltas = arr(best + 16 + segx2 * 2)
        ro_base = best + 16 + segx2 * 3
        ros = arr(ro_base)
        for i in range(seg):
            for c in range(starts[i], min(ends[i], 0xFFFF) + 1):
                if c == 0xFFFF:
                    continue
                if ros[i] == 0:
                    g = (c + deltas[i]) & 0xFFFF
                else:
                    p = ro_base + i * 2 + ros[i] + (c - starts[i]) * 2
                    if p + 2 > len(data):
                        continue
                    g = struct.unpack(">H", data[p:p + 2])[0]
                    if g:
                        g = (g + deltas[i]) & 0xFFFF
                if g:
                    m[c] = g
    elif fmt == 12:
        ng = struct.unpack(">I", data[best + 12:best + 16])[0]
        for i in range(ng):
            o = best + 16 + i * 12
            sc, ec, sg = struct.unpack(">III", data[o:o + 12])
            if ec - sc > 0x10000:
                continue
            for c in range(sc, ec + 1):
                m[c] = sg + (c - sc)
    return m

data = open(path, "rb").read()
t = tables(data)

upem = struct.unpack(">H", data[t["head"][0] + 18:t["head"][0] + 20])[0]

    return struct.unpack(">H", data[hmtx + (num_h - 1) * 4:hmtx + (num_h - 1) * 4 + 2])[0]

content.text:
This changes the diagnosis completely, and reverses two of my own commits.

**Both fonts advance every icon at exactly 1.000 cells. But their *ink* deliberately overflows:**

| glyph | ink / cell — Victor Mono | Hack |
|---|---|---|
| `M` (ASCII) | 0.832 | 0.859 |
| `` powerline | 1.060 | 1.060 |
| `` devicon | **1.833** | **1.661** |
| `` | 1.680 | 1.648 |
| `` | 1.600 | 1.450 |

Icons are *designed* to bleed past their advance box — that's how they look right in a terminal, which lets them spill into neighbouring cells. The PNG renderer drew them at natural size and let them bleed.

**So the real bug is `textLength` + `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"`.** It forces the ink into the advance width, squashing every icon to 55–70% of its designed size. That *is* your original complaint — the glyphs aren't too large, they're being crushed, and the crowding follows from it.

Three corrections to what I've committed:

1. **The double-width table is wrong and should be reverted.** No font in play draws icons at two cells. I ported it because `image.go` had it, without checking whether its premise still held.
2. **My cell-width "fix" made things worse.** I derived 28/48 = 0.58333 from the PNG canvas, but that 28 came from `MeasureString >> 6`, which *truncates* — the true value is 28.9. Hack's real ratio is 0.6021, so the original 0.6 was accurate to 0.35% and I replaced it with something 3.1% off. That's why the harness showed no improvement and two themes got marginally worse.
3. **`textLength` should be dropped entirely**, and runs positioned at grid origins with glyphs rendering at natural size — which is precisely what `dc.DrawString` did.

And to your question: **no font change is needed.** The font was never the problem. What Victor Mono *does* need is its own cell-width ratio — 0.5455 against Hack's 0.6021, a 10% difference — because run positions depend on it.

I'd rather verify that hypothesis before writing more code, since I've now been wrong twice in the same area.

import sys
import zlib
import struct


def read_png(path):
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    pos, w, h, idat = 8, 0, 0, b""
    while pos < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack(">I", data[pos:pos + 4])[0]
        typ = data[pos + 4:pos + 8]
        body = data[pos + 8:pos + 8 + ln]
        if typ == b"IHDR":
            w, h, depth, ctype = struct.unpack(">IIBB", body[:10])
        elif typ == b"IDAT":
            idat += body
        pos += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = {0: 1, 2: 3, 4: 2, 6: 4}[ctype]
    stride = w * bpp
    out = bytearray(h * stride)
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    p = 0
    for y in range(h):
        f = raw[p]
        p += 1
        line = bytearray(raw[p:p + stride])
        p += stride
        for i in range(stride):
            a = line[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
            b = prev[i]
            c = prev[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
            if f == 1:
                line[i] = (line[i] + a) & 255
            elif f == 2:
                line[i] = (line[i] + b) & 255
            elif f == 3:
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a + b) // 2) & 255
            elif f == 4:
                pa, pb, pc = abs(b - c), abs(a - c), abs(a + b - 2 * c)
                pr = a if (pa <= pb and pa <= pc) else (b if pb <= pc else c)
                line[i] = (line[i] + pr) & 255
        out[y * stride:(y + 1) * stride] = line
        prev = line
    return w, h, bpp, bytes(out)


def profile(path):
    w, h, bpp, px = read_png(path)
    rows = []
    for y in range(h):
        base = y * w * bpp
        ink = 0
        for x in range(0, w, 4):
            i = base + x * bpp
            if bpp >= 3:
                r, g, b = px[i], px[i + 1], px[i + 2]
                a = px[i + 3] if bpp == 4 else 255
                if a > 40 and (r + g + b) > 90:
                    ink += 1
        rows.append(ink)
    return w, h, rows


for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    w, h, rows = profile(path)
    peak = max(rows) if rows else 0
    active = [i for i, v in enumerate(rows) if v > peak * 0.25]
    name = path.split("\\")[-1].split("/")[-1]
    if active:
        print(f"{name:34} {w}x{h}  content rows {active[0]}..{active[-1]}  (span {active[-1] - active[0]})")
    else:
        print(f"{name:34} {w}x{h}  no content detected")

I'm seeing the font metrics now — Hack Nerd Font has a line height of 1.1641 em while Victor Mono NF is 1.4091 em, and our SVG is using 1.4 which matches Victor Mono almost perfectly but is way off from Hack. Since the PNG was rendered with Hack, its row height would've been calculated differently based on the line spacing value, so I need to track down what that line spacing actually was in the image.

Looking at the pixel measurements, the PNG content spans 441 pixels across 3 rows while the SVG spans 422 pixels — but this discrepancy isn't just about row height, it's about the starting offset and baseline positioning within each row. The math gets tricky because the span includes both the inked content and the blank rows between them, so I need to work backwards from the total span to figure out the actual row height and ink height separately.

Let me recalculate using the cobalt2 SVG as a reference: the total height of 189.87 em breaks down into margins, padding, a title offset, and then the actual content rows. If I subtract the chrome (margins and padding) and the title offset, I can solve for the per-row line height. At 48px em for both the PNG and SVG, the PNG's 632 pixels should follow the same structure — margins, padding, title offset, then rows — which gives me 88 pixels per row.

But wait, that's 1.833 em per row, which seems too large compared to the SVG's 1.4 em. Let me reconsider the scaling: if the factor is 2.0, then at 48px em, the margins would be 96, padding 48, and title offset 80. That leaves 264 pixels for content rows. If there are actually 4 rows instead of 3, then each row is 66 pixels, which is closer to 1.375 em — much more reasonable. So the PNG likely contains 4 rows: the content, a blank line, possibly another blank, and the watermark. The row count mismatch is the key — the PNG has four content rows while ours has three, which accounts for the missing blank line before the watermark. Looking at the metrics, the PNG uses Hack's line height (1.1641) multiplied by a 1.2 spacing factor to get 1.375 em per row, whereas we're using a fixed 1.4 em that happens to match Victor Mono instead. The solution is to make row height derivable from font metrics as an option, similar to how cell width works, rather than hardcoding it.

Now it's exact, and it explains everything.

| font | real line height |
|---|---|
| **Hack** (what the PNG used) | **1.1641 em** |
| **Victor Mono** (what the site uses) | **1.4091 em** |
| our hardcoded constant | **1.4** |

I reverse-engineered 1.4 from reference images and landed almost exactly on **Victor Mono's** metric — while the reference PNGs were rendered in **Hack**. It was fitted to the wrong font by coincidence.

And the canvas arithmetic shows a second error. At a 48px em the PNG is `632 = 192 margin + 96 padding + 80 title + 264 rows`, and 264 ÷ 66 = **4 rows**. Ours emits **3**. The PNG's `cleanContent` appends two newlines before the watermark; we append one. That's most of the 26px offset and all of the 19px span difference.

So the vertical story is three separate things, none of which is a guess any more:

- **row count** — we're one blank row short
- **line height** — should be the font's `ascent − descent + lineGap` × 1.2, which for Hack is 1.397 em, not a fixed 1.4
- **it's font-specific** — 1.1641 vs 1.4091 is a 21% difference, so like `CellWidth` it has to be an `Options` input, since Go can't know what font a viewer resolves

The measurement instrument matters too: the harness's aggregate percentage **cannot see any of this** — it stayed at 8.7% across all three of my horizontal attempts. The row profile found it in one shot. For the fix, that profile is the gate, not the diff percentage.

Two of my own commits to `src/svg/` were based on premises that direct measurement of the font files has now contradicted. Revert them and replace with values derived from real font metrics. ## The measurements that overturn the current code

I read the actual TTF tables for both fonts in play.

**Advances — every icon is exactly ONE cell in both fonts:**
```
Hack Nerd Font    units/em 2048  ASCII 'M' advance 1233 (0.6021 em)
Victor Mono NF    units/em 1100  ASCII 'M' advance  600 (0.5455 em)

```

**But glyph INK overflows its advance, by design:**
```
glyph        ink/cell VictorMono   ink/cell Hack
M (ASCII)         0.832               0.859
U+E0B0            1.060               1.060
U+F408            1.833               1.661
U+F044            1.680               1.648
U+E62A            1.600               1.450
```

**Line heights (hhea ascender − descender + lineGap):**
```
Hack Nerd Font    2384/2048 = 1.1641 em
Victor Mono NF    1550/1100 = 1.4091 em
```

1. **The double-width table** — `src/svg/doublewidth.go`, `doublewidth_test.go`, and its use in `svg.go`/`fit.go`. Its premise was that icons occupy 2 cells. They occupy 1 in both fonts. `Run.Cells` was already correct. Icons render wider than their cell because their *ink* overflows, which is intended and which terminals allow — that is not something to compensate for with extra cells.

2. **The `CellWidth` default** — currently `FontSize * 7.0/12.0` (0.58333), which I derived from the PNG canvas arithmetic. That 28px advance came from `MeasureString(" ") >> 6`, which **truncates**: Hack's true advance at a 48px em is 28.9px. So my "exact" derivation encoded the old renderer's truncation bug.

Keep `fit.go`'s overflow policy — it is still correct and useful; just stop budgeting against a double-width table.

## What to fix

3. **A missing row.** Canvas arithmetic on the reference PNG at a 48px em: `632 = 192 margin + 96 padding + 80 title + 264 rows`, and 264/66 = **4 rows**. We emit **3**. `cleanContent` in the old renderer (`image.go` ~:374-401) appends TWO newlines before the `ohmyposh.dev` watermark; our `decorate.go` appends one. This accounts for most of a measured 26px vertical offset and all of a 19px span difference.

4. **Line height must come from font metrics, not a constant.** `LineHeight` currently defaults to `FontSize * 1.4`, which I reverse-engineered from reference images — and which happens to match **Victor Mono's** 1.4091 while the reference PNGs were rendered in **Hack** (1.1641).    The old renderer used `regular.Metrics().Height * lineSpacing` (`image.go:310-312`, and see where `lineSpacing` is set). Find that multiplier. For Hack: 1.1641 × 1.2 = 1.397 em.

5. **Both `CellWidth` and `LineHeight` are font properties**, differing by 10% and 21% respectively between the two fonts. They must be `Options` inputs (`CellWidth` already is). Revert-and-derive is running.

**The measurements that settle it**, read straight from the TTF tables rather than inferred:

| | Hack (PNG reference) | Victor Mono (site) |
|---|---|---|

Three of my fixes were wrong for the same reason — I inferred font geometry from rendered images instead of reading the font:

- The double-width table assumed icons occupy two cells. They occupy one. What overflows is the *ink*, up to 1.83× the cell, deliberately, and terminals let it bleed.
- The cell width "correction" encoded the old renderer's `>> 6` truncation bug. The original 0.6 was accurate to 0.35%; I made it 3.1% wrong.

**And the instrument was the deeper problem.** The harness's structural percentage sat at ~8.7% across all three attempts — it force-fits the SVG into the PNG's dimensions, so it cannot see horizontal layout at all. A per-row ink profile found the real error, which is vertical, in one shot: content sitting 26px low and spanning 19px short, because we emit three rows where the PNG emits four.

I've written that up to memory, because the pattern is more valuable than the fix: *before compensating for font behaviour, read the font* — it's about 60 lines of `struct.unpack` — and pick an instrument that can actually see the thing you're changing.

One open question I've explicitly handed to the implementer rather than decided: whether the defaults should be the fonts' **true** metrics or the **truncated** values the PNG actually laid out with. True metrics are correct; truncated ones match the reference. I've asked for numbers and a recommendation, not a silent pick.

import sys

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[-1])
from rowprofile import read_png  # noqa: E402


def analyse(path):
    w, h, bpp, px = read_png(path)

    first_opaque = None
    first_colour = None
    last_colour = None

    for y in range(h):
        base = y * w * bpp
        opaque = 0
        colour = 0
        for x in range(0, w, 3):
            i = base + x * bpp
            r, g, b = px[i], px[i + 1], px[i + 2]
            a = px[i + 3] if bpp == 4 else 255
            if a < 40:
                continue
            opaque += 1
            mx, mn = max(r, g, b), min(r, g, b)
            # Saturated or bright => prompt content, not the dark window fill.
            if (mx - mn) > 45 or mx > 150:
                colour += 1
        if opaque > w // 20 and first_opaque is None:
            first_opaque = y
        if colour > 12:
            if first_colour is None:
                first_colour = y
            last_colour = y

    return {
        "size": f"{w}x{h}",
        "window_top": first_opaque,
        "text_top": first_colour,
        "text_bottom": last_colour,
        "text_span": (last_colour - first_colour) if first_colour is not None else None,
    }


for p in sys.argv[1:-1]:
    name = p.replace("\\", "/").split("/")[-1]
    r = analyse(p)
    print(
        f"{name:28} {r['size']:10} window_top={r['window_top']}  "
        f"text {r['text_top']}..{r['text_bottom']} (span {r['text_span']})"
    )

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

**Original (this session):** Implement Proposal B's faceted segment catalog, and fix homepage rhythm/card regressions from Phase 1.

**Then, sequentially authorized phases:**
- Phase 2.0 — golden-file harness + hermetic `--data` replay
- Phase 2.1 — collapse three duplicated tokenizers in `terminal/writer.go`
- Phase 2.2 — runs as an intermediate representation; SVG encoder
- Gallery migration to inline SVG
- PNG exporter deletion
- SVG rendering defect fixes (4 defects the user found by inspecting output)

**FINAL PIVOT (from compact instructions — this supersedes in-flight work):**
> "keep the website redesign guidelines, and I want to continue from there. Park all of the changes we did for SVG on a separate branch. Keep it there. Let's start fresh from a brand new main forked branch. What I want to do is understand if we can use the PNG functionality, put that behind an API endpoint, and return PNGs to create a studio in a way."

So: (a) preserve website redesign direction, (b) park all SVG work on a branch, (c) fork fresh from `main`, (d) investigate PNG-behind-an-API-endpoint to power a studio.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Docusaurus 3.10.2** (ESM config), Infima CSS, plugin `loadContent`/`contentLoaded`/`setGlobalData`, route-scoped data via static import + webpack per-route chunking, `usePluginData`, `useIsBrowser`, SSR via `<StaticRouter location={pathname}>` (pathname only, **no query string**)
- **Go**: `src/terminal/writer.go` (prompt hot path, 28 package globals), `src/prompt/engine.go`, `src/config/segment.go`, `src/svg/`, deleted `src/cli/image/`
- **Build posture**: `src/.goreleaser.yml` sets `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-extldflags "-static"`, cross-compiles 4 OS × 3 arch from ONE job. **CGO is a non-starter.**
- **Font metrics**: TTF `head` (unitsPerEm @+18), `hhea` (ascender/descender/lineGap @+4), `hmtx` (advances), `cmap` format 4/12, `glyf` bbox for ink width
- **Azure Static Web Apps** deploy with `app_location: "/website"`; `website/api/` holds existing Azure Functions (`website/api/auth/index.js`, `website/api/mcp/index.js`)

## 3. Files and Code Sections

### Website redesign (KEEP — user explicitly wants these guidelines preserved)
- **`website/src/pages/index.js`** + **`styles.module.css`** — hero left-aligned, `gap: 1.1rem`, `.heroTitle{max-width:20ch}`, `.subtitle{max-width:52ch}`, `.heroImageWrapper{background:#173448;border-radius:9px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;max-width:100%}`, feature `.card` with theme-split fill:
  ```css
  .card { background: var(--ifm-color-emphasis-100); border: 1px solid var(--ifm-color-emphasis-200); border-radius: 9px; padding: 1.15rem 1.25rem; height: 100%; }
  [data-theme='dark'] .card { background: var(--ifm-background-surface-color); }
  ```
- **`website/src/components/SegmentCatalog/`** + **`website/src/pages/segments.js`** + **`website/plugins/segments/`** — faceted catalog, 117 segments, facets = Group (8) / Setup (4 auth tiers) / Display (Nerd Font, 28). URL state `?group=cli,cloud&auth=oauth&nerdfont=1&q=kube` via `history.replace`.
- **`website/src/css/custom.css`** — hosts `VictorMono.ttf` which is **`VictorMono NF`**, a full Nerd Font (10,396 PUA codepoints, covers 245/246 theme glyphs; missing only `U+F8C5` in M365Princess):
  ```css
  @font-face { font-family: "Victor Mono"; src: url('/fonts/VictorMono.ttf') format("truetype"); font-display: swap; }
  --ifm-font-family-monospace: "Victor Mono", "Symbols Nerd Font Mono", "Symbols Nerd Font", ui-monospace, ...;
  ```

### SVG work (TO BE PARKED ON A BRANCH)
- `src/svg/svg.go`, `colors.go`, `window.go`, `decorate.go`, `fit.go` + tests
- `src/terminal/run.go` (Run type, RunMode, CaptureRuns), `src/prompt/runs.go`
- `src/cli/config_export_svg.go`, `src/cli/config_export_image.go`
- `website/plugins/themes/`, `website/src/components/ThemeGallery/`, `website/docs/themes.mdx`
- `tools/svg-png-compare/` (compare.mjs, zip.mjs, package.json)

### The deleted PNG renderer (CRITICAL for the pivot)
**`src/cli/image/`** was deleted in commit `4bc8a9cc`. Recoverable from git history or the worktree at **`/tmp/omp-png`** (commit `eb421824`). Contents were:
- `image.go` (920 lines) — `Renderer{AnsiString, Settings, Path}`, `Init(env)`, `SavePNG()`. Re-parses ANSI via `ansiSequenceRegexMap` (20 regexes, `image.go:185-208`), `processAnsiSequence` (`:767-820`), `buildLayout` (`:449-528`), `fitRow`/`wrapRow` (`:539-620`), `cleanContent` (`:374-401`, appends cursor + `\n\n` + bold `ohmyposh.dev` watermark)
- Window chrome at `factor = 2.0`: `margin = factor*48` (96), `padding = factor*24` (48), titleOffset 80, corner radius 12, fill `#151515`, stroke `#404040` width 2, traffic lights r=18 spacing=50 colors `#ED655A`/`#E1C04C`/`#71BD47`, stackblur shadow radius 32 offset (32,32) color `#10101066`
- `fontHeight() = regular.Metrics().Height >> 6`; `lineSpacing = 1.2`; `height = len(rows) * fontHeight() * lineSpacing`
- Downloads Hack Nerd Font v3.2.1 from GitHub at runtime (`image.go:236-255`), caches to `cache.Path()/Hack.zip`
- Dependencies (removed from go.mod in `4bc8a9cc`): `github.com/fogleman/gg v1.3.0`, `github.com/esimov/stackblur-go v1.1.1`, `golang.org/x/image v0.44.0`, `github.com/golang/freetype` (indirect). ~27,700 third-party lines.
- **Known bugs**: no 256-colour (`38;5;N`) patterns at all; single `style` string so bold+italic can't coexist; drops hyperlink URLs; hand-maintained `doubleWidthRunes` table

### Data/replay infrastructure (KEEP — needed for any endpoint)
- **`src/cli/config_export_data.go`** — `config export data`, `--sanitize`, `--themes <dir>` merge mode. Records post-`Enabled()` state.
- **`src/config/data.go`** — `DataVersion`, `RecordedSegment{Enabled, Data}` envelope, `Data.Version`
- **`src/config/segment.go`** — `restoreData()` at `:202` short-circuits before `writer.Enabled()` at `:242`; `overlayData()` at `:245`; `restoreCache()` at `:206` also calls `overlayData()`
- **`src/cli/data.go`** — `--data-derive` flag, hand-written-file warning
- **`src/prompt/testdata/fixtures/prompt.data.json`** — single 23.9 KB sanitized fixture for all 124 themes
- **`src/prompt/golden_test.go`** — `TestMain` pins `time.Local = time.UTC`, unsets `TERM_PROGRAM`/`WT_SESSION`, temp cache dir; hash manifest + 12 representative goldens

### SSRF constraint (MUST CARRY FORWARD)
`src/segments/http.go:27` takes an arbitrary URL from config properties. So do `owm`, `nba`, `ipify`, `todoist`, `wakatime`. **Any render endpoint must be data-replay only, with live segment resolution hard-disabled by a compile-time or entrypoint guard, not a config option — plus size/depth/deadline caps and per-IP rate limiting.**

## 4. Errors and Fixes

1. **Nerd Font scan missed `\uXXXX` escapes** — I claimed 0/117 docs had PUA codepoints and dropped the facet. Real: 112/117 docs, 28/117 segments need one in default `Template()`. Fixed by rescanning with the escape pattern.
2. **Golden gate had 0% coverage of the gradient path** — `writeBodyGradient`, `writeVisibleRune`, `stampGradient` all 0.0% during a golden run (no bundled theme uses gradients). Proved by mutation: deleting `cellIndex += 4` left goldens green. Fixed by adding characterization tests first (commit `e279f6a8`).
3. **Proposed cursor design was a 6.1x CPU pessimization** — `next()` too large to inline, destroying the fast path. All shapes were 0 allocs, so my allocation-only gate was blind. Fixed by sharing only `classifyAnchor` after `<`.
4. **"ignore ns/op" was my bad methodology** — 200x benchtime gave 25% spread; 2s gives ±2%. Fixed by re-recording baselines at `-benchtime=2s`.
5. **`--data` replay not hermetic** — recorder skipped disabled segments (`config_export_data.go:129`). `chips` replayed in 1.22s because `wakatime` made a live HTTP call. Fixed in `b8381b97` (record all segments with enabled flag).
6. **Sanitizer scrubs were silent no-ops** — matched Go field names against JSON with lowercase tags. **Leaked the user's real email `jan.de.dobbeleer@gmail.com` into 8 fixtures at `segments.az.data.user.name`**, and it rendered into visible prompt output. Fixed by correcting keys AND replacing the field-name backstop with a structural shape-based one.
7. **Merge rule picked most-common instead of richest** — git came from the 53 themes that don't fetch status, so goldens stopped exercising git status rendering entirely. Fixed to richest-variant.
8. **`config export image` exited 0 on render failures** — font download failure published an empty themes page with a green build. Fixed in `5a8ee35d` (exit 0 → 154).
9. **`isHyperlink` never reset** — one unbalanced `<LINK>` corrupted every subsequent Write for the process lifetime. Fixed in `1e610dff`.
10. **`countVisibleCells` had no `hyperLinkEnd` case** — `VisibleCells("ab<transparent,transparent>hidden</LINK>tail")` = 6 vs rendered 2. Plus leading-anchor divergence. 72 divergences → 0 (commit `4f658ca1`).
11. **`Plain` mode leaked hyperlink URLs** — guarding only escape emitters left the URL as 26 visible chars with length 6. Fixed by also returning early in `write()` (commit `beaa7160`).
12. **My `run.go` doc comments described pre-SGR-7-swap state** — the SVG encoder implemented the comment and painted transparency inverted. Fixed in `6e2377a9`.
13. **Double-width table premise was false** — measured `hmtx`: every icon advances exactly 1.000 cells in BOTH Hack and Victor Mono. Ink overflows (up to 1.833 cells) by design. Reverted in `9d4fdd6f`.
14. **Cell width "fix" 7/12 = 0.58333 encoded a truncation bug** — PNG's 28px came from `MeasureString >> 6`; Hack's true advance is 0.6021 em. Original 0.6 was accurate to 0.35%; my fix was 3.1% wrong. Reverted to true metrics.
15. **Line height 1.4 was nearly right (1.397)** — my "fitted to wrong font" claim was itself wrong. The real vertical bug was a **missing blank row** (PNG emits two newlines before watermark, we emitted one).
16. **The comparison harness's aggregate % is blind to horizontal layout** — stayed ~8.7% across three different fixes because it force-fits the SVG into the PNG's dimensions. A per-row ink profile found the real error immediately.
17. **Repeated cwd drift** — a failed `cd` in an `&&` chain left later commands running elsewhere, producing false results (e.g. "124 of 124 themes render empty"). Fixed by always using absolute paths.
18. **`git stash` while an agent was writing files** — pathspec scoped it so nothing was lost, but careless.

**User feedback that redirected me:**
- "review the plans with Opus 5 instead" (I had tried to use Fable for a plan review)
- "Ask me the questions again" (after rejecting an AskUserQuestion)
- "If you look at the generated SVGs... it is not aligned with what we have or had previously" — four concrete rendering defects

## 5. Problem Solving

**Solved:** Faceted segment catalog; homepage rhythm; golden harness over 124 themes; hermetic replay; tokenizer collapse; run stream as IR; SVG encoder; gallery migration (8 MB → 421 KB); PNG exporter deletion (2,046 lines, 918 KB smaller binary); 3 of 4 SVG rendering defects.
