import sys

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[-1])
from rowprofile import read_png  # noqa: E402


def analyse(path):
    w, h, bpp, px = read_png(path)

    first_opaque = None
    first_colour = None
    last_colour = None

    for y in range(h):
        base = y * w * bpp
        opaque = 0
        colour = 0
        for x in range(0, w, 3):
            i = base + x * bpp
            r, g, b = px[i], px[i + 1], px[i + 2]
            a = px[i + 3] if bpp == 4 else 255
            if a < 40:
                continue
            opaque += 1
            mx, mn = max(r, g, b), min(r, g, b)
            # Saturated or bright => prompt content, not the dark window fill.
            if (mx - mn) > 45 or mx > 150:
                colour += 1
        if opaque > w // 20 and first_opaque is None:
            first_opaque = y
        if colour > 12:
            if first_colour is None:
                first_colour = y
            last_colour = y

    return {
        "size": f"{w}x{h}",
        "window_top": first_opaque,
        "text_top": first_colour,
        "text_bottom": last_colour,
        "text_span": (last_colour - first_colour) if first_colour is not None else None,
    }


for p in sys.argv[1:-1]:
    name = p.replace("\\", "/").split("/")[-1]
    r = analyse(p)
    print(
        f"{name:28} {r['size']:10} window_top={r['window_top']}  "
        f"text {r['text_top']}..{r['text_bottom']} (span {r['text_span']})"
    )

package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/cache"
	"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/config"
	"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/prompt"
	"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/runtime"
	"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/shell"
	"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/template"
	"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/terminal"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

var (
	outputImage        string
	svgFontFamily      string
	imageTerminalWidth int
	svgCellWidth       float64
	svgLineHeight      float64
)

var imageCmd = &cobra.Command{
	Use:   "image",
	Short: "Export your config to an SVG image",
	Long: `Export your config to an SVG image.

The image renders straight from the prompt's own Run stream, so it stays crisp at any zoom level
and, unlike a rasterized image, faithfully reproduces every color and style the prompt itself can
render.

You can tweak the output by using additional flags:

- terminal-width: number of columns the image canvas is rendered at; this
  is also the width the prompt is rendered with, so right-aligned blocks
  and rprompts line up with the image the same way they would in a real
  terminal of that width (default 120). Lines that still don't fit either
  collapse their alignment padding or wrap onto the next row
- font-family: CSS font-family value the svg renders text with; defaults to
  a Nerd Font stack
- cell-width: horizontal advance of one monospace cell, as a multiple of
  font-size (e.g. 0.6021, not a pixel count); defaults to Hack Nerd Font's
  own advance ratio, matching the default font-family stack. Set this
  explicitly when font-family names a font with a different advance ratio
- line-height: vertical advance of one row, as a multiple of font-size;
  defaults to Hack Nerd Font's own line height. Set this explicitly
  alongside font-family/cell-width for the same reason

Example usage:

> oh-my-posh config export image --config ~/myconfig.omp.json

Exports the config to an image file called myconfig.svg in the current working directory.

> oh-my-posh config export image --config ~/myconfig.omp.json --output ~/mytheme.svg

Exports the config to an image file ~/mytheme.svg.`,
	Args: cobra.NoArgs,
	Run: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) {
		cache.Init(os.Getenv("POSH_SHELL"))

		err := setConfigFlag()
		if err != nil {
			exitcode = 666
			fmt.Println(err.Error())
			return
		}

		cfg := config.Load(configFlag)

		flags := &runtime.Flags{
			ConfigPath:    cfg.Source,
			Shell:         shell.GENERIC,
			TerminalWidth: imageTerminalWidth,
		}

		if err := applyDataFile(flags, cmd.Flags().Changed); err != nil {
			exitcode = 666
			fmt.Println(err.Error())
			return
		}

		env := &runtime.Terminal{}
		env.Init(flags)

		template.Init(env, cfg.Var, cfg.Maps)

		defer func() {
			template.SaveCache()
			cache.Close()
		}()

		// set sane defaults for things we don't print
		cfg.ConsoleTitleTemplate = ""
		cfg.PWD = ""
		cfg.ShellIntegration = false

		terminal.Init(shell.GENERIC)
		terminal.BackgroundColor = cfg.TerminalBackground.ResolveTemplate()
		terminal.Colors = cfg.MakeColors(env)
		terminal.CaptureRuns = true

		eng := &prompt.Engine{
			Config: cfg,
			Env:    env,
		}

		// Primary renders the prompt and, since CaptureRuns is set above, records
		// its structured Run stream for exportSVG to read back via CapturedRuns.
		eng.Primary()

		if err := exportSVG(eng, cfg, outputImage, svgFontFamily, imageTerminalWidth, svgCellWidth, svgLineHeight); err != nil {
			exitcode = 666
			fmt.Println(err.Error())
		}
	},
}

func init() {
	imageCmd.Flags().StringVarP(&outputImage, "output", "o", "", "image file (.svg) to export to")
	imageCmd.Flags().StringVar(&svgFontFamily, "font-family", "", "CSS font-family for the exported svg")
	imageCmd.Flags().StringVar(&dataPath, "data", "", "path to a template data file (json/yaml/toml) to render with")
	imageCmd.Flags().IntVar(&imageTerminalWidth, "terminal-width", 120, "number of columns to render the prompt and image at")
	imageCmd.Flags().Float64Var(&svgCellWidth, "cell-width", 0, "horizontal advance of one cell, as a multiple of font-size (defaults to Hack Nerd Font's own ratio)")
	imageCmd.Flags().Float64Var(&svgLineHeight, "line-height", 0, "vertical advance of one row, as a multiple of font-size (defaults to Hack Nerd Font's own ratio)")

	exportCmd.AddCommand(imageCmd)
}

func setConfigFlag() error {
	if configFlag != "" {
		return nil
	}

	configPath, OK := cache.Get[string](cache.Session, config.SourceKey)
	if !OK {
		return fmt.Errorf("no config found in session cache, please provide a config using the --config flag")
	}

	configFlag = configPath
	return nil
}

description: Read TTF tables directly instead of inferring font geometry from rendered output — three wrong oh-my-posh SVG fixes came from inference

While making the SVG prompt exporter match the retired PNG renderer, three fixes in a row
were wrong because font geometry was inferred from rendered images instead of read from the
font files. Each took a full implement-and-measure cycle to disprove.

1. **"Nerd Font icons are double-width."** Ported the old renderer's `doubleWidthRunes` table
   on that premise. Measured `hmtx`: every icon advances **exactly 1.000 cells** in both Hack
   Nerd Font and VictorMono NF. What actually overflows is the glyph *ink* (up to 1.83× the
   cell), by design — terminals let it bleed. `Run.Cells` was right all along.
2. **"The cell width is 28/48 = 0.5833 em."** Derived from the PNG canvas arithmetic. That 28
   came from `MeasureString(" ") >> 6`, which **truncates**; Hack's real advance is 0.6021 em.
   The original 0.6 default was accurate to 0.35% and the "fix" made it 3.1% wrong.
3. **"Line height is 1.4 em."** Reverse-engineered from reference images. Real values:
   Hack **1.1641 em**, VictorMono NF **1.4091 em** (hhea ascender − descender + lineGap). The
   constant had been fitted to the wrong font by coincidence — the references were rendered
   in Hack.

Reading a TTF for this is ~60 lines of `struct.unpack`: table directory at offset 12,
`head` for unitsPerEm at +18, `hhea` for ascender/descender/lineGap at +4, `hmtx` for
advances, `cmap` format 4/12 for codepoint→glyph. Scripts live in this session's scratchpad.

**Why:** cell width and line height differ by 10% and 21% between two fonts both in active
use, so any single hardcoded constant is wrong for one of them. They belong in options,
supplied per font, not guessed.

**How to apply:** before compensating for font behaviour, read the font. And note the
aggregate image-diff percentage was **blind** to all three — it sat at ~8.7% across every
attempt, because the harness force-fits the SVG into the PNG's dimensions. A per-row ink
profile found the real (vertical) error immediately. Pick an instrument that can see the
thing being changed; see [[omp-golden-harness-ambient-inputs]] for the same lesson about
green gates that measure nothing.

import struct
import sys


def tables(data):
    n = struct.unpack(">H", data[4:6])[0]
    t = {}
    for i in range(n):
        off = 12 + i * 16
        tag = data[off:off + 4].decode("latin-1")
        to, tl = struct.unpack(">II", data[off + 8:off + 16])
        t[tag] = (to, tl)
    return t


for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    t = tables(data)

    upem = struct.unpack(">H", data[t["head"][0] + 18:t["head"][0] + 20])[0]

    h = t["hhea"][0]
    asc, desc, gap = struct.unpack(">hhh", data[h + 4:h + 10])

    name = path.replace("\\", "/").split("/")[-1]
    line = asc - desc + gap

    print(f"{name}")
    print(f"  units/em        {upem}")
    print(f"  hhea ascender   {asc:6}  ({asc / upem:.4f} em)")
    print(f"  hhea descender  {desc:6}  ({desc / upem:.4f} em)")
    print(f"  hhea lineGap    {gap:6}  ({gap / upem:.4f} em)")
    print(f"  line height     {line:6}  ({line / upem:.4f} em)   <- Metrics().Height")

    if "OS/2" in t:
        o = t["OS/2"][0]
        ta, td, tg = struct.unpack(">hhh", data[o + 68:o + 74])
        print(f"  OS/2 typo       asc {ta} desc {td} gap {tg}  -> {(ta - td + tg) / upem:.4f} em")
        wa, wd = struct.unpack(">HH", data[o + 74:o + 78])
        print(f"  OS/2 win        asc {wa} desc {wd}            -> {(wa + wd) / upem:.4f} em")
    print()

CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread

Base directory for this skill: D:\oh-my-posh\.claude\skills\code-changes

# Code Changes

The workflow for going from an issue, pull request, idea, or feature request to shipped code.
Follow the phases in order. Analysis always comes first; code comes last.

Each phase has a reference file with the full instructions. **Read the reference file when you
enter the phase** — not before, and never skip it because the phase "looks obvious".

## Roles

Assign work based on model capability. The coordinator is not the strongest model — it's the one
that stays resident, owns every phase by default, and knows when it's out of its depth.

| Role        | Capability tier                                               | Owns                                                                          |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Coordinator | Capable mid-tier, resident for the whole task                | Analysis, plan, delegation, supervision, verification, delivery — by default |
| Escalation  | Strongest reasoning model available; invoked only on trigger | The specific judgment call the coordinator flagged, then control returns     |
| Implementer | Same tier as coordinator, or smaller for trivial edits        | Executing one pinned, self-contained task                                    |

Concrete model names per vendor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) and how to run the split in Claude
Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or IDE agents: [references/model-tiers.md](references/model-tiers.md).

When the current agent already runs at implementer tier, there's no separate delegation step for
standard work: plan and execute directly, still following every phase. Escalate to the strongest
model only when a trigger fires — see [references/escalate.md](references/escalate.md) — never by
default and never for a routine judgment call the coordinator is equipped to make itself.

## The flow

1. **Analyze** ([references/analyze.md](references/analyze.md)) — root cause and scope,
   validated against the code, never against the report alone.

# Phase 1 — Analyze

Start every task here, no matter how it arrived: issue link, PR number, verbal idea, bug report.
No code gets written or edited during this phase.

## Gather the full context

- Issues and PRs: `gh issue view <n> --comments` / `gh pr view <n> --comments`, plus linked
  issues, referenced discussions, and any code the report points at.
- Ideas and verbal requests: restate the goal and constraints in your own words. If the request
  is ambiguous, resolve the ambiguity now — not halfway through implementation.
- Check for prior art: existing helpers, similar segments/modules, and past commits that touched
  the same area (`git log -- <path>`).

## Reproduce before theorizing

Reproduce the problem when possible. A reproduction turns the analysis from a hypothesis into a
fact and gives Phase 5 its verification case for free. When reproduction is impossible (platform,
hardware, credentials), say so explicitly in the report and mark the fix as unverified-by-repro.

## Find the root cause in the code

- Read the actual implementation. Never reason from the issue text, a review comment, or a stack
  trace alone — reports and bot reviewers are frequently wrong.
- Distinguish the root cause from the symptom. Fixing where it crashes is not the same as fixing
  why it crashes.
- State what the change should be, which files it touches, and what it deliberately leaves alone.

## When to escalate

If root cause can't be pinned with confidence, or the fix looks architectural, security-sensitive,
or irreversible, hand the specific question to the strongest available model instead of guessing —
see [references/escalate.md](references/escalate.md). Resume ownership of the phase once the
question is answered.

## Output of this phase

A short analysis report to the user containing:

1. What is actually happening and why (root cause, with file references).
2. The proposed change and its scope.
3. What is intentionally out of scope.
4. Open questions, if any remain.

## Stop gate

Report the analysis and wait for a go before implementing. Skip the gate only when the user
already gave the go in the request itself ("do it", "fix it and commit", "implement with
Sonnet"). A go given for analysis is not a go for implementation.

1	package terminal
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/color"
7	)
8	
9	// CaptureRuns turns on the parallel Run stream Write/String build alongside the ANSI
10	// bytes they already emit, for a later encoder (an SVG renderer, eventually) to draw the
11	// prompt without parsing escape sequences. Off by default, mirroring Plain/Interactive:
12	// with it off, every capture site below is a single `if CaptureRuns` check and nothing
13	// else runs, so the ANSI hot path's allocation profile is unchanged (see the exact
14	// allocs/B-per-op gates in bench_test.go). With it on, capture is allowed to allocate.
15	var CaptureRuns bool
16	
17	// RunMode discriminates the three ways writeSegmentColors (and writeAnchorOverride's
18	// matching branches) can render a segment or override. All three print bytes that read
19	// back as the same ANSI token "transparent" once decoded, so a Run needs this field to
20	// tell them apart; see writeSegmentColors' switch for the three branches it names.
21	type RunMode int
22	
23	const (
24		// RunNormal is a run rendered with its own foreground/background: neither of the
25		// two transparent branches below applied.
26		RunNormal RunMode = iota
27	
28		// RunBackgroundPainted is the branch taken when the foreground is transparent and a
29		// terminal background color is known: the cell renders filled with the segment's own
30		// background color, and the glyph itself renders in the terminal's default background
31		// color, cutting its shape out of that fill — the SGR sequence sets the segment's
32		// background as a foreground code, resets the background to default, then SGR 7
33		// (reverse video) swaps the two, so what actually paints is the inverse of what the
34		// codes name.
35		RunBackgroundPainted
36	
37		// RunReverseVideo is the branch taken when the foreground is transparent and no
38		// terminal background is known: reverse video (SGR 7) still swaps foreground/
39		// background as described above, so the cell renders filled with the segment's own
40		// background color; the glyph itself renders in whatever the real terminal's default
41		// background turns out to be, which is unknown here (that's the "no terminal
42		// background is known" half of this branch's condition).
43		RunReverseVideo
44	)
45	
46	// runAttributeSlots mirrors len(knownStyles): one nesting-depth counter per style
47	// anchor. knownStyles is a var, not a const, so this can't be derived at compile time;
48	// TestRunAttributeSlotsMatchesKnownStyles pins the two in sync.
49	const runAttributeSlots = 8
50	
51	// Run is one contiguous span of text rendered under a single, unchanging style: the
52	// exact SGR pair and its pre-ToAnsi source form (a #RRGGBB hex, a colour name, accent,
53	// transparent, or a gradient definition — see color.History.Add), a render-mode
54	// discriminator, per-style-anchor nesting depth, and — for a cell stamped from the
55	// segment's own gradient — the true RGB behind the printed escape.
56	//
57	// Cells is the run's rendered width, a length delta matching what write() counts toward
58	// String()'s returned length; it can be zero (e.g. a hyperlink's URL text, which Text
59	// includes but write() never counts toward length) even when Text is non-empty.
60	type Run struct {
61		BackgroundRGB    *color.RGB
62		ForegroundRGB    *color.RGB
63		Text             string
64		Background       color.Ansi
65		Foreground       color.Ansi
66		BackgroundSource color.Ansi
67		ForegroundSource color.Ansi
68		Mode             RunMode
69		Cells            int
70		Attributes       [runAttributeSlots]uint8
71	}
72	
73	// Runs returns the Run stream captured since the last String() call. Empty when
74	// CaptureRuns is false.
75	func Runs() []Run {
76		return runsState.Runs
77	}
78	
79	// runState bundles the run-capture bookkeeping threaded alongside colorState through the
80	// same style-anchor and color-change events (see colorState's own doc comment), only
81	// touched when CaptureRuns is true. text accumulates the pending run's content exactly as
82	// write() sends it to builder — see write()'s mirrored calls. depth is the running
83	// nesting counter per knownStyles slot, mutated at the three style-anchor emission sites
84	// (Write's leading-anchor prologue, writeAnchorOverride's Start/End cases) and reset
85	// alongside the writer's own end-of-segment SGR reset and in String()'s defer; attributes
86	// is depth's last snapshot, copied into a Run at flushRun. background/foreground/
87	// backgroundSource/foregroundSource/mode/backgroundRGB/foregroundRGB are the pending
88	// run's style, refreshed by syncPendingStyle after every event that can change it.
89	type runState struct {
90		backgroundRGB    *color.RGB
91		foregroundRGB    *color.RGB
92		background       color.Ansi
93		foreground       color.Ansi
94		backgroundSource color.Ansi
95		foregroundSource color.Ansi
96		text             strings.Builder
97		Runs             []Run
98		mode             RunMode
99		cellsAtFlush     int
100		attributes       [runAttributeSlots]uint8
101		depth            [runAttributeSlots]uint8
102	}
103	
104	var runsState runState
105	
106	// flushRun cuts the text accumulated since the last flush into a Run using the pending
107	// style snapshot (background/foreground/source/mode/attributes/RGB), then resets the
108	// text accumulator. A call with nothing accumulated — no text, no cell delta — is a
109	// no-op: several call sites flush unconditionally on entry (writeSegmentColors,
110	// writeAnchorOverride, endColorOverride all flush before touching any state), and most of
111	// those calls land here with nothing pending, since the previous flush already cut it.
112	func flushRun() {
113		cells := length - runsState.cellsAtFlush
114		text := runsState.text.String()
115	
116		if len(text) != 0 || cells != 0 {
117			runsState.Runs = append(runsState.Runs, Run{
118				Text:             text,
119				Background:       runsState.background,
120				Foreground:       runsState.foreground,
121				BackgroundSource: runsState.backgroundSource,
122				ForegroundSource: runsState.foregroundSource,
123				BackgroundRGB:    runsState.backgroundRGB,
124				ForegroundRGB:    runsState.foregroundRGB,
125				Attributes:       runsState.attributes,
126				Mode:             runsState.mode,
127				Cells:            cells,
128			})
129		}
130	
131		runsState.text.Reset()
132		runsState.cellsAtFlush = length
133	}
134	
135	// syncPendingStyle snapshots cs's current active style — background/foreground/source,
136	// the render-mode discriminator, and the attribute nesting depth — as what governs
137	// whatever text comes next, and clears the gradient RGB (stampGradient sets it again,
138	// per cell, only for a channel it actually stamps). Called after every event that can
139	// change the active style: writeSegmentColors, writeAnchorOverride (including its
140	// style-anchor early returns, where only the attributes changed), and endColorOverride.
141	func syncPendingStyle(cs *colorState) {
142		runsState.background = activeBackground(cs)
143		runsState.foreground = activeForeground(cs)
144		runsState.backgroundSource = activeBackgroundSource(cs)
145		runsState.foregroundSource = activeForegroundSource(cs)
146		runsState.mode = deriveRunMode(cs)
147		runsState.attributes = runsState.depth
148		runsState.backgroundRGB = nil
149		runsState.foregroundRGB = nil
150	}
151	
152	// activeBackgroundSource/activeForegroundSource are activeBackground/activeForeground's
153	// source-form counterparts: the top of the override history's source, or the segment
154	// base's source when no override is active.
155	func activeBackgroundSource(cs *colorState) color.Ansi {
156		if bg := cs.currentColor.Background(); !bg.IsEmpty() {
157			return cs.currentColor.BackgroundSource()
158		}
159	
160		return cs.backgroundColorSource
161	}
162	
163	func activeForegroundSource(cs *colorState) color.Ansi {
164		if fg := cs.currentColor.Foreground(); !fg.IsEmpty() {
165			return cs.currentColor.ForegroundSource()
166		}
167	
168		return cs.foregroundColorSource
169	}
170	
171	// deriveRunMode mirrors writeSegmentColors' own switch (and writeAnchorOverride's
172	// matching branches) on cs's now-current active foreground and the package-level
173	// terminal background, so a single derivation covers all three call sites instead of
174	// each branch setting it inline (which would have to be threaded through every early
175	// return).
176	func deriveRunMode(cs *colorState) RunMode {
177		fg := activeForeground(cs)
178	
179		switch {
180		case fg.IsTransparent() && len(BackgroundColor) != 0:
181			return RunBackgroundPainted
182		case fg.IsTransparent():
183			return RunReverseVideo
184		default:
185			return RunNormal
186		}
187	}

1	// Package svg renders a captured terminal.Run stream to a self-contained SVG
2	// document. It is a sibling encoder to the ANSI writer (see
3	// terminal.CaptureRuns): both start from the same Run stream, one emitting
4	// escape sequences, the other emitting markup, so neither has to parse the
5	// other's output.
6	package svg
7	
8	import (
9		"hash/fnv"
10		"math"
11		"strconv"
12		"strings"
13	
14		"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/color"
15		"github.com/jandedobbeleer/oh-my-posh/src/terminal"
16	)
17	
18	// Options configures the SVG canvas: font metrics, plus the two colors a Run
19	// stream cannot carry itself. BackgroundSource/ForegroundSource can hold
20	// "accent" or the ansiColorCodes name "default", both of which resolve
21	// against live package state in the ANSI writer (color.Defaults' accent,
22	// the real terminal background) rather than anything in the Run itself.
23	// Taking them as explicit fields — instead of Encode reaching for that
24	// package state — is what makes color resolution unit-testable.
25	type Options struct {
26		TerminalBackground *color.RGB
27		AccentForeground   *color.RGB
28		AccentBackground   *color.RGB
29		// CanvasBackground serves two roles that must stay the same color for a
30		// reverse-video cutout to read as a hole punched through to the window
31		// behind it, rather than a mismatched patch: it is both the glyph color
32		// painted for a transparent-foreground run whose real terminal
33		// background is unknown (terminal.RunReverseVideo — see paintRun) and,
34		// since 6e2377a9, the fill of the terminal window Encode now draws
35		// behind every row (see window.go). A real terminal shows its own
36		// default background in both places; absent one to match, withDefaults
37		// falls back to the retired PNG renderer's own fixed #151515 for both.
38		CanvasBackground *color.RGB
39		FontFamily       string
40		FontSize         float64
41		// CellWidth is the horizontal advance of one monospace cell, in the same
42		// unit FontSize is (an absolute value, not a ratio of it — a caller sets
43		// both explicitly, e.g. testOptions' FontSize:10/CellWidth:10 pairing).
44		// Zero falls back to FontSize*defaultCellWidth (~0.6021em), Hack Nerd
45		// Font's own advance ratio read straight from its hmtx table (ASCII 'M':
46		// 1233 font units / 2048 units-per-em — see defaultCellWidth's doc
47		// comment). That default matches the bundled font stack (see
48		// defaultFontFamily), but the website renders these in Victor Mono,
49		// whose advance ratio is measurably different (0.5455em) — a caller
50		// with a different font should set CellWidth explicitly rather than
51		// assume this default (see cli/config_export_svg.go's svgOptions for
52		// how the CLI's --cell-width, quoted as a font-size ratio, converts to
53		// this field's absolute unit).
54		CellWidth float64
55		// LineHeight is the vertical advance of one row, in the same absolute
56		// unit as CellWidth. Zero falls back to FontSize*defaultLineHeight
57		// (~1.397em), Hack Nerd Font's own hhea-derived line height times the
58		// retired PNG renderer's lineSpacing constant (see defaultLineHeight's
59		// doc comment). Like CellWidth, this is font-specific — Victor Mono's
60		// is ~1.691em — and a caller rendering in a different font should set
61		// it explicitly.
62		LineHeight float64
63		// Padding is the gap between the window's rounded edge and the content
64		// grid on all four sides (the title bar reserves additional space of
65		// its own above the top padding — see windowGeometry). It defaults to
66		// FontSize, which is exactly the retired PNG renderer's own padding
67		// constant (48px) scaled by FontSize/48 at this package's default
68		// 16px FontSize — see newWindowGeometry's doc comment.
69		Padding float64
70		// Columns fixes the canvas' content width at Columns*CellWidth,
71		// independent of any row's actual content: the terminal-window
72		// presentation this package restores needs a stable frame size
73		// regardless of what a theme renders, exactly like every reference PNG
74		// the old renderer produced was a fixed-width window rather than one
75		// that shrink-wrapped to content. Zero falls back to defaultColumns
76		// (120), matching both the retired renderer's own default and the
77		// image-export CLI command's --terminal-width flag default, so a
78		// caller that doesn't set this still gets the terminal-shaped canvas
79		// the reference PNGs always had.
80		Columns int
81	}
82	
83	const (
84		defaultFontFamily = `"CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font", "FiraCode Nerd Font", "Hack Nerd Font", ui-monospace, monospace`
85		defaultFontSize   = 16.0
86		// defaultColumns matches the retired PNG renderer's own defaultColumns
87		// and the image-export CLI command's --terminal-width flag default: a
88		// caller that never sets Options.Columns still gets a 120-column window.
89		defaultColumns = 120
90	
91		// defaultCellWidth is Hack Nerd Font's true advance ratio for an ASCII
92		// glyph, read directly from the font's own hmtx table rather than
93		// reverse-engineered from a rendered reference: HackNerdFont-Regular.ttf
94		// reports unitsPerEm 2048 and an 'M' advance of 1233 units, 1233/2048 =
95		// 0.60205...em. Every Nerd Font Private Use Area icon measured
96		// alongside it (E0B0, F408, F044, E62A, E725, F489) also advances
97		// exactly 1.000 cell, in both Hack and Victor Mono — the icons overflow
98		// their own cell's ink, sometimes past 1.8 cells wide, but that is by
99		// design (a terminal renders the next glyph a full cell over
100		// regardless, letting the ink spill) and not something to budget extra
101		// cell width for; see the now-removed doublewidth.go this package used
102		// to carry for exactly that mistake.
103		//
104		// A prior version of this default used 7.0/12.0 (0.58333em), backed out
105		// from the retired PNG renderer's own reference canvas arithmetic. That
106		// number encodes a bug, not a font property: the PNG renderer computed
107		// its advance via `font.Drawer.MeasureString(" ") >> 6`, a 26.6
108		// fixed-point shift that truncates the fractional pixel rather than
109		// rounding it (image.go's fontHeight/spaceAdvance). At its 48px
110		// reference em, Hack's true advance is 48*0.60205 = 28.9px, which the
111		// PNG renderer truncated down to 28px — 0.9px lost per column, 3.2% of
112		// the true advance. Reproducing that truncation here would bake a
113		// rounding defect specific to one em size into a vector format that has
114		// no rounding to do at all, and it would be flatly wrong for any other
115		// font or FontSize. See defaultLineHeight for the matching line-height
116		// derivation and the residual drift this choice leaves against the old
117		// PNG references.
118		defaultCellWidth = 1233.0 / 2048.0
119	
120		// defaultLineHeight is Hack Nerd Font's own line height — hhea's
121		// Ascender - Descender + LineGap, 2384 units at unitsPerEm 2048 =
122		// 1.1641em — times 1.2, the retired PNG renderer's own lineSpacing
123		// constant (image.go: `ir.lineSpacing = 1.2`, applied as
124		// `regular.Metrics().Height * lineSpacing`, image.go ~:310-312,
125		// ~:727-761). 1.1641 * 1.2 = 1.397em.
126		//
127		// A prior version of this default was a flat 1.4, backed out from the
128		// PNG reference renders' pixel dimensions (48px em, 66px content rows,
129		// 66/48 ≈ 1.375) rather than font metrics. That number is close to
130		// Victor Mono's own ratio (1.4091 * 1.2 = 1.691em) but every reference
131		// PNG was actually rendered in Hack (1.397em) — a coincidence of
132		// fitting the wrong font, not a derivation. See defaultCellWidth's doc
133		// comment for why a metric derived from the font, not from the old
134		// renderer's rounded pixels, is the correct default here too.
135		defaultLineHeight = (2384.0 / 2048.0) * 1.2
136	)
137	
138	// defaultCanvasBackground is the retired PNG renderer's own fixed fallback
139	// (image.go's defaultBackgroundColor, #151515) for the glyph color a
140	// transparent-foreground run paints when no real terminal background is
141	// known; see Options.CanvasBackground.
142	var defaultCanvasBackground = color.RGB{R: 0x15, G: 0x15, B: 0x15}
143	
144	// withDefaults fills every zero-value metric with a sensible default, so a
145	// caller only has to set the fields it cares about — typically just the two
146	// colors — and still gets a fully specified canvas.
147	func (o *Options) withDefaults() Options {
148		out := *o
149	
150		if out.FontFamily == "" {
151			out.FontFamily = defaultFontFamily
152		}
153	
154		if out.FontSize == 0 {
155			out.FontSize = defaultFontSize
156		}
157	
158		if out.CellWidth == 0 {
159			out.CellWidth = out.FontSize * defaultCellWidth
160		}
161	
162		if out.LineHeight == 0 {
163			out.LineHeight = out.FontSize * defaultLineHeight
164		}
165	
166		if out.Padding == 0 {
167			out.Padding = out.FontSize
168		}
169	
170		if out.CanvasBackground == nil {
171			out.CanvasBackground = &defaultCanvasBackground
172		}
173	
174		if out.Columns <= 0 {
175			out.Columns = defaultColumns
176		}
177	
178		return out
179	}
180	
181	// Encode renders rows of runs — one []terminal.Run per output row, as
182	// prompt.Engine.CapturedRuns returns — into a self-contained SVG document.
183	//
184	// Layout is a monospace cell grid: every run advances the running column by
185	// its own Cells, never by measuring glyphs. Each <text> element also carries
186	// textLength/lengthAdjust pinning it to exactly Cells*CellWidth, so it lands
187	// on the grid regardless of the browser's own font metrics. A Nerd Font
188	// icon's ink commonly overflows that one-cell box (see defaultCellWidth's
189	// doc comment on measured ink-vs-advance ratios) — that overflow is left
190	// alone, exactly like a real terminal lets a wide glyph draw over the
191	// following cell's left edge, rather than compensated for with extra grid
192	// width.
193	//
194	// A run with Cells == 0 (e.g. a hyperlink's URL text — see terminal.Run's
195	// doc comment) is skipped entirely: no rect, no text, no column advance.
196	//
197	// font-family/font-size/white-space are written as presentation attributes
198	// on the root <svg> element rather than a <style> rule: all three are
199	// ordinary inherited CSS properties, so every descendant <text> picks them
200	// up for free, and a document embedding many of these SVGs inline never gets
201	// a document-scoped <style> block fighting its own page styles. Each <text>
202	// element carries no dominant-baseline/alignment-baseline attribute at all,
203	// so it renders on SVG's default alphabetic baseline; encodeRow computes
204	// that baseline's y itself (rowTop + 0.75*LineHeight, see writeText) rather
205	// than anchoring to a rect edge via "hanging", because this package has no
206	// server-side font metrics and "hanging" baseline placement is implemented
207	// inconsistently across browsers — a computed alphabetic-baseline offset is
208	// deterministic everywhere instead.
209	//
210	// A <style> block is emitted only when a run actually blinks (attrBlink >
211	// 0): no bundled theme does, so a gallery of these SVGs carries no <style>
212	// at all. When one does blink, its class name and @keyframes name are
213	// suffixed with a hash of the row content, so two different blinking SVGs
214	// inlined on the same page never share (and can't clash on) the same
215	// document-scoped class/keyframes name.
216	//
217	// Encode takes opts by value, not by pointer, even though Options is 80
218	// bytes (over gocritic's hugeParam threshold): Encode runs once per prompt
219	// render, so the extra copy is immaterial next to the string-building it
220	// does, and the by-value signature keeps the public API's ergonomic call
221	// shape (Encode(rows, Options{...})) rather than forcing every caller through
222	// a throwaway local just to take its address.
223	//
224	//nolint:gocritic
225	func Encode(rows [][]terminal.Run, opts Options) (string, error) {
226		opts = opts.withDefaults()
227		rows = decorate(fitRows(rows, opts.Columns))
228	
229		blinks := false
230		hasher := fnv.New64a()
231	
232		for _, row := range rows {
233			for i := range row {
234				if row[i].Attributes[attrBlink] > 0 {
235					blinks = true
236				}
237	
238				hasher.Write([]byte(row[i].Text))
239				hasher.Write(row[i].Attributes[:])
240			}
241		}
242	
243		var blinkClass string
244		if blinks {
245			blinkClass = "omp-blink-" + strconv.FormatUint(hasher.Sum64(), 36)
246		}
247	
248		geo := newWindowGeometry(&opts)
249		size := newCanvasSize(&geo, opts.Columns, opts.CellWidth, len(rows), opts.LineHeight)
250	
251		var b strings.Builder
252	
253		b.WriteString(`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="`)
254		b.WriteString(formatFloat(size.width))
255		b.WriteString(`" height="`)
256		b.WriteString(formatFloat(size.height))
257		b.WriteString(`" viewBox="0 0 `)
258		b.WriteString(formatFloat(size.width))
259		b.WriteString(" ")
260		b.WriteString(formatFloat(size.height))
261		b.WriteString(`" font-family="`)
262		b.WriteString(escapeAttr(opts.FontFamily))
263		b.WriteString(`" font-size="`)
264		b.WriteString(formatFloat(opts.FontSize))
265		b.WriteString(`px" white-space="pre">`)
266		b.WriteString("\n")
267	
268		if blinkClass != "" {
269			writeBlinkStyle(&b, blinkClass)
270		}
271	
272		// The window's own fill must stay the same color a reverse-video cutout
273		// glyph paints (opts.CanvasBackground — see its doc comment), unless a
274		// real terminal background is actually known, in which case that's the
275		// more accurate choice for both.
276		windowFill := *opts.CanvasBackground
277		if opts.TerminalBackground != nil {
278			windowFill = *opts.TerminalBackground
279		}
280	
281		writeWindowChrome(&b, size, &geo, windowFill)
282	
283		for rowIndex, row := range rows {
284			encodeRow(&b, row, rowIndex, size, opts, blinkClass)
285		}
286	
287		b.WriteString("</svg>")
288	
289		return b.String(), nil
290	}
291	
292	// fitRows applies fitRow (see fit.go) to every captured row when columns is
293	// positive, flattening any row that had to be collapsed/wrapped into
294	// several output rows. Options.withDefaults always leaves Columns positive
295	// (see its doc comment), so the columns <= 0 branch only matters for a
296	// caller that constructs opts by hand and skips withDefaults, e.g. a test.
297	func fitRows(rows [][]terminal.Run, columns int) [][]terminal.Run {
298		if columns <= 0 {
299			return rows
300		}
301	
302		fitted := make([][]terminal.Run, 0, len(rows))
303	
304		for _, row := range rows {
305			fitted = append(fitted, fitRow(row, columns)...)
306		}
307	
308		return fitted
309	}
310	
311	func writeBlinkStyle(b *strings.Builder, blinkClass string) {
312		b.WriteString("<style>\n.")
313		b.WriteString(blinkClass)
314		b.WriteString(" { animation: ")
315		b.WriteString(blinkClass)
316		b.WriteString(" 1s steps(1, end) infinite; }\n@keyframes ")
317		b.WriteString(blinkClass)
318		b.WriteString(" { 50% { opacity: 0; } }\n</style>\n")
319	}
320	
321	// paintState carries the last resolved, non-empty color per channel across
322	// runs in the same row. A Run whose source resolves to nothing — the ToAnsi
323	// failure path color.Defaults.ToAnsi documents (see resolveChannel) — must
324	// keep whatever was already active, exactly like a real terminal that never
325	// received an SGR code for that channel.
326	type paintState struct {
327		fg *color.RGB
328		bg *color.RGB
329	}
330	
331	// encodeRow takes opts by value for the same reason Encode does (see its
332	// comment): it runs once per row, not once per Run, so the 80-byte copy
333	// gocritic flags is immaterial. size.contentX/contentY (see canvasSize) is
334	// the content grid's top-left corner inside the window, replacing what used
335	// to be a flat opts.Padding offset from the canvas edge before the window
336	// chrome existed.
337	//
338	//nolint:gocritic
339	func encodeRow(b *strings.Builder, runs []terminal.Run, rowIndex int, size canvasSize, opts Options, blinkClass string) {
340		state := paintState{}
341		cell := 0
342		rowTop := size.contentY + float64(rowIndex)*opts.LineHeight
343	
344		// baseline places the glyphs roughly centered in the row instead of
345		// hugging its top edge (see the "hanging" removal note on Encode): 0.75
346		// of the row's height backed out from the retired PNG renderer's own
347		// background-rect placement (bgY = y - fontLineHeight*0.75).
348		baseline := rowTop + opts.LineHeight*0.75
349	
350		for i := range runs {
351			run := &runs[i]
352			textRGB, hasRect, rectRGB := paintRun(run, &state, &opts)
353	
354			if run.Cells == 0 {
355				continue
356			}
357	
358			x := size.contentX + float64(cell)*opts.CellWidth
359			runWidth := float64(run.Cells) * opts.CellWidth
360	
361			if hasRect {
362				writeRect(b, x, rowTop, runWidth, opts.LineHeight, *rectRGB)
363			}
364	
365			if run.Text != "" {
366				writeText(b, run.Text, x, baseline, runWidth, textRGB, run.Attributes, blinkClass)
367			}
368	
369			cell += run.Cells
370		}
371	}
372	
373	func writeRect(b *strings.Builder, x, y, width, height float64, rgb color.RGB) {
374		b.WriteString(`<rect x="`)
375		b.WriteString(formatFloat(x))
376		b.WriteString(`" y="`)
377		b.WriteString(formatFloat(y))
378		b.WriteString(`" width="`)
379		b.WriteString(formatFloat(width))
380		b.WriteString(`" height="`)
381		b.WriteString(formatFloat(height))
382		b.WriteString(`" fill="`)
383		b.WriteString(hexString(rgb))
384		b.WriteString("\"/>\n")
385	}
386	
387	// writeText writes a <text> element whose y is already the baseline
388	// coordinate (see encodeRow's baseline), not a rect's top edge: the element
389	// deliberately carries no dominant-baseline attribute, so it renders on
390	// SVG's default alphabetic baseline (see Encode's doc comment).
391	func writeText(b *strings.Builder, text string, x, y, width float64, rgb *color.RGB, attrs [8]uint8, blinkClass string) {
392		b.WriteString(`<text x="`)
393		b.WriteString(formatFloat(x))
394		b.WriteString(`" y="`)
395		b.WriteString(formatFloat(y))
396		b.WriteString(`" textLength="`)
397		b.WriteString(formatFloat(width))
398		b.WriteString(`" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"`)
399	
400		if rgb != nil {
401			b.WriteString(` fill="`)
402			b.WriteString(hexString(*rgb))
403			b.WriteString(`"`)
404		}
405	
406		if attrs[attrBold] > 0 {
407			b.WriteString(` font-weight="bold"`)
408		}
409	
410		if attrs[attrItalic] > 0 {
411			b.WriteString(` font-style="italic"`)
412		}
413	
414		if decoration := textDecoration(attrs); decoration != "" {
415			b.WriteString(` text-decoration="`)
416			b.WriteString(decoration)
417			b.WriteString(`"`)
418		}
419	
420		if attrs[attrDim] > 0 {
421			b.WriteString(` opacity="0.6"`)
422		}
423	
424		if attrs[attrBlink] > 0 {
425			b.WriteString(` class="`)
426			b.WriteString(blinkClass)
427			b.WriteString(`"`)
428		}
429	
430		b.WriteString(">")
431		b.WriteString(escapeXML(text))
432		b.WriteString("</text>\n")
433	}
434	
435	// attribute slot indices mirror knownStyles' order in terminal/writer.go
436	// (bold, underline, overline, italic, strikethrough, dim/faint, blink,
437	// reverse), which Run.Attributes' index space is keyed on; see run.go's
438	// runAttributeSlots.
439	const (
440		attrBold = iota
441		attrUnderline
442		attrOverline
443		attrItalic
444		attrStrikethrough
445		attrDim
446		attrBlink
447		attrReverse
448	)
449	
450	func textDecoration(attrs [8]uint8) string {
451		var parts []string
452	
453		if attrs[attrUnderline] > 0 {
454			parts = append(parts, "underline")
455		}
456	
457		if attrs[attrOverline] > 0 {
458			parts = append(parts, "overline")
459		}
460	
461		if attrs[attrStrikethrough] > 0 {
462			parts = append(parts, "line-through")
463		}
464	
465		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
466	}
467	
468	// paintRun resolves the RGB a run's rect and text should paint, applying its
469	// RunMode (see terminal.RunMode's doc comment) and its reverse-video
470	// attribute. bold/italic/underline/overline/strikethrough/dim/blink are
471	// applied later, directly from Run.Attributes, since they don't affect which
472	// color goes where.
473	func paintRun(run *terminal.Run, state *paintState, opts *Options) (textRGB *color.RGB, hasRect bool, rectRGB *color.RGB) {
474		fg, fgResolved := resolveChannel(run.ForegroundSource, run.ForegroundRGB, false, opts)
475		if fgResolved {
476			state.fg = fg
477		}
478	
479		bg, bgResolved := resolveChannel(run.BackgroundSource, run.BackgroundRGB, true, opts)
480		if bgResolved {
481			state.bg = bg
482		}
483	
484		switch run.Mode {
485		case terminal.RunBackgroundPainted:
486			// the foreground is transparent and a terminal background is known:
487			// the cell fills with the segment's own background, and the glyph
488			// is cut out of that fill in the terminal's own background color —
489			// matching the real terminal rendering (see terminal.RunMode's doc
490			// comment): SGR 7 swaps a foreground code carrying the segment's
491			// background with the just-reset default background, so the segment
492			// background ends up as the visible fill, not the glyph color.
493			rectRGB = state.bg
494			textRGB = opts.TerminalBackground
495		case terminal.RunReverseVideo:
496			// the foreground is transparent and no terminal background is
497			// known: same cutout as above, but the glyph color is the real
498			// terminal's default background, which this package can't observe —
499			// opts.CanvasBackground stands in for it (see Options' doc comment).
500			rectRGB = state.bg
501			textRGB = opts.CanvasBackground
502		default:
503			textRGB = state.fg
504			rectRGB = state.bg
505		}
506	
507		// SGR 7 (reverse video) is a real terminal's on/off flag, not a counter:
508		// sending it again while already in one of the writer's own
509		// transparent-driven reverse renderings above changes nothing, so the
510		// explicit <r> attribute only swaps anything in the RunNormal case.
511		if run.Attributes[attrReverse] > 0 && run.Mode == terminal.RunNormal {
512			textRGB, rectRGB = rectRGB, textRGB
513		}
514	
515		hasRect = rectRGB != nil
516	
517		return textRGB, hasRect, rectRGB
518	}
519	
520	// formatFloat renders v rounded to at most 2 decimal places, using the
521	// shortest representation that round-trips at that precision — an integer
522	// value still prints as "10", not "10.00" — since Encode's own arithmetic
523	// (cell/row counts times a float metric) routinely produces values like
524	// 140.79999999999998 that carry no visual meaning past the hundredths place.
525	func formatFloat(v float64) string {
526		return strconv.FormatFloat(math.Round(v*100)/100, 'f', -1, 64)
527	}
528	
529	func hexString(rgb color.RGB) string {
530		const hexDigits = "0123456789abcdef"
531	
532		buf := [7]byte{'#'}
533	
534		for i, c := range [3]uint8{rgb.R, rgb.G, rgb.B} {
535			buf[1+i*2] = hexDigits[c>>4]
536			buf[2+i*2] = hexDigits[c&0x0f]
537		}
538	
539		return string(buf[:])
540	}
541	
542	func escapeXML(s string) string {
543		return xmlReplacer.Replace(s)
544	}
545	
546	var xmlReplacer = strings.NewReplacer("&", "&", "<", "<", ">", ">")
547	
548	// escapeAttr escapes a value destined for a double-quoted XML attribute.
549	// This is stricter than escapeXML: an attribute value like Options.FontFamily
550	// ordinarily contains literal double quotes (e.g. `"CaskaydiaCove Nerd
551	// Font", ui-monospace`), which was harmless as plain text content inside the
552	// old <style> block but would prematurely close a font-family="..." attribute
553	// if left unescaped.
554	func escapeAttr(s string) string {
555		return attrReplacer.Replace(s)
556	}
557	
558	var attrReplacer = strings.NewReplacer("&", "&", "<", "<", ">", ">", `"`, """)

18	// is scaled here by FontSize/48 to keep the same proportions at this
19	// package's actual FontSize (16px by default) instead of reproducing the
20	// PNG renderer's pixel values verbatim.
21	type windowGeometry struct {
22		margin       float64
23		padding      float64
24		titleOffset  float64
25		corner       float64
26		trafficR     float64
27		trafficGap   float64
28		trafficNudge float64

34	func newWindowGeometry(opts *Options) windowGeometry {
35		scale := opts.FontSize / 48.0

37		return windowGeometry{
38			margin:       96 * scale,
39			padding:      48 * scale,
40			titleOffset:  80 * scale,
41			corner:       12 * scale,
42			trafficR:     18 * scale,
43			trafficGap:   50 * scale,
44			trafficNudge: 4 * scale,
45			strokeWidth:  2 * scale,

52	// once from a row count and geometry: the window itself (the rounded rect
53	// with the traffic lights and content inside it), the canvas as a whole
54	// (the window plus the margin the drop shadow needs room to fall into), and
55	// the content grid's own top-left corner inside the window.
56	type canvasSize struct {
57		width, height             float64 // the full <svg> canvas, margin included
58		windowX, windowY          float64
59		windowWidth, windowHeight float64

63	func newCanvasSize(geo *windowGeometry, columns int, cellWidth float64, rows int, lineHeight float64) canvasSize {

21	// its own line (image.go's cleanContent, ~:374-401: `ir.AnsiString +=

24	// own capture.
25	//
26	// Both additions use the ansiColorCodes name "default" as their foreground
27	// source rather than leaving it empty: an empty source means "keep
28	// whatever color was already active" (see resolveChannel's doc comment),
29	// which for the cursor would mean inheriting the last segment's own
30	// foreground — image.go's cursor and watermark render in the fixed default
31	// foreground color regardless of what precedes them, because cleanContent
32	// appends them after the prompt's own trailing SGR reset, and "default" is
33	// this package's equivalent of that reset state.
34	func decorate(rows [][]terminal.Run) [][]terminal.Run {
35		if len(rows) == 0 {
36			rows = [][]terminal.Run{{}}
37		}
38	
39		rows = append([][]terminal.Run{}, rows...)
40		last := len(rows) - 1
41	
42		cursorRow := make([]terminal.Run, len(rows[last]), len(rows[last])+1)
43		copy(cursorRow, rows[last])
44		cursorRow = append(cursorRow, terminal.Run{
45			Text:             cursorText,
46			Cells:            len(cursorText),
47			ForegroundSource: color.Ansi("default"),
48			// Explicit, not empty: an empty BackgroundSource means "keep
49			// whatever was already active" (see resolveChannel's doc comment),
50			// which here would paint the cursor with whatever segment's
51			// background happened to end the row it's glued onto. The cursor
52			// itself carries no background of its own, exactly like image.go's
53			// reference renders show it.
54			BackgroundSource: color.Transparent,
55		})

57	
58		rows = append(rows, nil, nil, []terminal.Run{{
59			Text:             watermarkText,
60			Cells:            len(watermarkText),
61			ForegroundSource: color.Ansi("default"),

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the architecture now—the engine captures terminal runs, which then flow through a fitting step to handle column wrapping, followed by decoration for the cursor and watermark, and finally get rendered as SVG.

The key insight is that everything up to the final markup emission is format-agnostic, so I could extract that into a shared layout package and then swap out just the backend—either an SVG emitter or a PNG rasterizer. The user wants PNG instead of SVG, but I'm realizing the website gallery switched to inline SVG, which complicates things. I need to figure out whether the gallery still depends on SVG or if PNG behind an API endpoint would work for their studio setup.

For the PNG backend, the main challenges are handling real font faces—the old renderer downloaded Nerd Font at runtime, which won't work for an API endpoint—and computing glyph metrics properly. I'd need to embed the font files directly in the binary or find another solution, and then handle per-glyph rasterization instead of relying on the browser.

The tricky part is that while drawing a whole run at once would be simpler, monospace grids require each glyph to land on its cell boundary. Since Hack Nerd Font glyphs all advance exactly one cell, a single `DrawString` call should work—but fallback glyphs (when a codepoint is missing) might have different advances, so drawing per-cell using grid coordinates is safer. And then there's the complication of wide characters like CJK that take up 2 cells.

I need to check if the codebase already has `runewidth` available to handle per-rune cell widths. Beyond that, I'm thinking through how to handle text attributes in PNG: bold and italic need separate font faces (the new design supports loading a BoldItalic face to avoid the old bug where they couldn't coexist), underline and strikethrough are drawn as lines, dim is alpha blending, and blink can't animate so I'll just render it as visible. Window chrome effects like drop shadows need to be drawn as a stack in PNG rather than using SVG filters.

For the implementation, I can either use an existing blur library or write a simple box blur myself to avoid the dependency. The rounded rectangles, strokes, and traffic lights are all primitives from the graphics library. The dependencies are all pure Go with no CGO, which keeps the cross-compile story clean, though embedding fonts will add to the binary size. I'm also considering how to handle anti-aliasing and DPI scaling, where the old renderer used a factor of 2.0.

Now I'm working through the text placement logic — both SVG and the old PNG renderer compute baseline positioning similarly, with the baseline offset by a fraction of the line height, so I need to ensure they map correctly across the different coordinate systems.

For gradients, each cell's foreground and background colors are stored in the Run, and since the encoder flushes a new Run whenever the style changes, gradients naturally produce one run per cell, which works fine for both backends.

Before diving deeper, I should verify that the color handling and fitting logic aren't backend-specific, check how the CLI wires everything together, and confirm the website still consumes SVG output properly.

content.text:
Read the current pipeline and the retired renderer side by side. Here's the shape.

## What already exists, and what's actually SVG-specific

Current chain:

```
Engine.Primary() → terminal.Runs()  (CaptureRuns)
   → prompt.CapturedRuns   [][]terminal.Run
   → svg.fitRows      fit.go        column fitting, gap collapse, wrapping
   → svg.decorate     decorate.go   cursor + blank rows + watermark
   → newWindowGeometry/newCanvasSize  window.go   chrome coordinates
   → paintRun + resolveChannel        colors.go   Ansi/gradient/accent → RGB
   → string building                  svg.go      ← only this is SVG
```

Everything above the last line is format-neutral. It already knows cell grid, row count, canvas size, window box, traffic-light positions, per-run resolved RGB, and attribute flags. A PNG backend consumes the same thing and calls draw primitives instead of `b.WriteString`.

So this is not a rewrite. It's extracting one seam and adding a second backend behind it.

## Proposed shape

Rename `src/svg` → `src/image`, split the emitter out:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `options.go` | `Options` + `withDefaults` — shared |
| `fit.go`, `decorate.go`, `colors.go` | unchanged, shared |
| `layout.go` | **new** — `rows → Layout{Canvas, Chrome, Rows[]{Top, Baseline, Cells[]{X, Width, Text, FG, BG, Attributes}}}` |
| `svg.go` | `Layout` → markup |
| `png.go` | **new** — `Layout` → `*image.NRGBA` |
| `font.go` | **new** — face loading + metrics, PNG only |

`layout.go` is pulled straight out of today's `encodeRow` + `window.go`. Both backends then draw the *same* numbers, so an SVG-vs-PNG pixel diff becomes a real regression test over one geometry — which is exactly the instrument that was missing when the top-offset drift went undetected.

## What the PNG backend must do that the browser did for free

| Concern | SVG today | PNG |
|---|---|---|
| glyph shapes | browser font stack | load TTF, rasterize |
| grid alignment | `textLength`+`lengthAdjust` forces the run onto grid | draw per cell at `Layout` x — no measuring |
| bold / italic | `font-weight`/`font-style` | separate faces; needs a BoldItalic face for both at once |
| dim | `opacity="0.6"` | blend toward background |
| underline / overline / strike | `text-decoration` | draw lines |
| blink | CSS keyframes | not representable — render visible |
| drop shadow | `feDropShadow` | stackblur (or ~40 lines of own box blur) |
| rounded rect, circles | `<rect rx>`, `<circle>` | `gg` primitives — direct port of old `SavePNG` |
| resolution | vector | needs an explicit raster scale |
| missing glyph | browser fallback chain | tofu, no fallback |

Deps back into `go.mod`: `fogleman/gg`, `golang.org/x/image`, `golang/freetype` (indirect), `esimov/stackblur-go`. All pure Go, no CGO — the `CGO_ENABLED=0` static cross-compile posture holds.

## Old renderer bugs that die on their own

The rebuild inherits none of these, because the Run stream carries resolved state:

- no 256-colour (`38;5;N`) support at all — `colors.go` has `palette256`
- one `style` string, so bold+italic could never coexist — now `Attributes [8]uint8`
- hyperlink URLs leaked into visible text — `Cells == 0` runs are skipped
- hand-maintained `doubleWidthRunes` table — measured wrong, `Run.Cells` is authoritative
- `fontHeight() = Metrics().Height >> 6` truncated 0.9px per row — real metrics now

Also: baseline placement stops being the `0.75 * LineHeight` fudge. With a loaded face we get `ascent`/`descent` and can center exactly, then feed that same number back to SVG. That closes the top-offset defect instead of parking it.

## Three forks I need you to pick

**1. Does SVG survive?** The website gallery inlines SVG today (`website/export_themes.mjs`, 8 MB → 421 KB). Dropping SVG regresses that back to megabytes of PNG. My read: keep both backends over the shared layout — SVG for the gallery, PNG for the CLI and studio.

**2. Where do the fonts come from?** Binary is 23.3 MB today. Hack Nerd Font is 2.34 MB per face, 4 faces = 9.4 MB raw / ~5 MB zipped.

**3. Scale factor.** Old renderer hardcoded `factor = 2.0` at a 48px reference em. For an API endpoint that should be a request parameter (`?scale=2`), not a constant.

questions.question: Does the SVG backend survive alongside PNG?

options.label: Keep both (Recommended)
options.description: One shared layout, two emitters. SVG stays for the website gallery (421 KB inline vs ~8 MB of PNG); PNG for the CLI export and the studio API. Cost: the layout seam has to be genuinely format-neutral, which it nearly is already.

options.label: PNG only
options.description: Delete the SVG emitter, rename the package, single backend. Simplest code. Cost: the theme gallery goes back to shipping raster images and the page weight regresses ~20x.

questions.question: How does the PNG renderer get its font faces?

options.label: Download + cache, fail loudly

Fixes the real bug by returning a hard error instead of exiting 0. The API container pre-warms the cache at build time so it never hits the network at request time.

options.label: go:embed a zipped bundle
options.description: Ship all four faces (Regular/Bold/Italic/BoldItalic) compressed inside the binary, ~5 MB. Binary goes 23.3 -> ~29 MB (+25%). Fully hermetic, works offline and air-gapped, zero cold-start cost.

options.label: go:embed uncompressed

options.label: Build tag: PNG out of the release binary
options.description: Release CLI carries neither gg nor fonts and exports SVG only. A separate server build embeds fonts and serves PNG. Binary unchanged. Cost: `config export image` no longer produces a PNG for end users, which contradicts reinstating the original functionality.

questions.question: How is raster resolution controlled?

options.label: Options.Scale, default 2 (Recommended)
options.description: Layout stays in abstract px; the PNG backend multiplies by Scale when rasterizing. CLI gets --scale, the API gets ?scale=. Default 2 reproduces the old renderer's factor = 2.0 output size exactly.

options.label: Fixed factor 2.0
options.description: Hardcode it like the old renderer. Less surface area now, but the studio can't offer retina/thumbnail variants without a code change.

        powerline_symbol: 
        options:

          style: round
        style: powerline
        template: " 󰔟{{ .FormattedMs }} "

import glob
import os
import re

    markup = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    rects = [(float(m[0]), float(m[1]), float(m[2]), m[4]) for m in RECT.findall(markup)]

"""Flag exported SVGs whose prompt text is invisible: alphanumeric runs that
carry no fill, or paint the same colour as the rect underneath them."""
import glob
import os
import re
import sys

RECT = re.compile(r'<rect x="([\d.]+)" y="([\d.]+)" width="([\d.]+)" height="([\d.]+)" fill="(#[0-9a-f]{6})"/>')
TEXT = re.compile(r'<text ([^>]*)>(.*?)</text>')
ATTR = re.compile(r'(\w[\w:-]*)="([^"]*)"')
WORD = re.compile(r"[0-9A-Za-z]")


def scan(path):
    markup = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    rects = [(float(m[0]), float(m[1]), float(m[2]), m[4]) for m in RECT.findall(markup)]

    words = 0
    invisible = []

    for attrs, body in TEXT.findall(markup):
        if not WORD.search(body):
            continue

        words += 1
        a = dict(ATTR.findall(attrs))
        x, y = float(a["x"]), float(a["y"])
        fill = a.get("fill", "")

        under = None
        for rx, ry, rw, rfill in rects:
            if rx - 0.01 <= x < rx + rw and ry <= y <= ry + 40:
                under = rfill

        if fill == "" or (under is not None and fill == under):
            invisible.append((body[:24], fill, under))

    return words, invisible


hits = 0
for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "*.svg"))):
    words, invisible = scan(path)

    if not invisible:
        continue

    hits += 1
    tag = "ALL INVISIBLE" if len(invisible) == words else ""
    print(f"{os.path.basename(path):34} words={words:3} invisible={len(invisible):3} {tag}")

    if len(sys.argv) > 2:
        for body, fill, under in invisible[:6]:

| | main | next | delta |

Net source is up because the deletions were mostly third-party (`gg`, `stackblur`, `x/image`, `freetype` — ~27.7k lines of dependency, which is what the binary saving comes from), while the additions are ours. By package:

```
svg        +1267   (new — 679 code, 588 comment/blank, 46% docs)
terminal    +485   (run capture + tokenizer collapse)
color       +272

cli          -419   (PNG renderer gone)

```

So: removed more *dependency* code than added, added more *own* code than removed.

---

Now, the four bugs. All four reproduced against the retired renderer's own output.

## 1. Spaces collapse — confirmed, SVG bug

Probed Chromium directly (`tools/svg-png-compare/probe-whitespace.mjs`), string `"  ab  "` = 6 cells:

```
root white-space="pre"          2.00 cells  COLLAPSED
root xml:space="preserve"       2.00 cells  COLLAPSED
root style="white-space:pre"    2.00 cells  COLLAPSED
text xml:space="preserve"       6.00 cells  PRESERVED
no declaration (baseline)       2.00 cells  COLLAPSED
```

`white-space` on the root `<svg>` ([svg.go:265](src/svg/svg.go:265)) does nothing. Only `xml:space="preserve"` **on each `<text>`** works — root doesn't inherit it.

Second-order damage: `textLength` + `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"` then stretches the surviving glyphs across the full run width. That's why glowsticks' `✓` renders as a wide swoosh — template ` ✓ ` is 3 cells, collapses to 1 glyph, stretched 3×.

## 2. Powerline/diamond inversion — **not** an SVG bug

The ANSI writer itself emits it that way:

```
ESC[48;2;51;57;91m ESC[38;2;255;151;46m           bg = session, fg = path
```

and the retired PNG renderer draws the same picture — I rendered it to check. Root cause is [engine.go:702](src/prompt/engine.go:702):

```go
if e.activeSegment.InvertPowerline || (e.previousActiveSegment != nil && e.previousActiveSegment.InvertPowerline) {
```

`invert_powerline` on the session segment is needed for its own leading `` cap, but the `previousActiveSegment` clause leaks the inversion onto the *next* separator too. Fixing it changes real terminal output for every theme using `invert_powerline` — glowsticks, iterm2, others. Your call, and it's an engine commit, not an SVG one.

## 3. Invisible text — confirmed, SVG bug

`cert` renders 6 of 7 text runs in exactly the background colour. Cause: [colors.go:128](src/svg/colors.go:128) `hexToRGB` requires exactly 6 digits, so `#fff` fails to resolve; `paintRun` then keeps the previously active colour, which after a leading diamond *is* the segment background. The terminal emits `38;2;255;255;255` correctly.

Six bundled themes use 3-digit hex: `cert`, `iterm2`, `montys`, `poshmon`, `uew`, `unicorn`. Fix is to match `gookit/color.HEX`'s accepted forms.

(`powerlevel10k_modern`'s invisible `at` is *not* this — the ANSI genuinely emits white-on-white there. Faithful.)

## 4. Cursor after the rprompt — confirmed, SVG bug

```
<text x="1194.3" ... fill="#ffffff">_</text>     ← after the battery glyph, far right
```

import struct

    n = struct.unpack(">H", data[4:6])[0]
    out = {}
    for i in range(n):
        off = 12 + i * 16
        tag = data[off:off + 4].decode("latin-1")
        to, tl = struct.unpack(">II", data[off + 8:off + 16])
        out[tag] = (to, tl)
    return out


def cmap_lookup(data, t):
    base = t["cmap"][0]
    count = struct.unpack(">H", data[base + 2:base + 4])[0]
    best = None
    for i in range(count):
        pid, eid, off = struct.unpack(">HHI", data[base + 4 + i * 8:base + 12 + i * 8])
        fmt = struct.unpack(">H", data[base + off:base + off + 2])[0]
        if fmt in (4, 12):
            best = (fmt, base + off) if (best is None or fmt == 12) else best
    fmt, sub = best

    mapping = {}
    if fmt == 4:
        segx2 = struct.unpack(">H", data[sub + 6:sub + 8])[0]
        seg = segx2 // 2
        ends = struct.unpack(">%dH" % seg, data[sub + 14:sub + 14 + segx2])

        deltas = struct.unpack(">%dh" % seg, data[starts_off + segx2:starts_off + 2 * segx2])
        range_off_base = starts_off + 2 * segx2

"""Report the horizontal advance, in cells, of specific codepoints in one or
more TTFs. A cell is the advance of ASCII 'M'."""
import struct
import sys


def tables(data):
    n = struct.unpack(">H", data[4:6])[0]
    out = {}
    for i in range(n):
        off = 12 + i * 16
        tag = data[off:off + 4].decode("latin-1")
        to, tl = struct.unpack(">II", data[off + 8:off + 16])
        out[tag] = (to, tl)
    return out


def cmap_lookup(data, t):
    base = t["cmap"][0]
    count = struct.unpack(">H", data[base + 2:base + 4])[0]
    best = None
    for i in range(count):
        pid, eid, off = struct.unpack(">HHI", data[base + 4 + i * 8:base + 12 + i * 8])
        fmt = struct.unpack(">H", data[base + off:base + off + 2])[0]
        if fmt in (4, 12):
            best = (fmt, base + off) if (best is None or fmt == 12) else best
    fmt, sub = best

    mapping = {}
    if fmt == 4:
        segx2 = struct.unpack(">H", data[sub + 6:sub + 8])[0]
        seg = segx2 // 2
        ends = struct.unpack(">%dH" % seg, data[sub + 14:sub + 14 + segx2])
        starts_off = sub + 16 + segx2
        starts = struct.unpack(">%dH" % seg, data[starts_off:starts_off + segx2])
        deltas = struct.unpack(">%dh" % seg, data[starts_off + segx2:starts_off + 2 * segx2])
        range_off_base = starts_off + 2 * segx2
        ranges = struct.unpack(">%dH" % seg, data[range_off_base:range_off_base + segx2])
        for i in range(seg):
            for c in range(starts[i], min(ends[i], 0xFFFF) + 1):
                if ranges[i] == 0:
                    g = (c + deltas[i]) & 0xFFFF
                else:
                    addr = range_off_base + i * 2 + ranges[i] + (c - starts[i]) * 2
                    g = struct.unpack(">H", data[addr:addr + 2])[0]
                    if g:
                        g = (g + deltas[i]) & 0xFFFF
                if g:
                    mapping[c] = g
    else:
        ngroups = struct.unpack(">I", data[sub + 12:sub + 16])[0]
        for i in range(ngroups):
            s, e, gid = struct.unpack(">III", data[sub + 16 + i * 12:sub + 28 + i * 12])
            for c in range(s, e + 1):
                mapping[c] = gid + (c - s)
    return mapping


def advances(data, t):
    upem = struct.unpack(">H", data[t["head"][0] + 18:t["head"][0] + 20])[0]
    num_h = struct.unpack(">H", data[t["hhea"][0] + 34:t["hhea"][0] + 36])[0]
    hmtx = t["hmtx"][0]

    def adv(gid):
        i = min(gid, num_h - 1)
        return struct.unpack(">H", data[hmtx + i * 4:hmtx + i * 4 + 2])[0]

    return upem, adv


CODEPOINTS = [
    ("M", 0x4D), ("space", 0x20),
    ("E0B0 powerline", 0xE0B0), ("E0B6 halfcircle", 0xE0B6),
    ("F07B folder", 0xF07B), ("F00C check", 0xF00C),
    ("F120 terminal", 0xF120), ("F051F hourglass", 0xF051F),
]

for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    t = tables(data)
    cmap = cmap_lookup(data, t)
    upem, adv = advances(data, t)
    cell = adv(cmap[0x4D])

    print(path.replace("\\", "/").split("/")[-1])
    for name, cp in CODEPOINTS:
        gid = cmap.get(cp)
        if gid is None:
            print(f"  {name:18} U+{cp:04X}  MISSING")
            continue
        print(f"  {name:18} U+{cp:04X}  advance {adv(gid):5} units = {adv(gid)/cell:.3f} cells ({adv(gid)/upem:.4f} em)")
    print()

<type>(<scope>): <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

### Types

| Type       | When to use                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `feat`     | A new feature                                          |
| `fix`      | A bug fix                                              |
| `docs`     | Documentation changes, no code                         |
| `style`    | Formatting, missing semicolons, etc. (no logic change) |
| `refactor` | Code change that is neither a fix nor a feature        |
| `perf`     | Performance improvement                                |
| `test`     | Adding or correcting tests                             |
| `ci`       | CI configuration changes                               |
| `chore`    | Maintenance tasks (updating deps, tooling, etc.)       |
| `revert`   | Reverts a previous commit                              |

Append `!` after the type/scope to signal a **breaking change**: `feat!:` or `feat(api)!:`
When a change breaks existing behavior, **both markers are mandatory**: the `!` suffix on the type
**and** the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. They always appear together — never one without the other.

### Scope

Optional. Use the name of the area affected, e.g., `segment`, `cache`, `config`, `ui`.
Omit when the change is truly cross-cutting.

### Description

- Required. One short imperative sentence, no period at the end. The full header line (type +
  scope + description) must be **72 characters or fewer**. Aim for **50 characters or fewer for
  the description itself** — this almost always keeps the full header within budget regardless
  of type and scope length.
- Use the imperative mood: "add", not "added" or "adds". Never past tense or present-third-person:
  ✗ `added`, `fixed`, `bumped`, `implemented` → ✓ `add`, `fix`, `bump`, `implement`.
- **Never mirror the input's phrasing.** If the request uses past-tense words (`updated`, `added`,
  `bumped`, `was removed`, `got regenerated`), convert them to imperative before writing the
  description: `update`, `add`, `bump`, `remove`, `regenerate`.

### Body

Optional. Add context about _why_ the change was made, not _what_. The diff shows that.
Wrap at 72 characters.

### Footer

Use for:

- `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>` (required when `!` is used; explains the break).
- Issue references: `Closes #123`, `Fixes #456`.
- Co-authors: `Co-Authored-By: Name <email>`.

## Workflow

1. Run `git status` to review changed files.
2. Run `git diff` and `git diff --cached` to inspect staged and unstaged changes.
3. Identify the **type** from the table above. Ask yourself: does this change **remove, rename, or
   alter existing behavior** that callers depend on? If yes → it is a breaking change: use `!`
   after the type/scope **and** add a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Both markers are always required
   together.
4. Identify the **scope** from the files/area changed.
5. Write a short **description** in the imperative mood.
6. Add a **body** if the _why_ needs explanation.
7. Add a **footer** for breaking changes or issue references.
8. Stage the relevant files explicitly (avoid `git add -A`).
9. Commit with a message that preserves multi-line formatting when body/footer are present.

## Examples

```text
feat(segment): add Ramadan segment with Aladhan API
fix(cache): always store mod time
docs(readme): update installation instructions
refactor(config): simplify option parsing logic
chore(deps): bump github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v4
feat(segment)!: rename template property StartTime to Start

BREAKING CHANGE: template strings using .StartTime must be updated to .Start
```

## Validation Checklist

- [ ] Type is one of the allowed values in .commitlintrc.yml
- [ ] The commit message respects the rules defined in .commitlintrc.yml
- [ ] Scope (if present) reflects the actual area changed
- [ ] Description is imperative mood, no trailing period
- [ ] Full header line (type + scope + description) is 72 characters or fewer
- [ ] Both `!` after type/scope **and** `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer are present whenever the change breaks existing behavior
- [ ] No sensitive files staged (.env, credentials, etc.)

"""Stage selected hunks of a file's working-tree diff.

    python pick_hunks.py <file> <1-based hunk indices...>

Writes the filtered patch to stdout; pipe it into `git apply --cached`.
"""
import subprocess
import sys

path = sys.argv[1]
wanted = {int(a) for a in sys.argv[2:]}

diff = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "diff", "-U3", "--", path],
    capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
).stdout.split("\n")

header = []
hunks = []
current = None

for line in diff:
    if line.startswith("@@"):
        current = [line]
        hunks.append(current)
        continue

    if current is None:
        header.append(line)
    else:
        current.append(line)

out = header[:]
for i, hunk in enumerate(hunks, start=1):
    if i in wanted:
        out.extend(hunk)

sys.stdout.write("\n".join(out).rstrip("\n") + "\n")

cell grid; the plain families stay in the stack as a fallback.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(svg): put the cursor where the shell leaves it

decorate appended the cursor indicator to the last row's tail. The
engine writes a right-aligned block into that same row, so on any theme
with an rprompt the cursor landed after it, at the far right edge of the
window, rather than after the prompt the user types at.

The anchor already exists in the engine: writePrimaryRightPrompt wraps
the rprompt in SaveCursorPosition/RestoreCursorPosition precisely so a
real terminal leaves the cursor back at the primary prompt's end.
markCursorAnchor records that same point, and CursorAnchor hands it to
the exporter through Options.Cursor.

Nothing in the Run stream itself distinguishes a left-aligned block's
runs from a right-aligned one's, so the anchor has to come from the
engine rather than be rediscovered by scanning the row.

Encode now decorates before fitting, since the anchor indexes the
captured rows and fitRow is free to collapse gaps and wrap a row into
several. insertCursor takes the cursor's cell out of the alignment gap
that follows it where there is one, so the row keeps its exact width and
the rprompt stays flush right — the same thing a terminal does, where
the cursor occupies a cell that is already there.
EOF
git log --oneline -1

name: omp-font-metrics-are-measurable
description: Read TTF tables directly instead of inferring font geometry from rendered output — three wrong oh-my-posh SVG fixes came from inference
